title: Blue Jays’ Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Announces Personal News in 1st Year Without Bo Bichette
description: Toronto Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. announces personal news amid a season without Bo Bichette, shouldering larger responsibilities. The post Blue Jays’ Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Announces Personal News in 1st Year Without Bo Bichette appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is playing his first season without Bo Bichette.

They both debuted with Toronto in 2019. Guerrero arrived on April 26 and Bichette followed on July 29. They were teammates through the 2025 season.

Bichette was very successful with the Blue Jays. He batted .294 with 111 home runs and 437 RBIs in seven seasons with Toronto.

But the 28-year-old became a free agent after the 2025 season and signed with the New York Mets in January. Guerrero, 27, stayed.

He signed a 14-year, $500 million contract in April 2025. Bichette's departure gave him bigger responsibilities. Shouldering them, he has not had a good season this year.

Through Saturday's game, Guerrero is batting .262 with nine home runs and 56 RBIs.

He recently announced that he has also struggled mentally at times and manager John Schneider has pulled him out of it.

Guerrero had four hits, including a home run and six RBIs against the Cleveland Guardians in early September. He still did not feel right, so he reached out to Schneider.

Guerrero said he was frustrated because nothing he tried was improving his results. The two talked for about 45 minutes.

"Sometimes we lie a lot, we say we're good and we're not good," Guerrero explained to Sportsnet's Shi Davidi. "If you need help, just ask for help. I learned a lot about that this year and the other day I told him I just need help and we talked for like 45 minutes in his office. After that, I felt relief, because I needed to talk with somebody that can hear me, besides my family. I talk with my family every day, but sometimes you need other people to hear you and feel you. Everything's been great after that. My mind has been clear."

Schneider told Sportsnet he sees Guerrero's difficult season as a chance for something positive to emerge.

"In watching Vlad go through it, I try to use it as an opportunity to make sure that good can come out of it and to his credit, he hasn't budged," Schneider said. "The fact that he has posted, the fact that he's continued to interact with his teammates and do the things that you notice is a step in the right direction for him as a leader of this team."

Guerrero works hard to fulfill his responsibilities. His efforts have not gone unnoticed.

"He works his (expletive) off," George Springer said. "He's here late. He's here early. He'll dissect everything. I'm sure he would like to have his normal season, but he shows up every day and he never gets down. He always looks like he's the same."

Guerrero is sure to fill his role better with time

Toronto fell to 76-79. The Blue Jays are three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the American League's final wild-card berth.

They have seven games left. It plays at Texas on Sunday and at Baltimore from Monday through Wednesday. It then hosts Cincinnati for three games to close the season.

The Blue Jays do not hold the head-to-head tiebreaker against the White Sox or the Rangers.

Right-hander Trey Yesavage will start Monday at Baltimore after undergoing left knee surgery in August. Schneider said Yesavage should throw about three innings. Yesavage, 23, is 5-5 with a 3.65 ERA this season.

Right-hander Shane Bieber, sidelined with right teres major inflammation, planned to throw off a mound Saturday. A regular-season return is unlikely, but he is building up in case Toronto reaches the postseason.

The Blue Jays could activate Anthony Santander on Monday if a Sunday rehab game goes well.

Right-hander Jameson Taillon said Sept. 15 that his season is over because of an elbow injury. He will see Dr. Keith Meister on Sept. 22.

title: Five standout performers from UCLA's Week 3 52-38 win over Purdue
description: The stars were plentiful for the UCLA Bruins in their 52-38 win over Purdue to move the Bruins to 3-0.
fullText:
There were plenty of standout performances in the UCLA Bruins' late-night 52-38 win over the Purdue Boilermakers to kick off their Big Ten Conference schedule with a high-scoring win.

It wasn't all pretty. The UCLA defense couldn't stop a cold, if not for three Purdue turnovers, things could have gotten real hairy in Westwood. UCLA's offense didn't need much help, leading the way to UCLA's 3-0 start. Here are five stars from Saturday's victory.

Sammy Omosigho's been one of the most important transfers of the offseason for UCLA. He's established himself as a team captain and he's performed between the sidelines too. Omosigho made 12 tackles, forced two fumbles and recorded two sacks in the win.

Without Mikey Matthews or Aidan Mizzell, UCLA needed production from other wide receivers. Semaj Morgan stepped up (more on him later) as did Leland Smith. Smith made three catches for 59 yards. It was the first three catches of the season for Smith, who played for Purdue in 2024.

Semaj Morgan made big plays when UCLA needed them in the passing game. Morgan was UCLA's most productive receiver with four catches and 72 yards. Morgan found the end zone twice, making the most of his big day.

Wayne Knight is running wild. The James Madison transfer rushed for 177 yards on 18 carries. Knight's touchdowns declined a bit in Week 3, scoring twice on Saturday after back-to-back hat tricks to begin the season.

It's hard to separate just one UCLA offensive lineman, or even just five, as UCLA has used multiple different units up front to begin the season. The offensive line allowed for the team to rush for 369 yards, including four different players rushing for at least 50 yards. On top of that, UCLA allowed just one sack in the game, a pretty solid showing from the Bruins up front.

title: Packers Former 1st-Round Pick Put on Notice
description: The Green Bay Packers offensive line was exposed against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 1. Most of the concern has been centered around the interior offensive line and the surprising decisions the Packers made at guard. However, that has excused the play of left tackle Jordan Morgan, who was not good in his first real […] The post Packers Former 1st-Round Pick Put on Notice appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers offensive line was exposed against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 1. Most of the concern has been centered around the interior offensive line and the surprising decisions the Packers made at guard. However, that has excused the play of left tackle Jordan Morgan, who was not good in his first real look as a starter.

Morgan struggled in Week 1, allowing five pressures and being graded as the 58th best tackle out of 65 qualified players. After the performance, Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report called out Morgan as the one player who has to perform better.

"Morgan was already under a fair amount of pressure when the season began, as he's being asked to replace former starter Rasheed Walker," wrote Knox. "Entering Week 2, he'll be under immense pressure to prove that he's up to the challenge of starting on the left side."

Questions already emerged around Morgan entering the year. Now, they are getting louder.

Morgan was a former first-round pick. However, he fell to the 25th pick because teams were unsure if he would be better at tackle or guard in the NFL. In his first two NFL seasons, he started in just one game at left tackle. That was a meaningless Week 18 game when the team rested their starters.

In his rookie year, he only started in one game. However, he got work at both left and right guard as a reserve. He got a little more work in his second NFL season. Morgan started in 13 games at four different positions.

He entered the year with 478 snaps at right guard, 256 snaps at left guard, 219 snaps at right guard, and just 51 snaps at left tackle. So, there were questions about how his real debut at left tackle would go, considering he was unable to win the job in past years.

After one week, the Packers' reasoning for not starting him early has become clear.

The reason the Packers' guards are getting more attention than the tackles is that the tackles still have room for growth. Morgan is a former first-round pick with talent. He has proven he can start at guard; he just needs time to adjust to the new position.

As he grows into his role, he can become a more trusted starter. Zach Bako-Bewele struggled as well, but he was coming back from an injury that ended his 2025 season. He can shake some rust off and look better.

At left guard, the team decided to start Donovan Jennings over Jager Burton, which was a surprise to many. At right guard, they decided to start Jacob Monk over Anthony Belton. Those two decisions could be questioned, and the team could have changed the outcome with those choices. That is why they are getting more heat than Morgan. Still, Morgan has to play better.

title: Chiefs star fined more than $8k ahead of 'SNF' matchup vs. Colts
description: The NFL fined Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III more than $8,000 ahead of Kansas City's Week 2 matchup against the Colts on 'Sunday Night Football.'
fullText:
Star running back Kenneth Walker III was fined $8,357 ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 2 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on 'Sunday Night Football.'

The fine was levied after Walker unwisely decided to throw a football into the stands at Arrowhead Stadium after he scored a touchdown during the Chiefs' primetime win over the Denver Broncos in Week 1.

In one of the best performances of his career, Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries against the Broncos. He also caught three passes for 18 yards and scored one receiving touchdown that helped lift Kansas City to victory.

Walker will have the opportunity to appeal the fine he incurred in Week 1, but given that his conduct was a clear violation of the NFL's player conduct policy, it is unlikely he would have a case to have the financial penalty reduced or cleared altogether.

title: Deion Sanders wasn't happy that some players were laughing after blowout loss
description: Saturday night's blowout loss to Northwestern had some Colorado players not behaving like they were in a "fucking library."
fullText:
Saturday night's blowout loss to Northwestern had some Colorado players not behaving like they were in a "fucking library." And coach Deion Sanders wasn't pleased with that.

After the 41-7 blowout absorbed by the Buffaloes, coach Deion Sanders made it clear that he wasn't happy that some players seemed to be happy after losing so badly.

"You know, you did see a couple guys that I just got on, because I don't understand how much — how you can have joy in a loss, especially when I'm upset," Sanders told reporters. "And I'm walking right behind you. I don't understand that. I can't never understand that. Because I want to win every darn thing, and I can't understand how in the world, do you find joy, or you could find a laughing matter when I'm right behind you walking in? I don't understand that. And I addressed it. And I'm gonna put my foot in it, not on it."

Based on the latest outcome, Sanders needs to put his foot in a lot of things, especially with the Big 12 schedule starting next week for 2-1 Colorado.

title: Flyers Roster Tracker: Tiering the Roster After Saturday’s Loans
description: The Philadelphia Flyers have held two practice sessions and a scrimmage so far in training camp before their first preseason […]
fullText:
The Philadelphia Flyers have held two practice sessions and a scrimmage so far in training camp before their first preseason game on Monday. So far, we've got a good look at the players who will be on the NHL roster, as well as an indication of who is fighting for a spot on the NHL roster and who is not.

The team made their first round of cuts on Saturday following the scrimmage, sending forwards Brady Berard, Alex Ciernik, Devin Kaplan, Owen McLaughlan, Ilya Pautov, and Zayde Wisdom, as well as defenseman Jackson Edward and Andrew Perrott to Lehigh Valley Phantoms training camp.

Additionally, forwards Nathan Quinn and KJ Sauer, defensemen Brek Liske, Maksim Sokolovskii, and Luke Vlooswyk, as well as goalies Martin Psohlavec and Marek Scklenicka, have been loaned back to their respective junior clubs.

The Flyers' training camp roster is now at 42 players and has to be shrunk to 23 before the season begins in 10 days.

Here is where things stand as of now.

*Note: Lists are in numerical order*

Again, this is the group of people who are all but certainly making the NHL roster. Barring anything unforeseen, this group of players entered camp with the expectation of making the NHL roster and having their spots safe.

Denver Barkey and Alex Bump were two of the only players, if any players, who needed to earn their spots. After a phenomenal showing for both players so far at camp, they've shown that they have nothing left to prove.

The only major change here is David Jiricek. He was in the roster battle tier last time. This time around, his spot looks solid.

D Travis Sanheim
D Cam York
D Jamie Drysdale
F Travis Konecny
F Sean Couturier
F Alex Bump
F Christian Dvorak
D Nick Seeler

G Dan Vladar
F Denver Barkey
F Porter Martone

Same as last time, this is the group of players, all of whom are expected to be on the NHL roster, but still have a little fight left to secure their spot.

As mentioned earlier, I moved Jiricek from this group to the locks tier. He was paired with Nick Seeler in the scrimmage. Honestly, he has not made any glaring defensive blunders thus far, and he was given power play time with the 2nd unit on Saturday. I thought maybe he had a little battle to do. It seems like the team has made up its mind.

I also dropped Simon Benoit down simply because of his pairing on Saturday. Clearly, the team envisions him as the 7D. He also only has one year left on his deal. I still expect him to make the roster, but if a young guy like Oliver Bonk or Ty Murchison makes a strong case for the big club, Benoit as the 7D could be the casualty on the roster.

However, the Flyers have shown a tendency to go 13F 8D in the past, so for that same reason, I have Carl Grundstrom still in this spot. I do expect Grundstrom to be in the NHL with the Flyers on opening night.

Nikita Grebenkin remains on the list simply because he has yet to be cleared to skate with the big club.

F Nikita Grebenkin
D Simon Benoit
F Carl Grundstrom

I did some moving around in this section as well. I beleive that the bubble players are shrinking a bit. While defensemen Helge Grans and Hunter McDonald have in no way been bad at training camp, I don't see them fighting for a chance at the NHL roster. They've been paired together, and ultimately, I see them as a Top-4 pair in Lehigh Valley.

If any defensemen were to give the Flyers a tough decision, it would be Murchison and Oliver Bonk. If I had to lean one way right now, I'd lean towards Murchison, simply because I do think it would be for a 7D role. The Flyers would be much better off having Bonk playing every night in Lehigh rather than only playing 20/30 NHL games.

Jacob Gaucher has always been a reliable "next man up" sort of player. Plus, being a center helps. He remains in this category as a just-in-case option.

Jett Luchanko is also making what should have been an easy choice hard. He's looked sharp in training camp – the best he has looked since being drafted. I still think he starts the year in Lehigh, but it won't be an easy decision.

Zach Aston-Reese got a good look in the scrimmage, but I don't think he did much with the opportunity on Saturday. He did not pop, and Danila Klimovich and Jack Studnicka outshone him. However, instead of moving them up, I moved Aston-Reese down in my rankings.

Cole Knuble got tasked with playing alongside Noah Cates and Tyson Foerster. He continued to rise to the occasion. While I don't think that if Grebenkin is healthy, Knuble has a chance. However, if Grebenkin is not good to go, Knuble is certainly earning a short look in the NHL. He's been great so far.

title: ‘Prayers Up for Him,’ ‘Talk to Somebody’ — NFL Fans Deeply Worried After Former Steelers Pro Bowler’s Raw Mental Health Confession
description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Diontae Johnson released a concerning video on social media on Saturday, talking about his mental health struggles more than a year after the Cleveland Browns cut him. Fans React to Diontae Johnson’s Emotional AdmissionFans on X were worried about Johnson after the clip of him admitting his struggles went viral.
fullText:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Diontae Johnson released a concerning video on social media on Saturday, talking about his mental health struggles more than a year after the Cleveland Browns cut him.

Fans on X were worried about Johnson after the clip of him admitting his struggles went viral.

One fan commended Johnson for speaking out about his struggles.

"Damn. Everyone knows this happens a lot to ex-NFL players, but a lot don't talk about it. You just find out eventually in the police blotter or obituaries. Good for him for speaking out and I hope it all ends well for him," the fan wrote.

Another fan advised the former Steelers wide receiver to seek professional help.

"Prayers up for you bro!!! Keep ya faith in god and talk to somebody," the fan posted.

One fan sympathized with the former Steelers star.

"He was a solid WR when he was in Pittsburgh. Sure he would have a bonehead play from time to time, but solid nonetheless. But football aside, I hope he can get to a better place mentally. Struggling mentally really sucks… prayers up for him," the fan remarked.

Another fan attributed Johnson's struggles to CTE (Chronic traumatic encephalopathy).

"CTE is so real. This is crazy," the fan opined.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

One fan suggested that Johnson could still make an NFL comeback.

"If he's still a precision route guy, we could use him! He was open in an instant most times," the fan commented.

Another fan wished the former Steelers wideout good luck after his confession.

"Best of luck on getting past this, Diontae!" the fan wrote.

After a stellar college football career with the Toledo Rockets, the Steelers selected Johnson No. 66 overall in the 2019 NFL Draft. He earned a Second-Team All-Pro selection as a punt returner in his rookie season, and then earned his first Pro Bowl nod in 2021 and signed a lucrative two-year, $36.71 million contract extension in 2022.

He was traded to the Carolina Panthers in 2024 after five seasons in Pittsburgh. Later that year, Johnson was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. The former Toledo wide receiver was suspended for one game for refusing to play in the Ravens' Week 13 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Ravens waived him after the incident.

The Houston Texans claimed Johnson off waivers before releasing him and paving the way for his return to Baltimore for his second stint. He signed a one-year contract with the Cleveland Browns in 2025 but was released during final roster cuts. In five seasons in Pittsburgh, Johnson caught 391 passes for 4,363 yards and 25 touchdowns.

title: Five takeaways from FSU's loss to Alabama
description: The Florida State Seminoles dropped to 1-2 on the season after falling to Alabama on Saturday. Here are five takeaways.
fullText:
The Florida State Seminoles were looking for a huge win in Tuscaloosa against the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday. It looked very promising when they took a 21-6 lead with just under 10 mins left in the second quarter.

After that, the floodgates opened. Alabama had streaks of 20 consecutive points and 17 consecutive points, and they eventually pulled out a 50-36 victory over FSU. This also kept an embarrassing streak of over 1,000 days since Florida State has won a game on the road.

Once they play the Central Arkansas Bears next week, the Seminoles will begin a tough ACC schedule, which is concerning considering how bad they've been in conference play since 2023. With that said, here are five takeaways from their loss to the Crimson Tide.

For the second straight game, Florida State's defense allowed nearly 600 yards of offense. They also allowed points on nine consecutive drives at one point as Keelon Russell, just like Kevin Jennings of the SMU Mustangs in Week 1, destroyed FSU with his arms and legs with nearly 400 all-purpose yards and four total touchdowns. A truly pathetic performance.

When looking at the remainder of FSU's road schedule, it's hard to see where they can put together any wins. They still have to play the Louisville Cardinals, Miami Hurricanes, Boston College Eagles, and the Pittsburgh Panthers away from Doak Campbell Stadium, and every one of those teams is better than Florida State, and some of them are a lot better. It's going to be extremely challenging.

On top of their road schedule for the rest of the season, Florida State still has to play the Virginia Cavaliers, Clemson Tigers, and the Florida Gators at home, which are all looking like losses right now. In fact, their game against Central Arkansas is really the only one that feels like they'll win. It's going to continue to be a rough year.

No disrespect to Ashton Daniels, but he's simply not the answer at quarterback for FSU. He was given the job too quickly, and he's done nothing to show that he can lead the Seminoles' offense consistently. In the coming weeks, Malachi Marshall or Kevin Sperry need to get a shot.

He's in his seventh season as head coach at Florida State, and Norvell is looking at his fifth losing campaign. Simply put, the Seminoles are not going to get where they need to be under his leadership. With the surrounding circumstances as it pertains to the program, that will take a while, but it's time for FSU to move on.

title: The Calm Before The Storm
description: Get ready for conference play!
fullText:
The final tuneup before things get real is out of the way. Penn State had a performance resembling the one of two weeks ago, with the biggest difference ever being the running backs actually performing well on the ground. There isn't much to learn from this game, so let's get right into it.

Penn State came out fast, controlling the first quarter. Ryan Barker opened the scoring with a 48-yard field goal, then James Peoples ran for a 16-yard touchdown. Rocco Becht then found Andrew Rappleyea for a short touchdown pass. Just like the game against Marshall, the Nittany Lions raced to a 17-0 start. Buffalo answered with an Oliver Hautanen field goal, though, and Penn State led 17-3 after one quarter.

The second quarter brought more Penn State scoring. Barker added a 25-yard field goal, then Koby Howard ran for a 20-yard touchdown. Becht later connected with Howard again, this time for a 70-yard touchdown pass. Buffalo closed the half with another Hautanen field goal. Penn State led 34-6 at halftime.

Penn State dominated the third quarter and Buffalo did not score. Carson Hansen ran for a 12-yard touchdown, and Peoples added his second rushing touchdown of the day, this one from 11 yards out. Penn State led 48-6 heading into the fourth.

The fourth quarter opened with Cam Wallace breaking off a 59-yard touchdown run, extending Penn State's lead to 55-6. Buffalo got on the board late when James McNeil Jr. scored on a short touchdown run, making the final score 55-13.

This game fulfilled the purpose it was scheduled for. It was a tuneup, against a team that had no chance, and played out exactly like this. Now, the Lions need to take all the lessons from the past three contests and get ready for conference play. Wisconsin suddenly looks better than we all thought coming in.

573 – Total yards for Penn State, they came real close to the record set against Kent State just two years ago!

100 – Rushing yards for Quinton Martin, Jr. Finally, a back goes for a hundred!

115 – Receiving yards for Koby Howard. The road to 1,000 continues

title: Other NASCAR drivers react to Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney fight
description: Here's a breakdown of the most notable reactions from current and former NASCAR drivers after a wild post-race brawl at Bristol Motor Speedway
fullText:
Drivers suddenly became spectators after the NASCAR Cup race at Bristol, watching on (most with glee) as Ryan Blaney confronted Carson Hocevar, with Hocevar punching Blaney twice in the face in the first real fight we've seen after a Cup race in over two years.

The last time there was a fight like this at the highest level of the sport was the 2024 All-Star Race, featuring Ricky Stenhouse Jr. and Kyle Busch at North Wilkesboro.

Now for a look at some of the best reactions from current and past drivers after a wild night of short track racing:

Ty Gibbs watching Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar fight. 🤣 pic.twitter.com/H5eptX8YWO

On the cooldown lap, it looked like there was a moment between Gibbs and Hocevar, with the No. 54 team warning him "don't clown with him." Afterwards, he was parked directly ahead of Hocevar and his rearview camera caught the entire fight.

Gibbs smiled wide as the brawl unfolded, and even tossed a water bottle into the middle of the fight. It flew over Hocevar's head, and struck the camera held by a Frontstretch.com reporter who was recording the confrontation.

😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/sgIHntqjPw

Here is the biggest clown in the sport @CarsonHocevar attempting to make contact with Ty Gibbs after the checkered flag right before his confrontation with Blaney. pic.twitter.com/nu6OLlx1mz

There was more than just a fight. pic.twitter.com/Wi6XZb000n

Moments after the fight, Hocevar turned to the fans and tried to hype up the crowd. Nearby, Ryan Preece was pointing at him and shouting something. Hocevar responded and it did not look friendly, but we aren't sure what words were shared.

Josh Berry was standing with Preece, and mockingly waved goodbye to Hocevar before mimicking the way he hyped up the track, laughing as he did.

"I didn't really see the accident to see what actually caused it, but just, yeah, it was a long time coming," Berry told Motorsport.com after.

Post-fight, Josh Berry and Ryan Preece display their on displeasure with Hocevar. #NASCAR pic.twitter.com/JVoXZaRhBA

"I was just trying to figure out what was going on," Wallace said in response to a question from Motorsport.com. "I was proud of Blaney for having some passion. I don't know what led to that, I've just seen the aftermath of him in the wall, but I'll have a beer with him and figure it out."

When asked if he had ever seen his close friend Blaney that angry, Wallace replied: "No, that surprised the f*** out of me."

.@BubbaWallace: “That surprised the f*ck out of me” on seeing his best friend @Blaney fight @CarsonHocevar #NASCAR pic.twitter.com/09Kdktxcio

"This place is awesome," said Bell, laughing. "This place is absolutely awesome "I love Bristol. I don't know what to say, but I love Bristol."

Trevor Bayne tried to ask him questions about his own race but Bell just kept laughing as he saw more replays: "I mean this is just awesome."

😭😭 pic.twitter.com/5jnf6g8Q29

"Yeah, again, I don't know the details of what happened there and how and why. I don't feel comfortable speaking on it until I see anything. I'd probably say something I regret if I haven't seen it. Like I said, I'm sure I'll see it. They'll probably forget who won the race (laughing)."

"I think he has shown that this is how he's going to race. You take a chance whenever you try to make a block on that young man, and that driver, who is very aggressive, doesn't mind being that and he stuck with that ... something that we haven't seen until this moment right here, and that he is willing to stand his ground.  If you're wanting to get physical about this and have something to say and start pushing around, he's going to be there.

"And look like he's willing to take on all comers whenever that happens."

"This incident, in and of itself, no big deal, but it's incident after incident after incident where the garage gets tired of it and this is where this spills over. This is bound to happen. It's just a matter of time, and I'll be honest, I'm surprised it took this long.

"And you have to know that's who you're racing.  In the same token, I've said before, the garage, at some point, is going to get tired of it, and they're not going to give him any slack.

"And no one has really stood up to him, to be honest with you.  Blaney is the first one to really confront him in a big, big way. It will continue to happen."

Taylor Gray: Big Blaney fan now" ... (In response to fan saying Blaney got his 'ass whooped') "Can't do much when the security guard tackles him.

Dean Thompson: Remember kids, always swing first

Regan Smith: Wanted to go to bed after the race, but what too much fun stuff to scroll coming out of Bristol right now. One thought: PLEASE NO PENALTIES NASCAR.

Corey LaJoie: Man I can't get enough of all the videos from last night. I've got many thoughts on Carson and Blaney scrapping but the main thing being…..I need to schedule myself a haircut.

Cleetus McFarland: Carson Hocevar keeping us entertained tonight!

Watch: From on-track to fight, this is what happened between Blaney and Hocevar

Carson Hocevar punches Ryan Blaney after late Bristol NASCAR clash

Ric Flair told drivers to take their helmets off and fight; NASCAR delivered

title: Three Keys For the Miami Heat to Win the Eastern Conference
description: Building around a newly acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Miami Heat must leverage elite interior defense and veteran perimeter shooting to overcome injury concerns and reclaim Eastern Conference dominance this upcoming season.
fullText:
MIAMI, Fla. – As training camp is on the horizon, here are three keys for the Miami Heat to win the Eastern Conference Finals in the 2026-27 NBA season:

Like the popular saying goes, "the best ability is availability." This take primarily falls upon Giannis Antetokounmpo, who played just 36 games last season; a new career low by a significant margin. The 10-time All-Star battled a calf injury and then the Milwaukee Bucks load-managed him. Antetokounmpo, when available last season, averaged 27.6 points on 62.4 percent shooting, 9.8 rebounds, and 5.4 assists.

Also, Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr., two of the Heat's free-agent signings, are over the age of 33. Both sharpshooters will get meaningful playing time, but putting a heavy workload on their shoulders should be taken with precaution.

Given the personnel, the Heat should have one of the best defenses in the league. Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo each received at least five All-Defensive selections. The Heat's new frontcourt duo should be difficult to score over, especially in the paint.

Davion Mitchell and Andrew Wiggins are two underrated defenders who don't get enough credit. They can both guard the perimeter and inside the arc. Despite being undersized (listed at 6'0), Mitchell shouldn't be classified as a lesser matchup. Wiggins, like Antetokounmpo and Adebayo, can guard multiple positions.

Coming off the bench are Bobby Portis Jr. and Pelle Larsson, both of whom are scrappy defenders.

As the saying goes, "defense wins championships." The Heat have the right personnel to live up to the phrase.

After acquiring Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster trade, the Heat needed to surround him with the right pieces, especially outside shooting. As the 31-year-old looks to dominate the paint, he will draw more attention to the defense, creating open looks for others.

Thompson and Hardaway Jr. were critical signees to provide Antetokounmpo floor spacing. Plus, the Heat retained three players (Wiggins, Mitchell, and Simone Fontecchio) who shot over 35 percent from behind the arc last season.

Following an eventful offseason, this team has the components to compete for a championship and win the Eastern Conference Finals. The Heat are among the early favorites, along with the Philadelphia 76ers, New York Knicks, and Boston Celtics. It's been 13 years since the last Larry O'Brien trophy made South Florida its home and a parade went down Biscayne Blvd. The current Heat team is looking to change that.

title: ‘Brilliant work’ – BBC pundit loved what Liverpool player did just before Alexander Isak goal
description: Alexander Isak fired Liverpool into the lead against Bournemouth this afternoon shortly before the hour mark, taking him to four goals for the season already and matching his tally from the whole of 2...
fullText:
Alexander Isak fired Liverpool into the lead against Bournemouth this afternoon shortly before the hour mark, taking him to four goals for the season already and matching his tally from the whole of 2025/26.

The first half had been a frustrating one for the Reds at the Vitality Stadium, with Andoni Iraola's side indebted to Alisson Becker for a brilliant reaction save from Evanilson to prevent his team from going behind.

The visitors didn't make the most auspicious of starts to the second half, either, but it was they who drew first blood on the south coast.

In the 57th minute, Cody Gakpo powered past Adrien Truffert on the right flank and delivered a cross into the penalty area that Florian Wirtz attempted to flick on. The ball fell to Isak, who anticipated the chance and promptly dispatched it past Djordje Petrovic.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, Rob Green was keen to give the Dutchman due credit for his role in the goal, saying: "Isak takes the plaudits from the Liverpool fans but it's Cody Gakpo down the right who does brilliant work and shrugs off two challenges.

"He finds the cross from under his feet and Antonio Silva, who's been brilliant, ducks the way out of the ball and I'm not sure why. That was the opportunity that Isak has been waiting for. No mistake from that."

(Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

All four of Isak's goals so far this season have been set up by Gakpo, whose contribution for the opener against Bournemouth was rightly praised by Green.

The persistence of Liverpool's number 18 in getting past Truffert and delivering the cross was exactly what Iraola would've loved to see, and it shows just why the Anfield hierarchy were right not to sell him to Manchester City in the final days of the summer transfer window.

The Dutchman was widely criticised by fans and pundits last season, when he played nowhere near his best, but he's been one of our best players in the opening month of this campaign.

The link-up between him and Isak has been increasingly productive, and it's a double act which could go a long way towards the Reds realising their ambitions for the 2026/27 season.

Both players deserve immense credit for how they've begun the campaign under Iraola.

title: Bournemouth vs Liverpool Confirmed Team News: The Latest Update Before Kickoff
description: Liverpool travel to Bournemouth for a 2 pm BST Premier League clash at Vitality Stadium. As of Sunday morning, both clubs have reported no fresh injury concerns following their midweek matches.The official starting lineups are expected about an hour before kickoff, so the main selection questions remain around Liverpool’s midfield and defense and Bournemouth’s rotation […] The post Bournemouth vs Liverpool Confirmed Team News: The Latest Update Before Kickoff appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Liverpool travel to Bournemouth for a 2 pm BST Premier League clash at Vitality Stadium. As of Sunday morning, both clubs have reported no fresh injury concerns following their midweek matches.

The official starting lineups are expected about an hour before kickoff, so the main selection questions remain around Liverpool's midfield and defense and Bournemouth's rotation after their European trip.

Liverpool remain without four players, while Bournemouth have four confirmed absentees. Andoni Iraola also returns to Bournemouth for the first time since leaving the club in the summer.

The Bournemouth vs Liverpool confirmed team news will settle the remaining questions before the match, with both sides looking to add an important result to their Premier League campaigns.

Liverpool's injury list remains unchanged from Friday. Conor Bradley is unavailable with a knee injury, while Giovanni Leoni is also out with a knee problem. Hugo Ekitike remains sidelined with an Achilles injury, and Federico Chiesa is unavailable because of a back issue.

Joe Gomez returned from a lay-off in Tuesday's 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Tottenham. His next appearance will be his 300th for Liverpool, but he is expected to start on the bench.

Virgil van Dijk is expected to return to the starting lineup alongside Jeremy Jacquet. Ronald Araujo could move to right-back, while Alisson Becker is expected to replace Giorgi Mamardashvili in goal.

Liverpool's expected formation is 4-2-3-1, with Alexander Isak leading the attack. Florian Wirtz should play behind him, with Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola on the wings. Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai are the expected midfield pairing.

Bournemouth also have four players unavailable. Eli Junior Kroupi remains out with a foot injury, while Amine Adli has a calf problem. Veljko Milosavljevic is sidelined with a knee injury and Julian Araujo remains out with a thigh issue.

Marco Rose reported no new injury concerns after Thursday's 2-1 Europa League win at Real Sociedad. He will assess his players after the trip before confirming his Premier League lineup.

Djordje Petrovic is expected to start in goal, with Adam Smith, James Hill, Antonio Silva and Adrien Truffert forming the back four.

Alex Scott is expected to start in midfield. Tyler Adams, Lewis Cook and Ryan Christie are options to partner him.

Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier are expected to play behind Francisco Evanilson. Tavernier has been Bournemouth's most productive attacker so far this season.

Bournemouth are still looking for their first Premier League win under Rose. They have drawn with Everton, Newcastle United and Brentford after losing their opening league game. Their European victory at Real Sociedad was the first win in the club's history in that competition.

Liverpool remain unbeaten in the Premier League but have had mixed results. They also made several changes during their midweek Carabao Cup match.

Liverpool have had more recovery time than Bournemouth, who traveled to Spain for their European fixture. Both managers have also said it's difficult to win at Vitality Stadium.

Iraola returns to his former club, while Rose has prepared for a Liverpool side with several selection options. Michael Oliver is the referee, and Sky Sports is showing the match live in the UK.

The Bournemouth vs Liverpool confirmed team news will be complete when the official lineups are released shortly before the 2 pm BST kickoff.

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Defense keeps searching for takeaways
description: Notes and thoughts on the Patriots defense, the home opener blues, Mike Smith’s connection with Aaron Rodgers, and more.
fullText:
Coming into Week 2 with a loss under their belt, the New England Patriots will try to get their season back on track in front of their home crowd. To do so, they will have to get their revenge against a Pittsburgh Steelers team that managed to beat them the last time they met in 2025.

Naturally, most of our attention this week was on that particular game. However, there is a lot going on at One Patriot Place these days, so let's clean out the notebook.

Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes.

The Patriots defense is one of the best in the NFL, but it is lacking in one critical area: taking the ball away. Last regular season, the unit ranked just 19th in the league with 19 takeaways. This year, it failed to record a fumble recovery or interception — while throwing three picks themselves — in the season-opening loss to the Seahawks.

Naturally, the Patriots are looking for ways to get better at creating turnovers.

"We focus on it like crazy," said defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr. "We focus on it in training camp, in OTAs, now. It's about the opportunity. Capitalizing on opportunity, in my opinion, is the biggest thing on takeaways. And the way you do that is you get more attempts."

For free agency pickup Kevin Byard, who led the NFL with seven interceptions last season, those attempts need to come within the framework of the defensive structure.

"You can't chase plays," Byard said. "You can't try to go out here and just say we're going to get turnovers and just try to magically just go make a play that's not for you. We have to stay true to the defense, stay true within the scheme. But for us, it's going to be more about trying to get those attempts at the ball.

"When I say attempts at the ball, just like, last week I think Jaylen Warren fumbled the ball, guys swarming the little check-down and the defensive line comes from the line of scrimmage and punches the ball out. I think those are the things that we can probably take to the next step as a defense. I think interceptions will come. Those things come in bunches. Those aren't situations where, if you're playing man coverage, you just turn around and look at the ball and you're not covering your man. I think it's one of those situations where the interceptions will come, but it's more about getting those attempts at the ball carrier."

Of those 19 regular season turnovers mentioned above, nine came in the form of fumble recoveries. That was good enough for 10th in the league. The interceptions, meanwhile, were not on the same level: despite fielding one of the NFL's top cornerbacks in Christian Gonzalez, New England's 10 picks ranked them only 18th.

Gonzalez did come close to an INT last week versus Seattle, but he dropped a Drew Lock pass attempt that landed in his hands. Needless to say, the Pro Bowler wants to get better at finishing plays.

He also thinks the Patriots as a whole need to get better at communicating on the defensive side of the ball.

"It just comes down to communication," he said, "getting us in the right spot and then capitalizing and making the play.

Historically, the Patriots are a pretty good team playing at home. However, Gillette Stadium has witnessed a disappointing streak as of late: between 2021 and 2025, the team has not won a single of its home openers:

2021: 17-16 loss vs. Miami Dolphins

2022: 37-26 loss vs. Baltimore Ravens

2023: 25-20 loss vs. Philadelphia Eagles

2024: 23-20 (OT) loss vs. Seattle Seahawks

2025: 20-13 loss vs. Las Vegas Raiders

The Patriots' last victory in their first home regular season game came in 2020, when quarterback Cam Newton led the team to a 21-11 win over the Miami Dolphins.

The Patriots' defensive quest for takeaways will be without Carlton Davis on Sunday versus Pittsburgh. The starting cornerback was ruled out for the game because of a neck injury, meaning New England will have to adjust at the position.

How? By primarily relying on two players, Marcus Jones and Charles Woods.

"It will be Marcus and Charles Woods that will come in and play a little bit 

Two members of the NFL's 2005 draft class will be in the spotlight on Sunday, albeit in different capacities. On one side, Aaron Rodgers will lead the Steelers offense as its starting quarterback; on the other, Mike Smith will try to help disrupt the future Hall of Famer.

The difference is, Smith will do so not from the field but the sidelines: he is in his second season coaching the Patriots' outside linebackers, despite getting drafted the same year as Rogers.

"It blows my mind," Smith said about their connection. "Somebody said the other day about 2010, I was with the Jets and we played New England in the playoffs. I was like, 'God, that was like 16 years ago.' And I was like, 'Oh my god, wait a minute, 16 years? Aaron Rogers is still playing.' It's like, 'What the heck?' That's just credit to him."

Whereas Rodgers was selected 24th overall in the first round in 2005, Smith remained on the board until the 234th pick in Round 7. His career also was significantly shorter, ending after just four seasons and 14 games. For comparison, Rodgers will start his 280th career game on Sunday.

"One guy had a better career than the other guy," said Mike Vrabel. "He's done it for a lot of years at a very high level, a Hall of Fame player. I guess it's funny to think that they're the same age and they got drafted the same year."

Due to injury and a drawn-out contract negotiation process, second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas had a slow start to his Patriots career and some rough stretches both in training camp and preseason. The season opener against Seattle was a different story, though: while only playing 19 snaps, Jacas registered a sack and a tackle for loss.

"I saw growth and that's what's most important, there is improvement," said Zak Kuhr. "There's going to be bumps and bruises along the way, and he's going to get some good experience. We just have to look through the bumps and bruises and make sure that's not the same mistakes. But I thought he played hard, he played physical, he played fast. Just have to clean up some details and technique. We want this week to look better than last week."

"Just playing a little bit faster, seeing things," added Mike Smith. "It takes time. We still have a long way to go, but things are starting to slow down, starting to recognize for him. We had loads of extra time to prepare for Seattle, but [this] is the player we expected to see and we've just got to continue from where that was at and keep building."

In its first training camp with Zak Kuhr as coordinator, the Patriots defense opted to incorporate more big nickel looks with three safeties on the field. In the season opener versus Seattle, the team used that package on 40% of snaps.

"It gives you some versatility in some calls and some structures," Kuhr explained. "When you play these teams that like to move around a ton, sometimes it just helps you to have that extra second-level defender rather than having a defender on the line of scrimmage. It just gives you some more multiplicity and you can kind of get to some different coverages easier with those guys than with the bigger guys."

When describing the Steelers' identity this week, Mike Vrabel specifically mentioned size and length. It's something no player will be more directly confronted with than Drake Maye.

The Patriots' starting quarterback will not just try to avoid the long reach of edge rushers such as T.J. Watt but also attempt to throw passes through what will be a forest of arms.

"I think it's hard to look at when they're jumping and when they're trying to get hands up," Maye said. "Cam Hayward had one last year that got tipped in the end zone and got picked. So, they have a special feeling for it, and they've done a lot in their careers of making plays, pass rush, and pass breakups. So, it can't be something I'm really thinking about. They're going to try to get their hands up.

"I think just finding good passing lanes and moving around the pocket in some different ways. But really, I think it's easy to say quick game, but at the same time, they know they're going to get their hands up fast. So, it's just being cognizant of it, whether it's technique or little things to get the hands down."

The Patriots have released multiple players with injury settlements over the last few weeks, but only in three of six cases have they actually agreed to pay a settlement sum. According to a report by salary cap expert Miguel Benzan, only offensive lineman Andrew Rupcich, defensive tackle Isaiah Iton and safety Eric Butler were financially compensated:

OL Andrew Rupcich: $94,167 (3-week salary)

DT Isaiah Iton: $28,611 (1week salary)

S Eric Butler: $143,506 (5-week salary)

Players released by a team with a settlement are allowed to return after an agreed-upon settlement period. This means that, theoretically, all six could come back to New England at some point.

For the second time over the last six months, TreVeyon Henderson was in the headlines because of a social media post. When asked about it this week, however, head coach Mike Vrabel came to the second-year running back's defense.

"I think he's handled it maturely, and I think he tried to explain himself," Vrabel said. "TreVeyon Henderson is a special person, a great teammate. I love being around him. I think he's pretty much spoke on what he thought and what he believes, and I think that that's impressive for him to be able to speak on it. I'll leave it up to him."

The Patriots will host the Steelers at Gillette Stadium for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday. From there, they are in their typical regular season mode.

This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday, off-day on Tuesday, and three straight practices plus injury reports from Wednesday through Friday. The team will then hold a final walkthrough on Saturday before traveling to Jacksonville for a 1 p.m. ET game with the Jaguars.

title: Yu, 13, wins record-breaking first major gold medal
description: China’s Yu Zidi, 13, wins a record‑breaking 200m women’s butterfly gold at the Asian Games in Tokyo.
fullText:
Chinese schoolgirl Yu Zidi lit up the opening day of the Asian Games with a record‑breaking 200m butterfly gold medal secured by a performance she described as "only so‑so".

The 13‑year‑old claimed her first major gold in two minutes 05.08 seconds, an Asian Games record that took almost half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei's mark from three years ago.

Yu, who is strongly tipped to make an impact at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, won by over three seconds in Tokyo from her team-mate Chang Mohan.

"It was only so-so," a smiling Yu said after receiving her medal, adding that her butterfly technique "is still slightly lacking".

"I hope I can swim even faster. I improved my time by 0.9 seconds here, and I believe I will perform better next time," she continued.

Yu, who will take part in two more individual events at the Asian Games, became the youngest ever swimmer to win a medal at the World Championships when she took bronze as a 12-year-old as part of China's 4x200m freestyle relay team last year.

title: The Washington Nationals had a roller coaster of a win last night that showed good and bad
description: The Nats pulled off a gritty win but we also saw bullpen woes and Blake Butera benching a star player
fullText:
I am sure plenty of people were watching college football over the Nats last night. However, if you did not catch this game, you missed out on a crazy contest. The Nats pulled off a wild 8-5 win in 11 innings. We saw the best and the worst of this team in this game. They got the job done and have won 6 of their last 7 games.

For the first 6 innings, the Nationals were in total control. That is largely due to the stellar work by Andrew Alvarez. He has fully established himself as a real piece in this Nats rotation. Since he re-joined the rotation following the deadline, he has a 2.15 ERA and a WHIP under 1.

Since rejoining the rotation after the trade deadline, Andrew Alvarez has a 2.15 ERA, 0.974 WHIP and 8.8 K/9. With one start to go this season, he's got a 3.17 ERA over 108 IP. Hasn't gotten a ton of attention, but he's solidified a spot in the 2027 rotation.

Alvarez has made it clear that he learned a lot from Foster Griffin this season. After Griffin got traded, Alvarez stepped into his shoes and provided similar performances. He has taken what he learned from Griffin and has used it to become a much better pitcher.

Even at the beginning of the year, Alvarez did a nice job limiting runs. However, he allowed a lot of base runners and could not go deep into games. Blake Butera only trusted Alvarez to go 4 innings or so. When he got past about 60 pitches, he would hit a wall.

Well, that is not the case anymore. Alvarez has gone at least 6 innings in three of his last four starts. The lefty is also riding a 13 inning scoreless streak. He only has one more start to go this season, but he has truly locked up a rotation spot for 2027. His fastball does not blow anyone away, but his curveball is such a weapon and allows him to rack up the strikeouts.

In the early going it looked like Alvarez was finally going to get the run support he deserves. Despite all of this brilliance, Alvarez is only 2-6 on the season. Of course, this is not his fault, but it is still a noteworthy stat.

The offense had Michael McGreevy on the ropes in the first inning. James Wood led the game off with a single and then Daylen Lile went deep to immediately make it 2-0. Lile hit his 22nd home run of the year. Surprisingly, only two NL outfielders have more RBI's than Lile, who has 88.

The only NL outfielders with more RBI than Daylen Lile (88 RBI) this season:

Pete Crow-Armstrong (105 RBI)
Jordan Walker (100 RBI) pic.twitter.com/SrJw1ewIi5

It looked like the offense was going to keep rolling in the first. They put more pressure on McGreevy who had to throw 34 pitches in the first inning. However, they could not get that big hit to blow things open.

That allowed McGreevy to settle in. While he only lasted 4 innings, he did not allow any more runs. The Nats added on in the 6th inning, but a 3-0 lead is still dicey with this bullpen. It was setting up for a nervy finish and that is exactly what happened.

In the 7th inning, the Nats defense melted down. They made two of their four errors in that inning, which allowed the Cardinals to pull within one. It was a sloppy game on both sides, with a combined six errors.

The defense was not the only thing that Blake Butera was not happy about though. After James Wood did not run out a grounder in the 8th inning, the Nats star got benched. Wood's effort has been inconsistent at best since coming back from his injury, so Blake Butera decided it was time to make a statement.

Blake Butera said he pulled James Wood in part because he did not run an 8th inning grounder out 100 percent.

Wood said he will be better moving forward. “I plan on being here for a long time, so I feel like I’ve got to be able to set an example for stuff like that.”

Both Butera and Wood handled things well after the game. Butera talked about how much faith he has in Wood and that he wants him to be more than just a slugger. For his part, Wood said he plans on being here for a long time. After the Cade Cavalli extension, that is an exciting thing for Nats fans to hear.

Whether it is injury related or just poor effort, Wood has not been running hard enough lately. Blake Butera made that known today and I like it. After Jorbit Vivas got benched a couple weeks ago, it seems to have gotten him going. Hopefully it can give Wood a second wind as well.

As we entered the bottom of the 9th, the Nats held on to a one run lead. They had a chance to put this game away early, but they let the Cardinals hang around. Erik Tolman tried to close the show, but he could not get the job done. To be fair to him, he mostly got blooped to death. Regardless, it was another blown save, the team's 40th of the season.

In the top of the 10th, the red hot Vivas saved the day for the Nats, guiding a ball into left field to score the ghost runner. However, the Nats could not put up another zero. It is harsh, but that is technically another blown save, extending the Nats record. However, Riley Cornelio only allowed that one run and avoided a walk off.

This was a weird game with a lot of bloops finding green grass. The weirdness continued in the 11th inning. After the Nats loaded the bases, they scored a run via catcher's interference. Then the struggling Jose Tena blew things open with a two-run double.

Jacob Young's IQ grabs the Nats a lead after Washington challenged a catcher's interference call and José Tena drives in a pair with a double! 👊 pic.twitter.com/hlEJURPX9k

With the Nats up 8-4, the lead finally seemed safe. However, if you have watched this team at all, you would know not to feel confident. After immediately allowing the ghost runner to score, Riley Cornelio got himself in a mess. He loaded the bases with nobody out in an 8-5 game.

All Nats fans watching the game were dreading and downright expecting a walk off grand slam. However, Cornelio locked in and got two strikeouts. Then Blake Butera replaced him with Will Dion, who got the final out to secure an 8-5 win.

This game had all the 2026 Nats staples. We got some huge performances from emerging talents, defensive miscues, a bullpen meltdown and a lot of runs. This game represents the best and worst of the Nats. In the end, the boys got the win and avoided a 90 loss season. They will look for the sweep this afternoon in St. Louis.

title: Sixers star LeBron James working out as he prepares for 24th season
description: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is back in the gym as he prepares for his 24th season in the league.
fullText:
For 23 seasons, LeBron James has been the gold standard in the NBA. Arguably the greatest player to ever play this game, James now heads to the Philadelphia 76ers as he prepares for an unprecedented 24th season in the league. One doesn't make it this far without work ethic and the mental toughness to keep going and keep working.

After averaging 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.1 rebounds in year 23 with the Los Angeles Lakers, James is back in the gym preparing for what's to come. The Sixers are a team that hasn't been past Round 2 since 2001 and hasn't won a title since 1983. This is also a team that has a lot of new pieces, which means there will be a lot of work to do in terms of chemistry and cohesion.

No matter what the challenges, James appears to be ready and prepared for what 2026-27 will throw at him.

title: Trinidad Chambliss took a win, and a title, from Lane Kiffin on Saturday night
description: LSU-Ole Miss lived up to the hype, and gave the sport a new main character
fullText:
Last fall, Lane Kiffin named Trinidad Chambliss the new starting quarterback at Ole Miss, after the Rebels lost Austin Simmons to an injury. Chambliss took that new title and ran with it, leading Ole Miss to a spot in the College Football Playoff and a thrilling upset of Georgia in the Sugar Bowl.

Kiffin ran to Baton Rouge to take over as the new head coach of the LSU Tigers.

On Saturday night in Tiger Stadium the two met again, this time on opposite sides of the field, and Chambliss took another title from his former coach.

The title of college football's main character.

Chambliss and the Rebels knocked off LSU by a final score of 32-24, in a thrilling contest that came down to the final seconds. In this highly anticipated matchup of top-ten teams, Ole Miss now has the edge on a path to the College Football Playoff this season, and Chambliss has put himself firmly in the discussion for national accolades.

A good personal barometer regarding whether a sports storyline has broken through to the mainstream is, well, my mom. My mom is a huge football fan, consuming all the content she can on both television and online, but her main focus is the NFL.

So when she brings up a college storyline — as she did on Saturday morning when she asked me why LSU and Kiffin were all she saw on TV this week — it means a story has escaped the sports world and become something more. This was certainly the case with Kiffin's return to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday night, a moment that has been hyped since Kiffin got on a plane to Baton Rouge.

As I explained to her on Saturday, that focus was because the LSU coach had cemented himself as the sport's main character.

A national conversation that focused on Kiffin, for good reason, now shifts to his former quarterback.

Chambliss was near-perfect on Saturday night, in the middle of a charged cauldron and frenzied atmosphere. He completed 33-of-48 passes for 363 yards and a pair of touchdowns, and one interception, and scored the decisive touchdown on a run in the fourth quarter, after the Tigers had come back from what was a 24-7 deficit to knot the game at 24-24.

The quarterback started red-hot, throwing both of his touchdown passes in the first half, but as the Tigers clawed back into the game, Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense started to slow down.

But then, when the Rebels needed Chambliss most, after the Tigers had tied the game and starting running back Kewan Lacy was sidelined with a shoulder injury, the quarterback stood tall. On the drive that culminated in his touchdown run to stake Ole Miss to a 32-24 lead, Chambliss completed 6-of-8 passes for 62 yards. Including his 14-yard touchdown run, Chambliss accounted for 76 of the yards on what was officially a 75-yard drive, which included a holding penalty.

Here is that touchdown run that sent Vaught-Hemingway Stadium into bedlam:

SMOOTH OPERATORRRR 😮‍💨@TrinidadChambl1 x #HottyToddy pic.twitter.com/IDyNQtXGEu

Speaking after the game Pete Golding, Chambliss' new head coach, highlighted his quarterback's competitive greatness.

He's a fierce competitor. Y'all know that and have seen that for a long time. When we talk about competitive greatness, being at your best when your best is needed, that's him. Our guys believe in him. He probably wants a couple throws back, but he made the ones when he had to. He doesn't get too high or too low; he's steady. I said that this morning on GameDay: I don't care what level you coach; if you don't have a quarterback, good luck. We've got a good one, and he's a good dude. I'm super grateful.

Some of the players on the other side of the field gave Chambliss his just due after the game, starting with LSU linebacker Whit Weeks, on what is so tough playing against him:

I think we say tonight, his versatility. He's a ball player, at the end of the day, we knew that going into it. He made more plays than we did.

Props to him. He is really good at what he does. Like you said he extends plays. I got to play better, everyone has to play better but I am going to take that one.

As is the case anytime a college quarterback becomes a national talking point, the conversation soon turns to the player's NFL prospects. That is just how things go in the football world. Chambliss will certainly face question marks as he embarks on an NFL journey, starting with his beginnings at Division II Ferris State, his age, and his size.

But what continues to stand out watching Chambliss is his willingness to, and success when, attacking the middle of the field in the passing game.

Take his first touchdown pass of the night, this strike over the middle to Traylon Ray:

ON A SILVER T-RAY 🍽️ @TraylonRay6 x #HottyToddy pic.twitter.com/4Oy0SkY6oP

These are the types of plays that will definitely serve his evaluation well.

There is also the creativity that Chambliss brings to the table, that the football world again saw on Saturday night:

TRINIDAD WITH THE ASSIST 😮‍💨@TrinidadChambl1 x @TraylonRay6 pic.twitter.com/JB4TxPrs5s

Or this beautiful throw on the move, fitting the ball over a pair of defenders while rolling to his right:

AN ABSOLUTE DIME 🤯 @TrinidadChambl1 x @TraylonRay6 #HottyToddy pic.twitter.com/36Vw4HlUya

Then of course there is how Chambliss ended the night — and perhaps took that title of main character — in this post-game moment that immediately went viral:

Trinidad Chambliss: “HOTTY FUCKING TODDY” pic.twitter.com/M5e11g8iW9

Chambliss later apologized for the moment, admitting that the emotions of the night got the better of him:

Emotions were high, that's the best play in football being in victory formation. My emotions were high for the game, and I kind of got caught up in the moment with the interview. That's not who I am with the interview. I'm deeply apologetic to Holly Rowe and everyone out there who was listening, and that's not who I am so I'm sorry about that.

Speaking after the game, Chambliss did conceded that it was an emotional night, and that he was happy this game was behind him and the Rebels:

Yeah, this one meant a lot more than the other games. I mean, the coaches that were here are now at LSU, some players as well. So a little bit more to it. So yeah, I'm really happy we got the win. I wanted this one really bad, and our team did too. So, just proud of them and so happy we got the win.

Yeah, finally got that one out of the way. I feel like we've been hearing and talking about this game all offseason. So proud of our team. So glad we got the win.

His former coach had some thoughts as well on the Ole Miss passer:

Yeah we were pretty conservative on him early. Tried to keep the score in front of us, tried to give him some softer looks, and he did a really good job. Guys made plays for them in the receiving game too. He's hard to defend, and a lot of people haven't beat him. So we let this one get away because I feel like we came back, had momentum, and let them go down and score. On the touchdown, we have a guy out there and Trinidad outruns him. Even with that, I felt like we were in a good position to go down and score and get a two-point conversion. It took a lot of time to get there, so he [Chambliss] wasn't going to get the ball back. The hope was to get it to overtime. We wouldn't have given them much time because again, you can't leave Trinidad with any time especially with their kicker.

Chambliss and the Rebels won a game on Saturday night, one that has been circled for months on everyone's college football character.

And in that win, the quarterback made himself the sport's main character.

At least until our next great Kiffin moment.

title: Patriots Wire staff predictions for Patriots-Steelers Week 2 game
description: The Patriots Wire staff make their final predictions for Sunday's Week 2 matchup between the Patriots and Steelers.
fullText:
The New England Patriots will try to right the many wrongs they had in the season opener in Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

For the Patriots, Week 1 was one of the most disappointing regular season losses in recent memory. They were on the road against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, who lost their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold, to an injury in the first drive of the game.

It was an opportunity for the Patriots to exact revenge on the team that crushed their championship dreams last season at Super Bowl LX.

Instead, they blew a 10-point lead in a game where Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions. Star wide receiver A.J. Brown is on injured reserve, and Maye is coming off the worst performance of his NFL career. The deck is stacked against the Patriots, despite the team being at home against a Steelers team with just as many issues.

Pittsburgh's Week 1 game was more eventful than New England's 13-10 loss in Seattle, but they still had to dig deep to knock off the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 with Cooper Rush at quarterback.

They couldn't get their running game going, and Aaron Rodgers went 24-of-40 passing for 221 yards and one touchdown. So, nothing to write home about for the future Hall of Fame quarterback.

The Patriots turned the ball over five times and still only lost by a touchdown when they faced the Steelers last season. Will things be different this time around?

Here are Patriots Wire's official staff predictions for the game:

Danny Jaillet: Patriots 21, Steelers 16

Jordy McElroy: Patriots 28, Steelers 17

Sophie Weller: Patriots 21, Steelers 17

Matt Legros: Patriots 23, Steelers 19

title: STRING’S SUNDAY MORNING THOUGHTS
description: Tbh before this season started I thought this was the year I made a clean break from writing for GBH. It’s been a good 15 year run and it’s time to just be done. And then yesterday happens…and here I am again on a Sunday morning needing to process my thoughts. I hate it but […]
fullText:
Tbh before this season started I thought this was the year I made a clean break from writing for GBH. It's been a good 15 year run and it's time to just be done.

And then yesterday happens…and here I am again on a Sunday morning needing to process my thoughts. I hate it but we are who we are.

THIS LOSS WAS MADE IN THE OFFSEASON

I think it's important to not be too critical because this is one loss not 5 but this is a big loss. And much of this loss happened in the offseason through replacement of critical coaching staff pieces. Bateman, replaced by Hemphill, Chaos, replaced by ERob, Klein, replaced by Wiggins/Joey Lynch…all contributed to where are today. DL was unproductive. Offense was called fine but QB play left everything to be lacking. Defense overall was not to our standard.

Side note. I cant excuse anything I saw on the field yesterday but I can explain the offense's performance. The defensive let down is inexcusable.

Back to the point here. We had a decent enough first staff. The single most important thing a HC will do is maintain a good staff and it looks like Elko fell short here. We made comfort hires and it showed up on the field this past weekend. That is both a short term (this season because we're locked in) and long term (will cover that next) issue.

Stephen Covey said that thing are made twice. First in the mind as a vision plan or blueprint and then physically through action. If we're going to agree that the hires that we made were perhaps part of the issue then we have to think about the process we used to get here. We, as an institution, allowed for this offensive staff to be put together as it is. We, as an institution, allowed for this defensive staff to be put together as is. Who gets to make the next set of decisions given how these are trending through three games? Even if the decision is to commit to what we have…who makes that decision? Does Elko have the credibility at this point to make that decision on his own? Should he?

I like Mike Elko. I think he's a systemic thinker. I think he values culture. I think he is a good leader of a program in the NIL era. I think he is an excellent defensive mind. I think Elko is an overfunctioner and is trying to do too much by having influence over both the offense and the defense while trying to make critical fourth down play calls in key situations. I think that's too much for anyone to handle and I think we need to review how many in game decisions run through our head coach because it seems like all of them, big or small, run through him.

He is who he is. I cant defend yesterday's performance. I can only look to the future and hope that the coaching staff recognizes that there is a distant blueprint on how to set Marcel up to be successful against a Blake Baker defense. I also dont think benching him is the solution because, while Brady Hart and Casuga might be good someday, I do not think that day is today. I dont think you make that choice unless you have to.

I go back to Elko's opening press conference as Texas A&M coach. In it he said "I think I embrace my process as a head coach. I think that's one of the things I told Ross in this process is I believe in who I am. I believe in my process for making decisions. We won't always make the right one. But when we make the wrong one, we're going to identify it, we're going to evaluate it, we're going to fix it, and we're going to move forward and not second guess what we're doing and believe in who we are and know that we have what it takes to build a blueprint for the best program in the country."

He clearly outlined the process by which he can get out of the situation we are currently in. This is predicated on him identifying that perhaps he did make a bad decision here. Maybe he didnt. Maybe this is a one off game and we go 11-1. But regardless, we clearly did not make the right decisions for this game. We need to identify it, evaluate it, and we need to fix it. Those are Coach Elko's words and we need to hold him to them.

title: 🐈‍⬛ Brian Brobbey earns cult hero status with hat-trick vs Man City
description: Sunderland's recent resurgence as a force to be reckoned with in the Premier League has been one of the feel-good stories in the top flight of English football. Under Regis Le Bris, the club has becom...
fullText:
Sunderland's recent resurgence as a force to be reckoned with in the Premier League has been one of the feel-good stories in the top flight of English football.

Under Regis Le Bris, the club has become one of the toughest outfits to come up against, and with Brian Brobbey impressively leading the line, few will fancy 90 minutes against the Black Cats.

And against Manchester City this afternoon, the Dutch international and former Ajax standout is putting together a one-off performance to remember, one week after he made himself out to be a nuisance against Arsenal at the Stadium of Light.

In doing so, Brobbey now sits alongside a handful of memorable figures and one outright club icon, becoming just the fifth Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick, joining Kevin Phillips (two), Darren Bent, Jermain Defoe, and Adam Johnson.

Brobbey is also the first player to hit City on three occasions in a single match since Jamie Vardy back in September 2020, signaling his arrival as a true goal threat in the league.

And with the transfer market now being the Wild West that it has become, Brobbey may well become the next big summer signing should this run of form continue.

title: Caitlin Clark, Nike release behind-the-scenes video on signature shoe design
description: With her Caitlin 1's scheduled to release to the public on Oct. 1, Nike revealed a behind-the-scenes video into Caitlin Clark's shoe design process.
fullText:
With her Caitlin 1s set to release to the public on Oct. 1, Nike unveiled a unique behind-the-scenes video highlighting the meticulous details of Caitlin Clark's shoe and the elements the former Hawkeye wanted to incorporate into its design.

The full video features Clark alongside Nike's Product Line Manager Alex Zerzan and Footwear Designer Ben Nethongkome, where the three-time WNBA All-Star describes exactly how she wants her first signature shoe to feel, look, and act for her and everyone wearing it.

We are very close 😏 https://t.co/vz1dW4rHFD

The first half of the behind-the-scenes video shows several beneficial design elements Zerzan and Nethongkame used to meet Clark's desires for the shoe. Some of those components include the multidirectional traction blade pattern on the base, the responsive Nike Air Turbo Zoom unit near the front of the shoe, and the first-of-its-kind Opticast technology in the upper, to name a few.

"Caitlin is elite. She's an elite basketball player, and her standard when it comes to her footwear as well is elite also, and you know, I think she really pushed and challenged the team," Zerzan said. "What I love about working with Caitlin is she knows exactly what she wants, and you'll know if Caitlin likes something because it's immediate."

The video continues to highlight more intricate designs within the shoe that pay homage to Clark's iconic personality and competitiveness, such as the split "C" and "2" shaped Opticast upper material, double beveled Nike logo that subtly forms her initials, various inverted colorway elements, and hidden "Easter Egg" quotes and phrases from Clark's past.

"Nike doesn't cut any corners, and a lot of time has gone into this, and, you know, I never thought I would get to have my own signature shoe, and now that I do. It's pretty special. They're waiting for this moment, and we definitely delivered," Clark said.

"I hope every hooper puts a shoe on and hopes that they can have a signature one day or that they can go on the court and make 35-foot threes. Just give them that sense of belief and that sense of confidence to achieve whatever they want to. We're trying to make the best shoe there's ever been."

Nike also revealed its full initial lineup of Caitlin 1 colorways, including shades such as "Warning Code," "Midnight Fever," "Caitlin Blue," "Ice Cold," "Purple Venom," and "Cave Stone."

TECH SPECS: Nike Caitlin 1 📋

-Nike Opticast upper
-Air Zoom Turbo
-Cushlon Foam
-Quick Response Caitlin Clark traction https://t.co/eqXkh8dVX3 pic.twitter.com/1A2JbZ3863

For the Oct. 1 initial launch, only "Caitlin Blue" and "Warning Code" will be released. Meanwhile, House of Heat has reported that the release dates for the four other colorways are as follows:

"Midnight Fever" - Oct. 14, 2026

House of Heat has also reported that the "WNBA All-Star" will be released sometime this fall/winter, while her "Teal Fade" will be released on Dec. 31, 2026, "Triple Black" on Jan. 5, 2027, "Friendship Bracelet" on Feb. 24, 2027, and "Electric Green" on March 15, 2027.

With so many options to choose from in the wide range of Caitlin1 colorways, Cark certainly hit a home run with her first Nike Signature shoe release.

title: Three Bold Predictions Bucs vs Browns
description: Three Bold Predictions Bucs vs Browns
fullText:
The Bucs drafted Rueben Bain Jr. to become the type of disruptive edge defender they have been missing, but his NFL debut was relatively quiet. Tampa Bay recorded only one sack against Joe Burrow, and that came from linebacker Josiah Trotter on a blitz. The Bucs will want significantly more production from a front that includes Bain, Yaya Diaby, Al Quadin Muhammad, Calijah Kancey and Vita Vea. Cleveland allowed Watson to be sacked five times in Week 1, and Bain has the power to take advantage of a Browns offensive line still trying to find its footing. The rookie gets home at least once and records the first sack of his NFL career.

Irving picked up where he left off last season in Week 1, finishing with 93 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown against Cincinnati. He was effective as both a runner and a receiver and became an important part of Tampa Bay's short-passing game. The Bucs do not necessarily have to give Irving 20 carries to make it happen. His involvement as a receiver gives Zac Robinson another way to manufacture touches and get Irving into space. After coming seven yards short in Week 1, Irving reaches triple digits against the Browns.

After losing three fumbles against Cincinnati, nobody on Tampa Bay's offense will have more attention on ball security than Baker Mayfield. Those turnovers were a major reason Tampa Bay lost despite Mayfield completing 23 of 28 passes and posting a 98.8 passer rating. Four Bucs fumbles resulted in 24 Cincinnati points. Now Mayfield gets his former team in his first home game of the season, and Cleveland allowed Jacksonville to score 34 points in Week 1, and this could be the game where Tampa Bay finally turns its offensive efficiency into points without giving possessions away. The prediction: Mayfield protects the football, throws three touchdown passes, and finishes the afternoon without a turnover.
