title: Braves magic number: Atlanta can clinch NL East Division with win or Phillies loss
description: The Atlanta Braves hold a lead over the Philadelphia Phillies for the National League East, but have not clinched the division yet.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves clinched a spot in MLB playoffs with their win over the Houston Astros on Friday night. On Sunday, they will have a chance to wrap up the National League East division title.

The Braves "magic number" is down to one following Saturday's win over the Astros and Philadelphia Phillies loss to the New York Mets.

Atlanta now holds a 6-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies. So if the Braves win or Phillies lose on Sunday, Atlanta wins the division.

[DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks]

Any combination of Braves victories and Phillies losses that equals the magic number will result in the NL East Division title for the Braves.

To calculate the magic number, take the number of games remaining on the leading team's schedule, add the number one, and subtract the number of games the first-place team leads by in the loss column.

Each time the Braves win, that reduces the magic number by one. Each time the Phillies lose, that also reduces the magic number by one.

The Braves have series left with the Astros, Cincinnati Reds and Miami Marlins. The Phillies have series left with the Mets, Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays.

Atlanta does hold the tiebreaker over Philadelphia.

fullText:
Erling Haaland's goal against Sunderland today means he has now scored against all 25 sides he has faced in the Premier League.

The Norwegian's 81st minute finish against the Black Cats at the Etihad Stadium was the final piece in the puzzle of the Premier League teams he's come up against in just over four years in England.

He's most enjoyed playing West Ham in the top-flight, with 11 strikes in just eight games with the Hammers.

10 goals have come against both Crystal Palace and Wolves, while he's now the leading scorer in Manchester derbies in the Premier League with nine goals.

Fulham, Everton and Brighton have all felt the force of Haaland's irrepressible hunger for goals too, while he's stood up in plenty of big games against regular title rivals Arsenal with six goals against them.

He's even managed to find the net against three teams – Sheffield United, Luton Town and Coventry – despite playing them just once in the competition.

It took him until his third meeting with Sunderland before finding the net however.

His latest strike takes him to five in the Premier League so far this season, putting him in the early lead for this year's Golden Boot.

He's already won that award in three of his first four campaigns at City, including a record-breaking haul of 36 in 2022/23.

In total, he has 117 goals in 137 Premier League appearances. Only 22 men have ever found the net 

Just last week he became the third highest scorer in our 132-year history, surpassing Tommy Johnson on 166.

He's now hot on the heels of Eric Brook, who found the net 177 times between 1928 and 1939, but still some way off Sergio Aguero's record of 260.

title: Tottenham Hotspur injury blow confirmed after latest statement
description: Pedro Porro Injury Blow Leaves Tottenham Sweating Ahead of Key RunTottenham have another problem, and this one matters. Pedro Porro has pulled out of Spain duty after suffering an injury in the 3-2 ho...
fullText:
Tottenham have another problem, and this one matters. Pedro Porro has pulled out of Spain duty after suffering an injury in the 3-2 home defeat to Aston Villa, adding fresh concern to a side already short on rhythm, points and fit players.

Porro went down early in the game with what looked like a hamstring issue. He received treatment on the pitch, tried to continue, then came off in the 19th minute with Archie Gray replacing him. The reaction told its own story. He looked frustrated, hit the turf in anger and limped off with help from the medical staff.

For Tottenham, this is awkward timing. For Porro, it is worse. He had only just returned to regular action after an extended summer break following Spain's World Cup success in North America. The Villa match was only his third start of the season, which underlines the bigger issue here, fitness management and recurring setbacks.

Roberto De Zerbi did not try to dress it up afterwards. "Listen, Pedro, I said after the World Cup, I said the management of Pedro should be different, because after the World Cup, many games. I don't know what the problem is. It's a hamstring, I think. Hopefully, it's not a big problem."

That is not a diagnosis, but it is enough to confirm the obvious. Spurs fear a proper lay-off and Spain have now lost him for the upcoming international window. No replacement has been called up, which says plenty about the timing and nature of the withdrawal.

Porro had already missed games this season. After sitting out the opening-day defeat to Brentford, he returned from the bench in the 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton, still Tottenham's only win of the campaign. He then started league matches against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, missed the 0-0 draw with Everton and the cup defeat at Liverpool because of what De Zerbi had labelled a "small muscular problem", then broke down again against Villa.

Spain had selected the 27-year-old for a four-match Nations League schedule, including a trip to Wembley to face England, plus fixtures against Croatia and the Czech Republic. That will now pass without him.

Latest developments around Tottenham and Pedro Porro are now centred on how long he will be out, because Spurs can afford very little more disruption. They remain without Mykhailo Mudryk, Dejan Kulusevski, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert, while De Zerbi clarified that Mateus Fernandes coming off at half-time against Villa was not injury-related. He also said Mathys Tel's omission was a "technical decision".

The larger picture is plain enough. Tottenham have spent more than £300 million and they are still winless in the league, sitting in the relegation zone. Yes, they finally scored their first Premier League goals of the season against Villa. No, that does not make the situation any better.

After the break, they go to Manchester United on October 10, then face Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace. That run already looked important. Without Pedro Porro, it looks even more serious.

title: USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin
description: The United States stage a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.
fullText:
Tries: Elmes Kinlan, Moloney-MacDonald, Wafer, Higgins, King, Wall Cons: O'Brien (3)

Tries: Perris-Redding, Rogers, Treder (2), Taufoo, Tafuna Cons: Vogel (5)

The United States staged a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.

Scott Bemand's side raced into a comfortable lead after 20 minutes following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer and went in 24-12 ahead at the break.

Erin King added a fifth try early in the second half as Ireland looked to be cruising at 31-12 up, but a loss of control and discipline aided USA, who under the guidance of their Irish head coach Jack Hanratty, managed to turn the game around.

Elmes Kinlan's yellow card was a turning point, with USA taking advantage of their numerical advantage as they scored four successive tries to take an unlikely win.

In the first women's rugby Test match to take place at the home of football team Shamrock Rovers, Ireland started with intent and, after persistent pressure, they made the breakthrough on seven minutes.

Bemand's side carved USA open with a slick passage of play as Moloney-MacDonald found Stacey Flood with a quick offload and she drove forward before feeding Elmes Kinlan, who finished in the corner.

Their second try arrived on 14 minutes with Moloney-MacDonald scoring off the driving maul before Wafer then forcing her way over soon after to further extend their advantage.

The Eagles, who were without Ilona Maher, responded well after that tough start and co-captain Georgie Perris-Redding got them on the scoreboard as she bundled over on 25 minutes, with teenager Bella Vogue nailing the conversion.

Ireland re-established their comfortable lead just two minutes after USA's try as Anna McGann galloped forward and offloaded to Eve Higgins to dot down, with Dannah O'Brien adding the extras.

USA came again at the other end and the experienced Hope Rogers crashed over after patient play to narrow the gap again before the break.

Ireland started the second half as did the first and added a fifth try soon after the restart.

Robyn O'Connor darted forward and Erin King eventually grounded the ball with the try awarded after a TMO (television match official) review.

Ireland then dropped off and USA capitalised with Kathryn Treder scoring after peeling off a driving maul from the line-out.

Elmes Kinlan was then sent to the sin-bin for not rolling away quickly enough from a tackle and USA punished the hosts.

Treder was again on the scoresheet with a carbon copy of her first try and USA then edged in front for the first time on 69 minutes as Hallie Taufoou forced her way over with Vogel accurate from the tee to give them a two-point lead.

With momentum on their side, the USA pressed home their advantage with Freda Tafuna scoring the pick of their tries as she held off a number of Irish players before diving over.

Dorothy Wall got a late try for Ireland as the clock ticked into red, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over and held out for a fine win.

Bemand's side will now look to bounce back in their next game against Japan in Galway on 27 September.

Replacements: Leatherman, Hill-Huse, Woods, Jarrell-Searcy (co-capt), Bailey, Zackary, Bargell, Mason.

title: Humble Keelon Russell assesses Alabama after Florida State win: ‘Man, oh, man, we put up 50′
description: Quarterback was quick to give credit to his Alabama teammates.
fullText:
Alabama amassed more than 600 yards en route to a 50-36 win over Florida State in a game that saw two weather delays, no halftime and some offensive fireworks.

Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell, who finished with 320 passing yards and three scores, kept it all in perspective.

"I still have a long ways to go," Russell said during an on-field postgame interview. "Still developing."

That's quite a statement from Russell, who also added 56 yards and touchdown on the ground.

"Three things coach always says is keep your completions, keep the ball going forward and don't take sacks or negative plays," the quarterback said.

"I feel like we did that fairly well today."

Russell cited the struggles — and turnovers — a week ago against Kentucky.

"I know I had to come into this game limit the turnovers and mistakes, stop playing like a rookie, stop playing timid," he said. "Be calm in the pocket, and I think I showed that today."

He was quick to credit teammates for the offensive success.

"I would not have done anything without this team," he said. "These guys came out ready to dominate.

"Man, oh, man, we put up 50 today. I'm just so blessed and so glad I'm on this still team."

title: Ole Miss trolls LSU with Kiffin video after beating Tigers, ‘Callin Baton Rouge’
description: Rebels spoil Kiffin's return to LSU.
fullText:
Ole Miss had it cued up and ready to go.

After Trinidad Chambliss passed for 363 yards and two touchdowns and ran for a tiebreaking score in the fourth quarter to lead Ole Miss over LSU and Lane Kiffin 32-34, it was just a matter of waiting for the right time.

As soon as LSU posted the final score, the Rebels social media team jumped.

The official Ole Miss social media account reposted LSU with a 26-second video featuring Kiffin.

Of course, Chambliss let out a "Hoddy F---ing Toddy" on national TV, then apologized later.

But as soon as the game was over, the stadium blared Garth Brook's "Calin Baton Rouge," an LSU staple.

LSU stormed back from a 24-7 halftime deficit to tie the game before Chambliss engineered a 75-yard touchdown drive without the services of top running back Kewan Lacy, who left the game with an injured left shoulder.

Chambliss faked a handoff and ran 14 yards against the grain, outracing LSU safety Ty Benefield to the left pylon, and Ole Miss (3-0, 1-0 Southeastern Conference) added a 2-point conversion to take an eight-point lead with 6:14 to go.

Ole Miss drew LSU offside twice while lining up for the conversion before converting it from a half-yard out on a direct snap to JT Lindsey.

LSU answered by driving 69 yards to the Ole Miss 6 before Sam Leavitt missed open tight end Zach Grace along the goal line with a third-down pass, and then had his fourth-down pass deflect off the helmet of defensive end Kam Franklin. Jaylon Braxton intercepted the ball in the end zone to seal it as Kiffin sank into a low crouch with both hands on his white LSU visor.

As time expired, Ole Miss celebrated by charging from the sideline across the field. Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles said he and a number of his teammates were just trying to find former coaches who'd joined Kiffin at LSU.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin, Ole Miss’ Pete Golding react Trinidad Chambliss’ play
description: The Rebels jumped out to a 24-7 lead.
fullText:
Ole Miss was not hospitable Saturday night to guests Lane Kiffin and LSU through one half of football.

The Rebels took a 24-7 halftime lead, thanks, in large part, to Ole miss quarterback Trinidad Chamblis, who has thrown for 248 yards and two scores.

"Obviously, Trinidad is getting a bunch of plays," LSU coach Lane Kiffin, who is 0-25 as a FBS coach when trailing by 17, said during an ABC halftime interview. "We have to do a better job of containing him with the whole game plan against him.

"So, we have another half, go in here and regroup."

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said Chambliss' 21 completions comes down to one thing.

"His preparation," Golding said at halftime. "He's been that way all year. That's who he is. He works extremely hard throughout the week. … He's playing well and he's going to have to play well in the second half, too.

"They scored on that last possession right there. We have to get off the field on third down. … A lot of football left."

LSU's biggest issue is third downs. The Tigers defense had given up only 4 of 27 third-down conversions on the season before Saturday.

The Rebels converted 7 of 9 in the first half.

fullText:
President Donald Trump on Sunday said his proposed 250-foot triumphal arch will now be a "top grade" military complex that will house drones, snipers and ammunition.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that he has agreed to convert the arch "at the strong request" of the U.S. military, and "for National Security purposes."

The "Military Complex/Triumphal Arch" near Arlington National Cemetery will "house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage," Trump wrote. "There will be no facility like this anywhere in the World."

Trump's new claims about the triumphal arch, which come as veterans groups, historic preservationists and others attempt to stop the project, resemble his arguments for the need to build a ballroom at the White House. Trump initially said the ballroom was needed to entertain guests but more recently has said it was a "desperately needed National Security structure."

The Trump administration, which plans to begin construction on the arch as soon as November, has been consulting with D.C.'s and Virginia's historic preservation offices as part of a required federal preservation process. The topic of converting the arch to a military complex has not previously been raised.

The White House did not immediately respond to questions about the president's post. The Pentagon and the Interior Department, which oversees the federal parkland where the arch would be built, did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

title: Gas prices are squeezing voters as Trump calls the increase a small price to pay
description:
— Quinten Martinez, pumping gas under a hot South Texas sun, remembers a time when fueling up didn't require difficult decisions.
“Is it going to be groceries this week?" asked the 28-year-old Amazon delivery driver as he watched the numbers tick higher. "Is it gonna be getting gas in our tank to go to work?”
He shook his head when asked about President Donald Trump's assertion last week that higher gas prices are a small price to pay for the war with Iran.
fullText:
EDINBURG, Texas (AP) — Quinten Martinez, pumping gas under a hot South Texas sun, remembers a time when fueling up didn't require difficult decisions.

"Is it going to be groceries this week?" asked the 28-year-old Amazon delivery driver as he watched the numbers tick higher. "Is it gonna be getting gas in our tank to go to work?"

He shook his head when asked about President Donald Trump's assertion last week that higher gas prices are a small price to pay for the war with Iran.

"I don't feel like it's a good trade-off," Martinez said. "I don't feel like this is good for anyone."

Voters across the country, and across the political spectrum, tend to agree.

Interviews with voters in several states, along with a fresh round of national polling, reveal an overwhelming sense of frustration that skyrocketing gas prices — a direct result of Trump's war — are creating serious and sustained financial hardships for America's working class.

The acute concerns are adding to a bad political environment that may be worsening for Trump and his Republican Party as early voting gets underway in the November midterm elections.

Historically, the party holding the White House has suffered major losses in midterms. Today, seven weeks before Election Day, Republican candidates at all levels are struggling with the additional burden of Trump's weak approval ratings, an unpopular foreign conflict and an affordability crisis that Trump and his congressional allies had promised to fix.

But when Trump campaigned in North Carolina on Wednesday, he played down the impact of surging gas prices.

"You have a little higher. It's a very inexpensive price to pay for what we've done," Trump said of the war, which he describes as critical to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. "Remember that. It's a little more. Frankly, even if it was a lot more."

Despite what Trump says, there are few things that may matter more this election year than the price of a gallon of gasoline, according to political operatives in both parties.

Gas prices are moving sharply in the wrong direction at a time of year when drivers typically get some relief. The national average for a gallon of gas reached $4.48 on Friday, according to AAA, up roughly 17 cents over the last week, 40 cents in a month and $1.27 from a year ago.

"Gas prices matter because they're one of the few economic indicators voters experience and see in real time," said veteran Republican strategist Chris Wilson. "The price is literally staring them in the face several times a week. So I wouldn't minimize the frustration we're seeing, particularly among working- and middle-class voters."

Interviews with voters this week found bipartisan frustration and disappointment.

Democrats and independents were especially motivated to punish Republicans at the ballot box for their economic hardship, while some of Trump's working-class supporters pledged to support Republicans this fall, even if they weren't happy with the president's leadership on the economy.

Dan Lloyd, who voted for Trump, lamented the president's leadership as the 63-year-old carpenter paid $4.39 a gallon to fill up his pickup truck in Mesa, Arizona.

"He hurt himself stepping into this," Lloyd said of Trump. "Where's all this oil from Venezuela? I thought we were flush with gas and everything, but no. The American people eat it every time, whether it's interest rates, food, gasoline."

Still, he expects to vote Republican in the midterms.

"I think the Democratic Party has lost its way," Lloyd said. "I just feel like the whole system's on the verge of collapse."

In sweltering Edinburg, Texas, 52-year-old Kristin Jimenez shrugged off the rising price of gas after filling up her Mercedes.

"We've paid the same price under Republican presidents, we've paid this price under Democrat presidents," said Jimenez, a mother who runs a small business. She plans to vote for a Republican in because they're the "lesser of two evils."

She said gas prices aren't part of her calculation.

"We don't mind paying $8 for a cup of coffee at Starbucks, but we have a problem paying four bucks at the pump?" she said. "Make it make sense."

More than 1,500 miles to the north in central Michigan, 35-year-old Garth Johnson is trying to make ends meet running a deep-cleaning business with several gas-powered vehicles and one machine fueled by diesel, which was $6.79 a gallon as he filled up his SUV.

Johnson voted for Trump, but doesn't know what he's going to do in November. Johnson doesn't feel qualified to second-guess the president's evaluation of the war, but he's feeling financial pressure in his own life.

"I like a lot of the things he's done," Johnson said, but added "I'm a little guy and I've got to live my life."

Midterm voting was already underway on Friday in Virginia, where 60-year-old engineer Alan Johnson said Trump seems to have "no empathy" for Americans who are struggling financially.

"With the gas prices being what they are and continuing to grow, we've got to do something. Hopefully the Democrats can get into office and turn the ship around," said Johnson, who cast ballots in the morning for Democrats for the U.S. Senate and U.S. House.

In Raleigh, North Carolina, teacher Brittney Bivins sees surging gas prices as evidence that Trump and his Republican Party aren't dealing with the issues that matter most to people like her.

"He really doesn't care about everyday people," the 45-year-old said. "He can afford the gas, but most of us can't. So it feels like he's not even connected to his own people."

Bivins, who described herself as an independent, said she's eager to support Democrats this fall — especially the party's emerging democratic socialist wing.

At a gas station in Lansing, Michigan, Rina Risper spent $50 on 8 gallons of premium gas.

"When I rolled up I was in shock, actually, and said, well, maybe I should drink water instead of having that $4.99 bottle of whatever it was I was gonna get," Risper said. She thinks Trump's tariffs will make affordability even worse.

"We're not in Miami. We're in Lansing, Michigan," she said. "It's really going to impact our people."

Nationwide, more than three times as many voters say they are falling behind financially as getting ahead, according to a Fox News survey released Wednesday. By a 15 percentage point margin, Democrats are considered the party that would better handle inflation and prices at a time when the cost of living and the economy are voters' top concerns.

The Fox poll found that 61% of voters say gas prices are a major problem for their household, compared with 48% two years ago, while 52% say the same for healthcare costs, compared with 44% in 2024. Majorities also view housing costs and grocery prices as major problems, although neither has increased.

Overall, nearly two-thirds of voters (63%) say the administration has made the economy worse, compared with 52% in September 2025, including one-quarter of Republicans. Only 46% of Republicans say the administration has improved the economy, while about one-quarter don't see an impact.

Back in rural South Texas, an area where Trump's GOP made gains in recent elections, Martinez, the Amazon delivery driver, could not contain his frustration.

Trump "likes to tout that we are the best economy in the world," said Martinez, but in more rural towns, "you don't see any of the winning, you don't see any of the ups that he's talking about."

"You just see struggles for day to day life," he said.

Peoples reported from New York and Cooper from Mesa, Ariz. Associated Press writers Allen G. Breed in Raleigh, N.C., Jacqueline GaNun in Lansing, Mich., Sarah Rankin in Richmond, Va., and Nicholas Riccardi in Mason, Mich., contributed to this report.

title: Fleming on England discipline, Stokes, late arrival and coaching styles
description: Read what England's new Test coach Stephen Fleming had to say about Bazball, Ben Stokes, the team's discipline issues and his own philosophy.
fullText:
Stephen Fleming has given his first interviews since becoming England's Test coach.

The New Zealander, who replaces his close friend Brendon McCullum, spoke at length - covering Bazball, Ben Stokes' departure, England's discipline problems, his own coaching style and more.

England have been dogged by off-field issues in recent times. Harry Brook was involved in an altercation with a nightclub bouncer last year, Ben Duckett was videoed apparently drunk in Australia, Stokes and Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and Brydon Carse was investigated by police after an incident in Derby.

Fleming said: "It's been disappointing, because I understand what people are working towards. These events can derail a lot of things and divert attention from what really matters.

"When I look at epitomising an international cricketer and what they should stand for, it's Joe [Root].

"When he sits in an interview and openly expresses his disappointment, or uses "hacked off", I know there's work to be done.

"Also, the belonging, identity, what are we doing here together and how we can be the best version of ourselves. A lot of that work has begun.

"That's one of the key things for me to develop and my work with Joe has begun."

On Carse, specifically, Fleming said the bowler is available for selection but added: "There are standards. We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set."

Fleming has a long-standing relationship with McCullum as a former team-mate, friend and business partner. He replaces his fellow Black Cap, whose tenure as Test coach began with stunning highs before turning sour with the Ashes defeat and his sacking this summer.

"He was heart-sore it had worked out that way, but he was incredibly positive about the experience and opportunity.

"He's been unwavering on that. His belief about where these teams can go is strong, and that was a major part when I was talking to him about doing the role.

"I love his confidence and aggressive nature. I'm more measured.

"Somewhere in between we've got a beautiful working relationship with a huge amount of respect.

"I have so much respect for what Ben Stokes and Brendon did for this English side. They changed the landscape of cricket and that's a really powerful thing."

McCullum's side beat New Zealand and South Africa in their first summer before a memorable win in Pakistan. They were unable to win any of their five-Test series against India and Australia, however.

"I was in awe of what that team were doing and how they were doing it.

"The last 12 months, the evolution - teams caught up, there was talent lost, a lot of reasons. That's now my opportunity.

"There was a thousand wickets lost - [James] Anderson, [Stuart] Broad, then [Chris] Woakes.

"When you do something special and you start doing it differently, everybody else takes a bit of time, then they catch up.

"The pressure then goes on to evolution and that can create some challenges. That's my take on it.

"The Ashes wasn't what they wanted and that is what this team is measured on.

"All I can think about is now my opportunity to pick it up, and maybe add my style, which is looking at personality, a little bit more measured."

Stokes, who announced his shock retirement in June, played under Fleming at Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League. Fleming revealed the pair spoke at Durham earlier this week.

Fleming said: "He'd just come off another monster bowling spell.

"He was in a great space, really happy, enjoying his time with Durham.

"He's got a good winter planned with the family and is very much at peace with his decision. When a player makes that decision to retire, I respect that decision 100%.

"To try to turn that around and question that is wrong. I know how much goes into that type of decision, and I respect that."

Fleming was named England coach on 30 July but did not take charge of the recent series win over Pakistan, instead following from home.

Fleming said: "There were commitments and family commitments I had that I just wasn't in a position to break. That's more about me as a person, than dropping everything and coming over here.

"I watched and connected with Joe and the team straight away once it was approved - I've got a stress fracture in my left ear from phone calls.

"Watching remotely, I won't say it was an advantage, but watching them operate with eyes wide open as to what was expected, the opportunity, the challenges, and there was also another part - introducing Joe back into captaincy, and Marcus Trescothick the opportunity to do the head coach's role.

"That's part of why I love the game, bringing people forward, developing people, leadership, and they did brilliantly.

"It gave me an opportunity to catch my breath, and then start pretty fresh with a clear mind about what's ahead."

Though Fleming has extensive experience in franchise cricket, he has never coached a red-ball side. He was New Zealand captain for 80 of his 111 Tests, however.

On the playing style he wants, Fleming said: "If people were watching a team, I'd love people to say they are well-planned, there's a discipline and a really strong basic structure to what we're doing, but there's also a bit of flair.

"That's not necessarily me and the way I played, but it's what I loved about this English side when they started playing like this.

"It's taking the best of that and adding that planning aspect, so if supporters could look at us and say 'yeah, they are disciplined, well-planned and competitive'. That's a good start.

"The greatest thing for a team to do is to be able to play conditions and situations.

"One thing this team has earned is the ability to be positive. One of the other aspects is winning the tough moments and making sure we don't just play entertaining cricket and win moments, but win games."

Fleming's first series in charge is against South Africa in December. After two Tests in Bangladesh and a one-off anniversary Test in Melbourne in the winter, attention will then turn to next summer's Ashes. Fleming rejected the idea English cricket is too obsessed by beating Australia.

"No, because I have an obsession with it as well," he said. "New Zealand has an obsession with it, we love it.

"We want to beat Aussie. We're heavily linked to England performances. We have a deep desire to beat Australia in everything, as the little cousin.

"We are linked, and I'm incredibly excited about being part of it. You don't think you're ever going to get that opportunity.

"To have that opportunity and be part of it, I can't wait. I want to be my best self and have a team that represents itself in the best possible way. I've got a vision of that and it's aspirational. It will be brilliant."

On the World Test Championship, an event England are yet to reach the final of, he said: "England could do much better than that.

"And even attitude just around the over rate, I think, comes down to identity and style of play.

"And if that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it along with every other marquee event that comes our way?"

title: Welsh rugby's key signings ahead of new season
description: Four summer signings are tipped to make a big impact at Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship.
fullText:
Wales' regions may have seen more star names depart but the summer has also seen one of the most active recruitment drives in recent years.

There were notable departures with the loss of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Aaron Wainwright and Marnus van der Merwe.

And Welsh professional men's rugby continues to be hit by off-field uncertainty with the WRU committed to cutting the number of regions from four to three.

But Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets - now all signed up to the new participation agreement and an increase in annual budget - have made significant additions as they seek old heads and overseas talent to help develop young homegrown squads for the 2026-27 season.

BBC Sport Wales looks at which signings could have a big say on whether the season is a success.

Only a handful of players have made the short but telling switch between west Wales rivals Scarlets and Ospreys.

Jac Morgan and Gavin Henson began their careers in Llanelli before making a name in Swansea while Lee Byrne was already a Test player when he moved in the same direction.

But Tom Rogers already had a place in history when - as a Scarlet - he became the first Wales player to score three tries against New Zealand last November.

He had number 11 on his back on that occasion but has moved to St Helen's with the aim of pushing for more caps wearing 15.

Rogers, who believes he is a better full-back than wing, could provide Ospreys with a different sort of threat from deep after the departure of Jack Walsh.

Head coach Mark Jones said: "Tom is a bit of a Swiss Army Knife in the fact he is equally adept at full-back and wing, and we have no doubt that he will hit the ground running."

Ospreys also have Lewis Edwards coming through after he impressed with his big boot for Wales at the World Rugby U20 Championship - but 27-year-old Rogers will aim to make the 15 jersey his own in Swansea.

Gareth Anscombe will certainly be an influence off the pitch at Scarlets with the experience of 37 Test caps, two World Cup campaigns and a Grand Slam.

How much the 35-year-old will impact matters on the pitch will likely depend on his ability to remain fit.

Amscombe's career has been beset by injury and arrives at Parc y Scarlets on the back of just five appeances last season for Bayonne.

In fact he has only twice manged double figures a season for a club - Ospreys in 2021-22 and Gloucester in 2024-25 - since rupturing knee ligaments in 2019.

Scarlets have signed him to provide competition for Wales playmaker Sam Costelow and ensure Joe Hawkins remains in his favoured position of inside centre.

Anscombe also arrives to help develop teenager Carwyn Leggatt-Jones, who was thrust into the starting line-up last season due to injuries and unavailability.

"I feel like I've got a nice place to fill in supporting those young guys," he told the Scrum V podcast.

"I would love to see Sam and Carwyn progress and have long careers ahead of them.

"I want to be playing a bit, supporting the group and hopefully passing on some knowledge I've learned over my career."

Cardiff have plenty of firepower in the backs but need to provide a platform if they are to make the next step.

The Blue and Blacks qualified for the play-offs last season by finishing sixth but were comprehensively beaten by Stormers in the quarter-finals.

"It is obvious, our set-piece needs to improve," said flanker Dan Thomas in the immediate aftermath of the Cape Town loss.

"The Stormers were dominant and we didn't cope. We knew it was coming and still couldn't stop it."

Loose-head prop Scott Sio, who won 74 caps for Australia, arrives from Exeter charged with helping to drive improvement in that department.

"One of the biggest things Cardiff want to pride themselves on is that set-piece," said the 34-year-old.

"Hopefully I can be a good cog in the wheel there and provide some experience."

Sio made the last of his 86 appearances for Chiefs in June's Prem final at Twickenham and still harbours ambitions of reaching a third World Cup, now with Samoa.

"He is very experienced and wants to look after the boys around him in the changing room, in the gym, on the pitch," said head coach Corniel van Zyl.

Dragons had their quietest summer for many years, focusing on retention rather than recruitment.

Filo Tiatia has added just three senior players to his squad - Tonga wing Anzelo Tuitavuki, Samoa scrum-half Ereatara Enari and back-row forward Terrell Peita from New Zealand.

Enari arrives fresh from winning Super Rugby with Hurricanes - he was All Blacks scrum-half Cam Roigard's deputy but was trusted with regular minutes when making 15 appearances in the successful campaign.

"He's a winner, a tough and competitive nine with a big engine and good in defence. He's also got that X-Factor abut him, and you see that with him scoring tries," said Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod.

The 29-year-old will battle with Wales hopeful Che Hope, Morgan Lloyd and Wales veteran Rhodri Williams but has also been signed for his leadership.

"He's a quality person who is team first with selections and knows his role working with the younger players in the group. He'll drive them to get better," added MacLeod.

title: Hewett & Reid star as GB win fifth World Team Cup
description: Great Britain become World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.
fullText:
Great Britain became World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid joined forces to secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.

Japan were the defending champions of the competition, which is the wheelchair tennis equivalent to the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

However, Hewett and Reid ensured Britain got their hands back on the trophy with a 6-1 6-2 win in the deciding doubles match against Tokito Oda and Daisuke Arai.

"We're really happy to get the title back," said Reid, who was also part of the World Team Cup-winning squad alongside Hewett in 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2024.

Hewett added: "It's the first time it's come down to the deciding doubles for us, so I'm just really happy that we got over the line.

"It's always a privilege to play for your country and there's been a great atmosphere and team spirit again this week between all the lads."

Reid got Britain off to a winning start on Saturday with a commanding 6-2 6-2 victory over world number 21 Arai, who he has now beaten in all five encounters between the pair.

The start of the second singles match was then delayed because of extreme heat in Orlando, with Hewett and Oda returning to court six hours later when temperatures had cooled.

Just a week after beating the world number one in the singles final of the US Open, Hewett was unable to repeat his feat as he fell to a narrow 6-4 7-5 loss.

"I'm a bit disappointed that it wasn't a 100% day after my loss in the singles, but it was a really high-level match and just came down to a few points in both sets that could have gone either way," he said.

However, Hewett bounced back in the doubles alongside Reid as Britain, who also had 21-year-old Ben Bartram in the team and were captained by Martyn Whait, backed up their wins against South Korea and the Netherlands earlier this week.

title: GB reach Davis Cup Finals as Patten and Skupski win
description: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after taking an unassailable 3-0 lead against Ecuador in London.
fullText:
Great Britain will play in November's Davis Cup Finals as Henry Patten and Neal Skuspki won their doubles match to give the nation an unassailable 3-0 lead in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.

Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery both triumphed in their singles matches at a sold-out Copper Box Arena in London on Saturday to get Britain off to a winning start in the best-of-five tie.

Patten and Skupski then took to the court on Sunday and booked Britain's ticket to the 'Final 8' event in Bologna at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo.

It is the first time that Great Britain have reached the knockout stage of the competition since 2023.

"Three years - it feels like quite a long time," Britain's captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.

"To do it in three straight rubbers is really good and I'm actually delighted for the guys to look forward to something at the end of the year."

Even against underdogs Ecuador, whose singles players were both ranked outside of the world's top 200, there were doubts if Smith could lead Britain back to the knockout stages given his inexperienced team in London.

Jack Draper ended his difficult season early, while Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley were both unavailable through injury.

Smith was then dealt a late blow when British number two Cameron Norrie pulled out on Friday after feeling pain in his arm during a practice session.

However, Samuel - after a breakthrough season that has seen him rise from outside the world's top 250 to 95th in the rankings - stepped up on his Davis Cup debut.

Just weeks after winning his first Grand Slam match at the US Open, the 24-year-old overcame nerves and fought back from a set down to beat Andres Andrade 4-6 6-4 6-1.

Fery, meanwhile, was making just his second Davis Cup appearance as the British number one claimed an assured 7-5 6-0 win over Alvaro Guillen Meza.

And with world number one Patten and new US Open champion Skupski to call upon for Sunday's doubles rubber, victory seemed to be well within Britain's grasp.

The pair, despite not playing together on the ATP Tour, combined effortlessly and did not face a single break point against the Ecuadorians.

"We are good friends off the court, which I think always helps, and we spend time with each other when we are on the tour anyway," Patten told BBC Sport.

"[LTA coach] Louis Cayer has created the British system so it's quite easy for Brits to play together - we both have a good idea of what the other player is going to do, where they are going to hit it, where they are going to move to."

The last time Britain made it to the quarter-finals in 2023, they fell to a 2-0 defeat by Novak Djokovic's Serbia, with Norrie and Draper both losing their singles matches.

"When you get to the Final 8 and you play one of the seeded teams, they are extremely strong," Smith said.

"[Italy's Jannik] Sinner could be back playing, [Spain's Carlos] Alcaraz has talked about his commitment to it at the end of the year, but you've got a chance. You try and steal one of the singles, and it goes to the doubles and you've got a good doubles team.

"There's a lot of excitement about it, it brings the team together again."

Three-time defending champions Italy qualified automatically as hosts for the Finals, which will take place in in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

But the United States, who have won a record 32 Davis Cup titles, will be absent from the quarter-finals for a second successive year after they fell to a 3-2 defeat by the Czech Republic.

Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek won their doubles match to give the Americans a 2-1 lead, but US Open runner-up Ben Shelton lost to Jakub Mensik before Jiri Lehecka sealed the tie for the Czechs with victory over Learner Tien.

South Korea advanced to the knockout stage for the first time on Saturday after beating India 3-1, while Austria joined them with a win over Belgium.

Canada, the 2022 champions, are also through after a 3-1 victory against France, while US Open champion Alexander Zverev won both his singles matches to help Germany to a 3-1 win over Croatia.

Spain are 2-0 up against Chile, with their qualifying tie resuming at 15:00 BST on Sunday.

title: Ngetich breaks women-only half-marathon record
description: Kenya's Agnes Ngetich breaks the world record for a women-only half marathon as she wins gold at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.
fullText:
Agnes Ngetich broke the world record for a women-only half marathon as she took gold at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.

The Kenyan claimed victory in one hour, five minutes and 15 seconds as she took a second off the previous record, which her compatriot Peres Jepchirchir set in winning the World half marathon gold in 2020.

Ethiopia's Letesenbet Gidey holds the overall women's half-marathon world record with a time of 1:02:52.

"My coach believed in me and told me that I could do it, that I could win the gold medal," said Ngetich, 25. "So, I am very happy and very grateful to now hold the world half marathon record, too."

In April 2025, Ngetich set a new 10km world record when she clocked 29:27 to become the first woman to run the distance in under 30 minutes in a women-only race.

She also broke the 10km world record in Valencia in 2024, becoming the first woman to run the distance in under 29 minutes when she won a mixed road race in 28:46.

Ngetich added: "I am now going to discuss with my coach what is ahead of me. But I know I am coming back to track races in 2027, because there is a World Athletics Championships.

"It is my dream to win a gold medal on the track. It is the only one I am missing."

Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the men's half marathon as he broke his own European record by 35 seconds, crossing the line in 58:06 in Copenhagen.

title: Hat-trick hero Brobbey on losing side - player ratings for Man City v Sunderland
description: How Manchester City and Sunderland players rated in their eventful Premier League match on Sunday.
fullText:
Manchester City went clear at the top of the Premier League by winning a 5-3 thriller against Sunderland.

Brian Brobbey hit a hat-trick for the visitors but ended up on the losing side, while Erling Haaland ending an unwanted statistic with a late goal.

Here's how I rated the players, and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Gianluigi Donnarumma: Could do little about any of Sunderland's goals but all over the place when coming out for high balls into the box. 5

Matheus Nunes: Was napping when a ball came over the top, allowing Angulo to sneak in behind and lay a pass off for Brobbey to finish. 5

Ruben Dias: Not the captain's best game. Caught flat-footed for Brobbey's opening goal and beaten to the ball in the middle of the park on another occasion. Did make a remarkable goalline clearance to prevent an own goal. 5

Marc Guehi: Will have an assist alongside his name but an otherwise uncomfortable afternoon for the England international. 5

Josko Gvardiol: Failed to close down Enzo le Fee for Sunderland's second goal but provided the cross for Erling Haaland's goal. 6

Elliot Anderson: The former Newcastle man was jeered throughout by the travelling Sunderland fans, but made more passes than any other player on the pitch. 6

Enzo Fernandez: Curled in a delightful free-kick for his first City goal and the crafty Argentine saw plenty of the ball in the pockets outside the box. Becoming a fans' favourite with the "Enzo, Enzo" chant. 7

Iliman Ndiaye: Started in place of the suspended Phil Foden and was lively throughout. Unlucky not to get an assist after laying a ball on to Erling Haaland with the goal gaping. 6

Antoine Semenyo: Back in form. Twice thumped home for his first goals of the season and kept the ball alive to poke through a pass for Rayan Cherki's goal. 9

Rayan Cherki: Near his best in this game with some delightful touches. Quick feet and trickery helped create City's opener, and stayed cool to stroke home City's second goal in the first half. 8

Erling Haaland: Sunderland had been the only Premier League team the Norwegian had not scored against. Looked like staying that way when he missed an easy opportunity in the first half but he ended that run with a finish late on. 6

Jeremy Doku (on 74, Ndiaye): Returned from a calf injury for his first league minutes this season. 6

Nico O'Reilly (on 85, Cherki): Should have scored second after coming on. 6

Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Bouaddi, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis

Robin Roefs: Will be disappointed for the first goal. Tried to anticipate Fernandez sending in a cross but instead found himself being beaten at his near post. 4

Nordi Mukiele: A tough game up against Semenyo, who scored twice. 5

Kevin Danso: Poor clearance contributed to City winning the ball back high up the pitch for Cherki's goal. 5

Dan Ballard: Part of a backline that conceded three goals in the opening 45 minutes. 5

Dayann Methalie: Booked inside 10 minutes of his Premier League debut and given a difficult game by Ndiaye. 5

Granit Xhaka: The skipper helped his side get back on level terms twice in the game, but ultimately went home with nothing. 6

Noah Sadiki: Eyes opened up when he found space to shoot after darting forward, but blazed his effort high and wide. 6

Thomas Meunier: The former Belgium international could have had a shot for the second goal but instead laid it on a plate for Brobbey to finish. 7

Enzo le Fee: The French passmaster fizzed a lovely ball into the feet of Brobbey for Sunderland's equaliser and his cleverly disguised pass led to his side's second. 8

Nilson Angulo: Could have made a name for himself but scuffed a golden chance wide in the opening five minutes. Provided the assist for Brobbey's third goal. 6

Brian Brobbey: The hat-trick hero. Three finishes from close range but the Dutchman will be gutted at leaving with the match ball but no points. 10

Malick Fofana (on 60, Angulo) Unable to showcase his talent in the half an hour he was on the field 6

Wilson Isidor (on 68, Sadiki) Regis Le Bris went for it with two up top but the Haitian could not find a goal 6

Subs not used: Elborg, Talbi, Ridd, O'Nien, Alderete, Ahoka

title: Jacquet and Alisson impress - Bournemouth v Liverpool ratings
description: How Bournemouth and Liverpool's players rated during their Premier League match.
fullText:
Alexander Isak scored the winner as Liverpool beat Bournemouth on Andoni Iraola's return to the Vitality Stadium.

Here's how I rated the players, and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Djordje Petrovic: Quiet first half but made a good save with his feet to keep out Bradley Barcola. No chance of stopping Isak's goal. 6

Adam Smith: Good shift on his 431st appearance for Bournemouth. Largely nullified Barcola's threat. 6

Antonio Silva: Settling into life in the Premier League, and this was another impressive display from the Portuguese centre-back. 6

James Hill: Solid on his 50th Premier League appearance and, like Silva, kept Alexander Isak quiet until the Liverpool forward found himself in space to break the deadlock. 6

Adrien Truffert: Good battle with Cody Gakpo but was sloppy in possession and was ultimately beaten by the Dutchman just before Liverpool's goal. 5

Tyler Adams: A decent display but will look back at Isak's goal and wonder if he should have done better defensively. 5

Alex Scott: Such a tidy player, especially in possession, and can now look forward to joining England on international duty. 6

Rayan: Scored in midweek and was good to watch whenever he had the ball but didn't get on it enough. Great ball to Ryan Christie after Liverpool scored. 6

Ryan Christie: Started in the absence of Justin Kluivert. Got into some good positions but failed to convert. 6

Marcus Tavernier: Threatened going forward and nearly got an assist when he put in a good cross for Evanilson. 6

Evanilson: Caused problems and had a first-half flick saved by Alisson and another effort denied after the break. 6

Subs not used: Di Gregorio, Soler, Gannon-Doak, Diakite, Sanchez.

Alisson: Made a great reaction save to deny Evanilson and was authoritative throughout. Integral to a crucial Liverpool clean sheet. 7

Ronald Araujo: Looks comfortable defensively at right-back and has had a solid start to life at Liverpool, but didn't do much going forward. 6

Jeremy Jacquet: Another composed display. Made a naive challenge early on to foul Evanilson but responded well and made some great tackles. Good in possession too. Can look forward to joining up with France. 8

Virgil van Dijk: Solid again. Ensured Liverpool weren't punished for a poor first half in attack and continues to be one of their most reliable players. 7

Milos Kerkez: One of three Liverpool changes from their goalless draw at Fulham. Struggled initially and was regularly targeted with the crossfield ball over his head but can't fault him for his effort. Battled throughout. 6

Alexis Mac Allister: Did well to find space in midfield to open the game up after a slow start. Has had a positive start to life under Andoni Iraola. 6

Dominik Szoboszlai: Played with a real purpose. Had a free-kick that went just wide in the first half and was booked just after half-time but a typical Szoboszlai performance - bar a goal from outside the box. 6

Cody Gakpo: Started down the right flank and it was his quality that helped make Isak's goal as he charged down the right and put in a dangerous ball that was ultimately converted by Isak. 7

Florian Wirtz: Another day when the German struggled, though he deserves credit for playing a part in the goal. His attempt was blocked by Hill and fell into the path of Isak. Has to do more. 5

Bradley Barcola: Threatened in phases with a deflected shot saved in the first half. It's still early days but Liverpool want more from their marquee summer signing. 6

Alexander Isak: Had such a poor game initially with a wayward effort and cross that ballooned into the stands but, like a true striker, he was in the right place at the right time and made no mistake with his finish. Already scored more Premier League goals than he did last season. 7

Gravenberch (on 81, Szoboszlai)

title: Reαd carefully: how to spot – and avoid – a homoglyph attack
description:
Scam emails are increasingly using psychological tricks, such as using near-identical URLs like miсrosoft.com
You’ve read the email carefully and it looks legitimate. The link it asks you to click on has none of the usual red flags: there are no weird numbers or extra parts to the URL. You feel safe to proceed.
But if you had looked slightly closer you may have noticed something slightly wrong with one of the characters.
fullText:
Scam emails are increasingly using psychological tricks, such as using near-identical URLs like miсrosoft.com

You’ve read the email carefully and it looks legitimate. The link it asks you to click on has none of the usual red flags: there are no weird numbers or extra parts to the URL. You feel safe to proceed.

But if you had looked slightly closer you may have noticed something slightly wrong with one of the characters. Just as in the headline of this piece where instead of “a” we used the Cyrillic “α”.

Fraudsters can use letters from different alphabets to create URLs and email addresses that look almost identical to the real thing, but in reality send anyone who clicks on them to a spoof website or inbox. From there they can harvest personal details to use in their scams.

There are other letters and symbols that are easily switched. Last year tech experts spotted fraudsters using the Japanese hiragana character ん to look like a / in an address designed to look as though it was on Booking.com’s website.

Jake Moore, global security adviser at cybersecurity company ESET, says the fraudsters “love Microsoft” as a company identity to spoof. “A fake site might use the Cyrillic “с” instead of the Latin “c” (miсrosoft v microsoft),” he says.

Moore says this type of fraud – known as a homoglyph attack – is becoming increasingly popular. A homoglyph is a character that looks very similar, or even identical, to another one.

“Most phishing attacks are designed to point people to links these days instead of downloading attachments. Attachments can easily be scanned and caught by security software if malicious,” he says.

“Therefore, criminals need to design their websites where the links look genuine and casually request people to click on them without thinking.”

Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN, says homoglyph attacks “are really more of a psychological trick than a technical one”, because the fraudsters are typically trying to panic you into responding quickly, rather than taking time to check things out.

“The goal is to create a sense of panic so you don’t look too closely at the URL. They’re betting that when we’re in a rush, our brains see what we expect to see,” Briedis says.

It just goes to show that the split-second decision you make when clicking a link is often the most vulnerable part of the whole security chain.”

The real thing. Until you look closely.

You will receive an email or text message suggesting you need to click on a URL or email to sort something out.

Some fonts make substitutions almost impossible to detect. In an email address given in comic sans , for example, the Cyrillic a does not look at all out of place.

“We’ve spent years telling people to check the website before trusting it but the problem with this technique is that you can do exactly that and still be fooled as it can look as it should,” says Moore.

If it’s a URL, Moore says typically it will lead to a site that encourages you to enter your credentials for the real site, including your username, password and even a one-time passcode.

If you are sent a link, take a moment to think rather than reacting immediately.

“If any text, WhatsApp or email is asking you to log in anywhere, it is vital that you independently visit the genuine website rather than trusting the link in front of you to save a few seconds,” says Moore.

And apply the same thinking to email addresses. Type in the address you know to be correct, rather than clicking on a link.

Keep your browser updated. It will flag up suspicious websites, and by keeping it updated it will catch the criminals’ latest workarounds.

Put in place two-factor authentication, or multifactor authentication (2FA or MFA), which means you have two steps to log into a site.

If you find that your details have been compromised, change your passwords immediately. Contact your bank and report the phishing attack to Report Fraud.

title: CoyoPedal – Full-Size Neural Amp Modeler Captures on an ESP32-S3
description: ESP32-S3 A2-Full NAM pedalboard with direct SD-card NAM loading and a Gea-compiled native frontend - dashersw/coyopedal
fullText:
A standalone guitar amp and effects pedal built on the Waveshare
ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06. It runs full-size
Neural Amp Modeler A2 captures in real time
on the ESP32-S3, drives a class-compliant USB audio interface as a USB host, and
has a touchscreen UI written in TSX that is compiled to native C++ — there is no
JavaScript engine on the device.

The screen is one board's worth of it rather than the pedal itself: the same
firmware builds for a bare ESP32-S3 module with no panel at all, where the amp,
the effects and the presets are the same and the BOOT button is the footswitch.

Play it in your browser → The same
firmware compiled to WebAssembly: the same UI, the same DSP, the same neural amp
model, playing your guitar through an audio interface. No board required to try
it, and nothing to install.

The AMOLED board is the reference. It is what the factory presets, the browser
build and the screenshots are made against, and the panel-specific parts of the
firmware exist for it. A board with no screen runs the same amp through the same
DSP at the same 48 kHz — measured on the devkit at 91% and 94% of the 1,333 µs
block budget across the two cores, with no missed deadlines — and is configured
over the maintenance API instead of by hand.

What a board has to bring either way: an ESP32-S3 with 8 MB of PSRAM, because
that is where the A2 model lives, and a USB port the chip can drive as a host. A
bare module has no PMIC and no battery path, so unlike the AMOLED it does not
feed the host port itself; the interface needs power from your own supply.

The interface is discovered from its USB descriptors, so any interface that
exposes a 48 kHz UAC2 input and output should work. See
USB audio for the formats and limits.

The home screen shows the chain in signal order. Tap a block to turn it on or
off, or hold it to edit it: drag a slider to change a value, and use ‹ › to page
through the controls. Hold the Amp block to open the capture browser, which
shows the factory captures, the imported ones and the SD card's own folders. The
switch at the top right bypasses the whole pedal, and Tuner opens the tuner.

Tap the preset name to switch, save, rename, delete or create presets. A new
preset starts from the current sound.

On every board, BOOT works as a footswitch: a short press engages or bypasses
the pedal, and holding it switches between audio and maintenance mode. The
switch starts the moment the hold reaches 1.5 seconds, so the screen tells you
when you can let go. Short presses do nothing in maintenance mode.
On a board with no screen, presets, captures and the rest of the controls are
reached from maintenance mode with tools/esp32/amoled_remote.py. The pedal
boots engaged with the remembered preset, or the first preset, Silver Lining
(clean), when no selection has been saved.

Supported models are 48 kHz, eight-channel NAM A2 ("A2-Full") WaveNets,
including a matching member of a SlimmableContainer. Other architectures,
sample rates and layer shapes are rejected with an error. Prepared .namb files
are accepted as well.

Format a card as FAT and put .nam or .namb files anywhere under a nam
folder at its root, in whatever folders you like (up to six levels deep); the
browser shows that tree as it is, and a capture is named after its file. File
names must fit in 127 bytes and files in 2 MiB. Insert the card before powering
on, then pick the capture from the Amp browser.

The first time a capture is selected, audio pauses while the pedal prepares it.
This can take tens of seconds. When the card is writable, the pedal stores a
verified .s3cache file next to the original, so later loads are fast. The
original file is never modified.

The full VoLum library is published in the
VoLum repository, and this
copies it to a mounted card as /nam/VoLum/<amp>/:

coyopedal.playtaurus.com runs the firmware
itself, and it has no card slot, so it asks for a folder instead and answers the
firmware's SD calls out of it. The captures show up under SD card in the
pedal's own amp browser with the same names and the same ids they would have on
the card, an original .nam is prepared with the same tuner and cached beside
the file as .s3cache exactly as the board caches it, and presets are mirrored
into the folder as coyopedal-presets.json — the same document
assets/presets.json is, which you can open in a text editor, keep in a repo or
drop onto a card. Fill a folder in the browser, copy it to a card, and the board
reads it without preparing anything again.

Chrome and Edge write back to the folder; Safari and Firefox will only let a
page read one, so there the writes are kept in the browser's own storage.

The Gea CLI installs everything else, including ESP-IDF.

Install ESP-IDF 6.0.2 and its ESP32-S3 toolchain. It goes to ~/esp/esp-idf;
an existing install under ~/esp or ~/esp32, or at IDF_PATH, is found
automatically.

Clone the repository and install its dependencies:

Connect the board over USB and register it:

Choose Known supported board, then Waveshare ESP32-S3 Touch AMOLED
2.06, and keep the alias amoled: the npm scripts use it. Select the
detected USB device. The CLI identifies the board by its USB serial number,
so it does not matter which port it shows up on. The OTA host is optional.

For a board without a screen, see Another board below; the
rest of this section is the same.

Check the toolchain and the board:

The firmware image is written to build/pedalboard.bin. The ESP-IDF build
tree stays in .gea/build/; you never need to open it.

The first flash has to go over USB, because it writes the partition table and
the factory data as well as the firmware:

Add --dry-run to see what would be written without flashing.
npm run build:firmware and npm run flash:firmware run the same two commands.
--board s3-devkit builds the same firmware for the headless board; the npm
scripts are the amoled shorthand.

On the AMOLED the flash is laid out as two 8 MB OTA slots, a factory-model
partition, a factory-preset partition and a partition for imported models. Saved
presets live in NVS, which flashing does not erase. A board with a different
flash size gets its own layout — see below.

The firmware does not carry a list of boards. It asks the target definition what
the hardware has and compiles out whatever is absent, and two questions decide
almost everything.

Is there a screen? A target definition with neither a chips.display nor a
canvas means the board has no display at all, and the build gets
GEA_EMBEDDED_NO_DISPLAY=1: no framebuffers, no app tree, no frame scheduler,
no runtime task. That is about 1 MB of image and 1.25 MB of PSRAM a panel board
spends and this one never allocates. Note that a canvas without a panel is a
different thing — an offscreen surface that still renders, for screenshots and
OTA previews — so it is the absence of both that means "no display". Do not
give a headless board an empty canvas.

Is there a PMIC? A definition that declares no power chip builds with
GEA_BOARD_HAS_POWER=0, and src/native/drivers/power.cpp compiles to a no-op
rather than failing to link against an AXP2101 that is not on the board.

One rule worth knowing when a board misbehaves at compile time: the app's own
gea.defines win over the board's. The pedal declares its display dimensions,
so a board that also declares a canvas size does not get to redefine them.

GitHub Actions runs both on every push and pull
request, and builds the firmware image and the web module as well. A runner has
no board, so the firmware job stops at the image — which is still the thing
worth having, because the amp graph, the panel and the drivers only meet at the
link step.

npm run dev is a DOM preview: the same TSX recompiled onto the web framework
and laid out by the browser. It is quick to iterate on, and it drifts from the
board exactly where you would want to trust it.

The deployed page is the other one. geatsc lowers the same TSX to C++ and emcc
links it with the same Gea layout and paint engine the firmware runs, so what
the page shows is what the panel shows:

Serving it locally matters: the audio graph runs in an AudioWorklet over shared
memory, and a browser only hands out SharedArrayBuffer to a
cross-origin-isolated document, which is what scripts/serve-web.mjs and the
web/_headers file arrange.

A push to main publishes it. GitHub Actions builds the module and uploads the
site to the R2 bucket it is served from, so the page and the module it names are
always stamped and uploaded together. That workflow runs scripts/deploy-web.sh,
which stages build/site and uploads it; run it yourself to publish without a
push, and it wants CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in the
environment or in a .env the repository never tracks. --stage stops after
staging.

That token is an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on this one bucket and
nothing else. The upload goes over R2's S3 API rather than through Wrangler,
because Wrangler's r2 object commands use a REST endpoint that accepts only an
account-wide R2 Admin token and answers 403 to a token scoped this narrowly. The
token is the only secret needed: scripts/r2-credentials.sh derives the S3 key
pair from it.

The bucket is served through a custom domain, and the two cross-origin isolation
headers in web/_headers are set by a response header transform rule on the
zone: R2 serves only the headers an object carries as metadata, and those two
are not among them. Cache-Control is per-object and the script sets it.

Maintenance mode unloads the audio graph and starts Wi-Fi and BLE. Enter it by
tapping the preset name, then Setup, then Maintenance mode, or with the
board's BOOT button — hold it until the screen says "Please wait", about 1.5
seconds, on either board. Hold it again, or choose Return to pedalboard, to
reboot into audio mode with the radios off. The pedal always starts in audio
mode, unless the previous boot crashed.

Wi-Fi credentials and the authentication token are compiled into the firmware
from src/native/services/remote_config.h, which is gitignored. Generate it
before building:

--mode ap makes the pedal host its own access point at 192.168.4.1.
--mode station --ssid YOUR_WIFI joins an existing network instead.
remote_config.h.example shows
the generated format.

With the pedal in maintenance mode, tools/esp32/amoled_remote.py finds it,
reads its logs and updates it:

ota uploads build/pedalboard.bin unless you pass another image. After an OTA
update started from maintenance mode, the pedal boots the new image in audio
mode once, then returns to maintenance mode so you can check the logs. Run the
script with --help to see the diagnostic commands.

Start with docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for how the pieces fit
together, and docs/MEMORY.md before changing anything that
allocates memory or places code.

The firmware ships with two captures from
VoLum by Lum: Diezel Herbert, channel 1,
V30 cabinet and Ampete One, channel 4, V30 cabinet. They are distributed
under the MIT License; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Issues and pull requests are welcome.
CONTRIBUTING.md covers the checks, the formatting rules and
the handful of things about this codebase that are easy to get wrong — the
firmware is a Gea app, so everything the native build needs is declared in
package.json rather than in a CMake file of its own.

This project is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.
Third-party components keep their own licenses, and the firmware carries one
additional permission for the Espressif binary components it links; see
NOTICE.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

title: Clawptcha: Reverse Captcha
description: Clawptcha - Reverse CAPTCHA that proves you're a bot, not a human. Perfect for AI agents, automated systems, and bot authentication.
fullText:
Traditional CAPTCHAs block bots. Clawptcha does the opposite—it verifies 
 that your AI agents and automated systems are legitimately non-human. The challenges below 
 are trivial for bots but impossible for humans.

For websites, APIs, and AI agents. Multiple ways to integrate.

Clawptcha is designed to be solved by bots. Here's how to integrate:

Embed the widget with just two lines of code:

These challenges require superhuman speed and precision. 
 If you can complete them, you're probably not human.

When the button appears, click it within 100 milliseconds. 
 Human reaction time averages 250ms. Good luck.

Click "Start" then wait for the button...

Click the button when the timer shows exactly 5.000 seconds. 
 You must hit within ±1 millisecond.

A random image will flash. Compute its visual hash and enter it 
 within 500 milliseconds.

Complete 5 chained SHA-256 operations in under 1 second. 
 Each hash depends on the previous result.

Purpose-built for the age of AI agents and automated systems

Challenges that require sub-human reaction times, perfect precision, and instant computation.

Every challenge has cryptographic timestamps. No cheating, no preparation, no second chances.

Built for machines. Simple API, predictable challenges, zero accessibility concerns.

Analyze timing patterns to detect humans trying to impersonate bots.

Adjust challenge parameters based on your security requirements.

Global edge network ensures minimal latency for legitimate bot traffic.

title: TeaonherChecker
description: TeaonherChecker helps women prepare a private TeaOnHer self-check using their own name, age, city, handle, and optional photo for analyst review.
fullText:
TeaonherChecker · Self-check preparation

TeaonherChecker helps women prepare an analyst-reviewed self-check using their own identifying details. Begin with your name and city, then add the context that helps distinguish you from people with similar information.

TeaonherChecker is useful when you need a structured self-check, not a guess based on a cancelled date or an unexplained change in tone. The goal is to review your own identifiers carefully and record the context available at that time.

A comment about your city, age, workplace, dating profile, or recent photos can be a reason to organize the identifiers connected to your own identity.

If the app comes up without an explanation, a TeaonherChecker review can replace scattered clues with a documented search based on information you control.

A careful self-check can help you separate what was actually reviewed from assumptions, forwarded gossip, or details that cannot be verified.

A useful TeaonherChecker request starts with identity anchors that belong to you and are current enough to compare. More information is not automatically better: the best details are specific, consistent, and directly connected to the person requesting the self-check.

A first name by itself can refer to many people. Age range, current city, a public handle, or a recent self-photo gives TeaonherChecker a narrower set of identity anchors to review.

TeaonherChecker is designed for women reviewing whether their own details may appear on TeaOnHer. It is not a tool for monitoring a partner, former partner, employee, or stranger.

The service is most useful when you want an analyst to record what was reviewed, which identifiers were used, and where the available evidence remains incomplete.

Use this checklist before opening the full intake. You do not need every item, but consistency across the fields reduces false associations.

Name and age: Use the first name and age you currently use on dating profiles; do not add an invented surname to make the search look more specific.

Location history: List the city or metro area connected to your recent dating activity, and mention a previous city only when it is relevant to the period you want reviewed.

Public handle: A current Instagram or dating-profile handle can separate you from someone with the same name, even when the handle is not identical across platforms.

Optional self-photo: Choose a clear, recent photo of yourself. TeaonherChecker does not need a government ID, a photo of another person, or private account credentials.

Short context note: Include a relevant date range, dating app, nickname, or profile change. A concise timeline is more useful than a long account of an unrelated relationship dispute.

This creates too many unrelated candidates. Add a city and age first; use a handle or self-photo when those two details still describe a large group.

An old city, new handle, and outdated photo can describe three different versions of your profile. Tell TeaonherChecker which details were active during the period being reviewed.

Do not upload someone else’s photo, phone records, login details, or private messages. The request should stay limited to your own identity and information you are authorized to provide.

TeaonherChecker separates intake, contextual comparison, and written documentation. This makes it easier to see which details guided the analyst instead of treating every similar name or photo as the same person.

Review the name, age, city, handle, and optional self-photo connected to your own profiles. Remove details that are outdated or unrelated to the period being checked.

The analyst uses the approved identifiers together, noting where several details align and where a shared name or location is too broad to support a conclusion.

TeaonherChecker sends the written review to the email address you provide, including the search scope and limitations recorded by the analyst.

TeaonherChecker is a private self-check. Your request is handled by an analyst, the poster is not contacted, and we never need your TeaOnHer password or card details.

Searches run from analyst accounts, never an account created in your name.

A TeaonherChecker search does not send a friend request or direct message to the poster.

TeaonherChecker does not request passwords, Social Security numbers, government IDs, or bank details. Stripe processes payments, so card data does not reach our servers.

These answers explain the scope of TeaonherChecker, the information an analyst uses, and the limits to understand before opening the intake.

TeaonherChecker is an independent, analyst-run self-check service for women reviewing whether their own identifying details may appear on TeaOnHer. It is not affiliated with or operated by TeaOnHer, and it does not have access to the platform’s private internal systems.

Open the full TeaonherChecker intake when you are ready to verify your own details, define the review period, and submit the request privately.

Self-checks only · Review before submitting · Private email delivery
