title: Will the three-week break put more pressure on managers?
description: So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs, but plenty of others will be looking over their shoulders heading into the new, extended international break.
fullText:
Three weeks is a long time in football - especially if you are a manager struggling for results.

So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs - Paul Heckingbottom at Preston North End, Michael Duff at Wycombe Wanderers and Peterborough's Luke Williams.

But plenty of others will be looking over their shoulders heading into the new, extended international break.

That includes the managers of Fulham and Manchester United, who on Sunday meet at Craven Cottage in the final fixture before players jet off around the world with their countries.

It will all be pretty new to Alvaro Arbeloa, appointed as Fulham's manager in the summer after taking charge of just 28 games as Real Madrid boss in the second half of last season.

But with no wins and three defeats in his first four Premier League matches, and speculation of unrest among the squad due to players' social media activity, the pressure is already on Arbeloa.

Likewise Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, especially after the 3-2 EFL Cup exit to Brighton on Wednesday.

It was the first time United had led at home by two goals and lost since they were beaten 3-2 by Tottenham in 1976, half a century ago.

Coming on the back of the 1-0 loss to 10-man Manchester City, and with their only victories this season against Ipswich Town and Sabah, Carrick needs results.

But they are not the only managers who might have cause for concern.

Over the past 10 years, it has been rare for a Premier League manager to be replaced this early in the campaign.

Even more so in the international break.

But could it be different this year? The first break is longer, three weeks rather than two, and comes later.

The September slot used to come at the start of the month when clubs had only played three league fixtures.

In the past 10 years only two managers - Watford's Javi Gracia in 2019 and Nottingham Forest's Nuno Espirito Santo last year - moved on during this break.

What about the October stoppage? Again, only two managers have previously lost their jobs during the same period - Francesco Guidolin at Swansea in 2016, and Xisco Munoz at Watford in 2021.

This suggests clubs do not tend to use an international break to change manager.

It is, though, far more likely to happen in November, with six bosses replaced in the past 10 years.

That does not mean managers are safe, though. The changes simply were not made during the breaks.

In the past 10 campaigns, nine coaches had left their jobs by the time the second international break came along - which is where we are in the number of games.

With no manager to move on yet, could it come in the next three weeks?

Former Stoke, West Brom and Middlesbrough boss Tony Pulis explains when the pressure can build for a football manager.

With the first international break upon us, rumblings around certain clubs that have started the season poorly have surfaced.

In my time, the October/November international breaks, the pause just after the Christmas period, and then early March would be the three sticking points for any manager who was struggling with results.

Why these breaks are used for clubs to make changes is plain to see. The pause in the season gives football clubs the chance to appoint a new manager with time for them to settle into their new role, to take stock of the surroundings, staff and time to prepare for their first game in charge.

After Christmas, usually the first game is an FA Cup match, which again gives the new boss a chance close up to see what they have to work with. First impressions can be a vital starting point, so again the manager has time to prepare and deliver their principles to the lads.

Personally, I've joined quite a few of my clubs midway through seasons, and have left a few clubs going the other way, but I do honestly believe that those international breaks, for the reasons I've given, definitely heighten the chances of struggling managers getting the sack.

I don't see this September break as a flashing light, it is too early in the season, but from then on in, the dates I have mentioned really do come into play.

But this early international break doesn't help any managers.

Whether your team is winning or losing, on both accounts, it's a nightmare. If you're winning you want to keep playing, and yet if you've started badly as a manager you want more time to put it right. Players travelling and the chance of injuries at such an early stage of the season is completely bonkers in my opinion.

While the evidence suggests things have to get pretty bad for a club to change manager early in the season, a few bosses are feeling the heat.

There are ways of losing games of course, but I don't see the trip to Fulham as being 'make or break' for Carrick in the sense of his job.

Carrick says it would be "ridiculous" to think that way - and I agree.

He got enough credit in the bank last season by steering Manchester United into the Champions League to ride out a poor start to the season.

I think the issue is United generate so much debate that a loss at Craven Cottage, which would be United's first since 2009, against a team that has only one point and is bottom of the table, would lead to numerous external inquests - which in turn puts a laser focus on the club when they resume their campaign against Tottenham on 10 October.

It is unclear exactly how much danger Arbeloa is in, but there appears to be some substance to reports of disgruntlement among elements of Fulham's squad early in the campaign.

His significant tactical changes since replacing Marco Silva have left the Cottagers vulnerable at the back, although they produced a more solid display in a goalless draw away to Liverpool last weekend. Silva spent five years at Craven Cottage.

However, owner Shahid Khan has shown a ruthless streak in the past when making managerial changes. Claudio Ranieri lasted just 106 days in charge, while Felix Magath was sacked in September 2014, albeit having been appointed the previous season.

The results go from bad to worse for Tottenham. Having spent about £300m on new talent over the summer the club's owners are getting very little bang for their buck in terms of points (and goals) scored.

But there is no sense whatsoever that Roberto de Zerbi is under pressure despite the club's difficult start - no wins from five games.

The vibes with regards to how the team is starting to play are positive amid a sense that it is only a matter of time before they click.

Of course, for Tottenham, it needs to click sooner rather than later.

Pierre Sage has endured an indifferent start to life at Palace. One league win so far hasn't gone down particularly well internally, nor has the team's leaky defence since the Frenchman's arrival from Lens.

Allowances will be made for the unavailability - for a manner of reasons - of key attacking duo Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta.

The 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in the Europa League on Thursday eased some of the pressure, but a defeat at Leeds this afternoon would come at the worst possible time for Sage.

Nicky Hayen quit Genk to spearhead Burnley's bid to return to the Premier League at the first attempt.

The Clarets started the season as third favourites for promotion, behind West Ham and Wolves, but are winless in their first eight matches.

In his pre-match news conference on Friday, the Belgian faced questions about his future.

Hayen admitted he was under pressure and Saturday's game against fellow slow starters Derby was a must-win fixture.

But a disappointing 1-1 draw, with the Rams scoring a stoppage-time leveller, left Burnley rock-bottom going into the break.

The Burnley board might now be assessing their options.

Derby manager John Eustace, who almost took the club to the play-offs last season, is not safe either with the club in the relegation zone.

A Watford manager can never rest easy in their seat. Alessio Dionisi, appointed in the summer, became their 27th permanent manager in just under 18 years.

Friday's defeat at Bristol City left the Hornets with two wins from their first eight league games under the Italian, who managed Empoli before moving to England.

Sitting in 19th position in the league table, three points above the drop zone, it would not be a surprise if owner Gino Pozzo decided to make an early change.

title: Littler could boycott Dutch events over booing
description: Luke Littler threatens a boycott of playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
fullText:
World champion Luke Littler has threatened to stop playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The referee stopped the match during his narrow win against Nathan Aspinall in the last eight on Saturday to warn the hostile crowd about its behaviour, before play resumed.

It followed Littler also being booed during his win against home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday.

Littler has faced similar treatment in Germany and has stopped playing in European Tour events in the country.

Asked if he was prepared to take a similar stance for Dutch events, the 19-year-old told Online Darts: "100%."

Littler, who is expected to play at the European Championship in Dortmund in October, added: "With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same.

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage and not thanked anyone. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Littler was also booed during a win over Rob Cross at the PDC World Championship in December.

After the match, he said: "I'm not bothered [by the booing]. Really not bothered. You guys pay for tickets and you pay for my prize so thanks for booing me."

Littler seals dramatic final-leg win over Aspinall

title: 'Beat the Aussies' - new England coach Fleming's key aim
description: New Test coach Stephen Fleming says he shares English cricket’s “obsession” with the Ashes and arrives with the goal to “beat the Aussies”.
fullText:
New Test coach Stephen Fleming said he shared English cricket's "obsession" with the Ashes and arrives with the goal to "beat the Aussies".

Fleming was speaking to the media for the first time since being appointed in July and ahead of taking charge for the tour of South Africa in December.

Like his predecessor Brendon McCullum, Fleming is from New Zealand, the "little cousin" to Australia, in his words.

The next Ashes series is in the UK next summer, when England will look to defeat the Australians for the first time since 2015 and avenge a dismal 4-1 defeat down under last winter.

Asked if England are too obsessed with beating Australia, Fleming told BBC Sport: "No, because I have an obsession with it as well. New Zealand has an obsession with it, we love it.

"We want to beat the Aussies. We're heavily linked to England performances. We have a deep desire to beat Australia in everything, as the little cousin. We are linked, and I'm incredibly excited about being part of it.

"You don't think you're ever going to get that opportunity. To have that opportunity and be part of it, I can't wait.

"I want to be my best self and have a team that represents itself in the best possible way. I've got a vision of that and it's aspirational. It will be brilliant."

Listen to the full Stephen Fleming interview on the TMS podcast

Fleming on England discipline, Stokes, late arrival and coaching styles

Fleming, the former New Zealand captain, did not taste victory in any of the 14 Tests he played against Australia.

He succeeds his former team-mate McCullum, who was sacked as Test coach earlier this summer, but remains as boss of the white-ball team. England won only two of McCullum's final 10 Tests in charge, including the hammering in Australia.

Part of the criticism of England under McCullum and former captain Ben Stokes was their inability to adapt to the changing situations of Test cricket, as well as a lack of attention to detail.

Fleming is a great friend of McCullum – the pair are business partners. He described the difference between the two as being: "I'll bet on the favourite and he'll bet on the longest odds possible."

On whether a Test team should have a brand or style, Fleming said: "I don't think so. The greatest thing for a team to do is to be able to play conditions and situations.

"I'd love people to say we are well-planned, there's a discipline and a really strong basic structure to what we're doing, but there's also a bit of flair."

The final months of McCullum's reign were dogged by late-night drinking controversies, which continued after England changed the Test coach.

On Friday, Derbyshire Police announced they had closed an investigation involving England pace bowler Brydon Carse following allegations of an assault last month.

Though Carse will face no action from the police, he now faces an investigation from the Cricket Regulator.

He remains available for England selection, albeit has not been part of a squad in any format since the Derby incident.

"There are standards," said Fleming. "We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set.

"You need to behave in accordance with your position. We're in a very privileged position, and it's understanding that privilege and what goes along with it. It can't be convenient. You can't be when it suits you to do the right things, then when you don't want it to suit you, not.

"You've got to live it every day. If we can create something when you want to live it every day and better, then that's really powerful."

Fleming was at Old Trafford for England's defeat of Sri Lanka in the third T20 on Saturday. Earlier in the week he visited a number of counties and met Stokes during Durham's draw against Worcestershire.

Stokes abruptly retired from international cricket in July and has a previous relationship with Fleming from their time together with Chennai Super Kings at the Indian Premier League.

But Fleming said he had too much "respect" for Stokes' decision to attempt to coax him out of retirement.

"He was in a great space, really happy, enjoying his time with Durham," said Fleming.

"He's got a good winter planned with the family and is very much at peace with his decision. When a player makes that decision to retire, I respect that decision 100%.

"To try to turn that around and question that is wrong. I know how much goes into that type of decision, and I respect that."

Almost two months after being appointed Test coach, Stephen Fleming outlined what the England team may look like under his stewardship.

He was calm, measured and authoritative, perhaps showing he is exactly the sort of leader England need after a chaotic period on and off the pitch.

There were also signs of Fleming's character and sense of humour. He joked he has a "stress fracture of the left ear" after all the phone calls he has had with those connected with the England team, then laughed about occasionally turning up in fancy dress to relax the environment of his Chennai Super Kings team.

Most revealing was the description of his relationship with Brendon McCullum – "I'll bet on the favourite and he'll bet on the longest odds possible". There were plenty of times during McCullum's reign as Test coach where those long-odds bets were placed, while Fleming seems much more likely to play the percentages.

The two are great friends, which should help with a split-coaching dynamic that has not always served England well in the past. "Big brother" was one way the Fleming-McCullum dynamic was referred to, and there was a sense that England now have a grown-up in charge, following the freewheeling of McCullum.

Fleming covered a range of topics: he won't try to persuade Ben Stokes to come out of retirement, he will give the World Test Championship a level of respect lacking from previous England teams, he explained he missed the Pakistan series because of family and commercial commitments.

Fleming also addressed discipline and the late-night controversies that have dogged England in the past 12 months. Talk of "standards" may not be good news for Brydon Carse's prospects of a swift return to the set-up.

And, of course, there was the question of "Flemball", dismissed as a "medical condition".

On this evidence, Fleming's England will be more assured, mature and level than the team led by McCullum. Possibly less fun, too.

The most important thing is they win more, starting in South Africa in December.

title: In chaotic L.A. skies, news helicopter pilots juggle competition, camaraderie, risk
description:
For the record:
1:38 p.m. Sept. 19, 2026: An earlier version of this article stated KCAL's helicopter is owned by Angel City Air. It is owned by Helicopters Inc.
fullText:
For the record:
1:38 p.m. Sept. 19, 2026: An earlier version of this article stated KCAL's helicopter is owned by Angel City Air. It is owned by Helicopters Inc.

Whether it's a brush fire, a mass shooting, a car chase or the aftermath of a major storm, viewers in Los Angeles are used to getting the news from above.

Television news helicopter coverage has become one of the most important elements of any local newscast, with the high-flying helicopters roaring overhead a common fixture of breaking news scenes.

These images are so ubiquitous, it may have been easy to take them for granted, until Tuesday, when an NBC4 helicopter carrying reporter Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw crashed while covering breaking news in Chatsworth. Both died, along with a bystander on the ground.

The tragedy has prompted soul-searching in the world of TV news helicopter pilots and focused attention on safety issues.

Pilots describe a high-stakes race in the skies of Los Angeles, with the TV stations battling to get breaking news on the air first. The airspace easily becomes crowded, and in the case of moving stories like car chases, a bit unpredictable and chaotic. The crews who take to the air in Los Angeles must not only navigate one another, but air traffic to three regional airports and smaller, local airstrips across the Southland when doing their job.

They say that safety is always the top priority and that everyone in the air works together to avoid problems.

The NBC4 crash marks the most serious incident involving an L.A. news chopper crew since 2000, when a Fox 11 helicopter covering the Academy Awards crashed and burst into flames at Van Nuys Airport.

Nationally, National Transportation Safety Board data show that 16 people have died in eight fatal crashes involving news helicopters in the United States since 2000. A cause of Tuesday's crash has not been determined, but some experts have said they believe mechanical failure might be responsible.

"It crushed us all," said Tim Lynn, a now-retired helicopter pilot and reporter who flew for 16 years for KTLA-TV. Lynn worked with Moreno and knew how much she cherished her job.

"She loved the job so much that she put her all into it," he said.

For all the camaraderie in the air, there is also some competition.

Stations want to be first to get to the scene of breaking news.

Kurt Deetz, a former news helicopter pilot who retired five years ago, said it's a difficult business to be in.

"It's very competitive, and at what cost?" Deetz said.

News pilots tend to have plenty of experience, former pilots said, and dangerous incidents are rare. But Deetz said pilots are pushed to be out in the air first, get to the scene, and remain on scene for extended periods of time.

"If you can be the first on the scene, you're a hero," Deetz said. "I think about that now and think, that is so dumb."

Deetz started his career with KMEX in 1995, and worked for nearly every station in the area while working with Helinet, he said.

In the sky, reporters and pilots keep an eye out for one another, warning when one is drifting too close to another or if there is something else to keep an eye on.

"We all know each other," Lynn said. "Maybe we never met, but we've all talked on the radio and know the names."

There are unspoken rules that news helicopter pilots learn once they join, Lynn said.

During a police chase, for example, the first helicopter on the scene immediately takes the front position left of the fleeing vehicle, he said. The next helicopter takes a position behind that helicopter. The third takes a spot in the front right side of the chase, and the fourth sits behind it. All four maintain those spots throughout the chase, regardless of the turns and twists throughout the area.

And when the pursued begins to circle a residential area — a common occurrence during police pursuits — all news helicopters are expected to stop and hover in place, even if their shots are temporarily blocked by trees and buildings.

That's because the tight turns and circles could result in a crash if all helicopters remain in pursuit.

"You never move unless you say something," Lynn said. "It's a well-coordinated operation."

Lynn remembers at least once when a new pilot joined in a pursuit.

"We were all stopped and he's just chasing the guy like he's the police," he said.

Lynn got on the radio and, as the other three choppers kept their position, Lynn asked him to stick to "one of the corners."

"That was a learning curve for that guy," he said.

But Lynn said there's respect for new staff and veterans in the field. Regardless of what station they work for, reporters and pilots are constantly helping one another, abiding by unspoken rules to keep them all safe.

There is one maneuver that pilots say brings them particular anxiety.

Jack Cress, a former helicopter pilot for the Marine Corps and a helicopter accident investigation instructor for USC's Aviation Safety and Security Program, said news helicopters will often spend time hovering over an incident, sometimes at a low altitude.

"That is a dangerous place to be," Cress said.

For Deetz, he said he'd often say that he wouldn't hover low for extended periods of time, especially if he didn't see a place he could land in case of an emergency.

"You set up, get your shot, and then you move on," he said. "I made a point of saying, 'I'm not going to hover here for hours.' "

He knows the practice is still popular among current pilots, which he thinks needs to be rethought.

"In this day and age, there's no need to hover," he said. "Those cameras are so powerful. There's no need to be so low."

Helicopter pilots are trained to stay away from those conditions because, in case of trouble like engine failure, the lack of altitude and forward momentum gives the pilot little recourse. If the engine were to fail, for example, a pilot can sometimes perform an "autorotation" procedure to use altitude and forward momentum to force the rotors to turn, easing their descent.

The procedure is one that Lynn is familiar with. In 2012, he was covering an incident in Hollywood for KTLA when his helicopter started to smoke heavily. He had no idea until one of the other choppers radioed him to tell him.

"As soon as I turn it, he said, 'You need to put it on the ground now,' " Lynn said.

Lynn headed down and started getting the helicopter ready for an autorotation, as heavy smoke started to shoot from the engine. Lynn looked toward the ground and was eyeing Highland Avenue or Los Feliz Boulevard for a makeshift landing spot. He gripped the controls and expected the engine to give out at any second, until he spotted a parking lot. He watched for the wires, watched for the trees and set it down. The motor never gave out.

Pilots will constantly eye one another in the formation.

News helicopter pilots will normally stay around 1,200 to 1,500 feet above the ground, Lynn said. That is to stay above police helicopters, under commercial flights, and still have enough space in case they need to perform an emergency autorotation procedure.

Although news helicopters are touted as a cornerstone of local news broadcasts, the aircraft are owned and operated by third-party companies. KTLA and NBC4's helicopters, for example, are owned and operated by Angel City Air, part of Welk Aviation. ABC 7's helicopter is operated by Helinet, and KCAL's helicopter is owned by Helicopters Inc.

Many of them are flying the same kind of helicopter that crashed Tuesday, the AS350 B2, which aviation experts said is a popular helicopter for news stations and police departments.

Deetz said he flew that helicopter for his entire career in news, and never once had a dangerous mechanical issue.

It took minutes for word of the NBC4 crash to spread across the world of Los Angeles news chopper pilots and journalists.

"I immediately wondered who. We all know each other," Lynn said.

One of Lynn's former colleagues told him they saw a tail rotor on the ground, and Lynn quickly learned it was Moreno and Marciniw who were aboard.

A former police pilot for Huntington Beach and a retired news helicopter pilot after 16 years, Lynn said he and other pilots have shared the established rules with new pilots and reporters who joined the business over the years — including Moreno, whom Lynn said he helped train when she joined Angel City Air as a reporter.

Lynn remembers when she joined the company, he said. She quickly picked up on the equipment she had to use and eagerly sought advice to get better at the job.

The National Transportation Safety Board, which is investigating the crash, is expected to release a preliminary report on the incident in the coming days. A complete report on the incident is expected to take up to 18 months to be completed.

title: Ukraine targets Moscow with hundreds of drones in ‘largest ever’ attack
description:
Ukrainian forces fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, including hundreds that were launched toward Moscow, officials said Sunday as the Kremlin was wrapping up the third and last day of its parliamentary elections. 
Moscow’s mayor described the wave of drones as the “largest ever” attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.
Across the wider Moscow region, the attack killed two people and wounded 20, local Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said. The dead were a 74-year-old man and a 44-year-old woman, he said.
fullText:
Ukrainian forces fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, including hundreds that were launched toward Moscow, officials said Sunday as the Kremlin was wrapping up the third and last day of its parliamentary elections.

Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.

Across the wider Moscow region, the attack killed two people and wounded 20, local Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said. The dead were a 74-year-old man and a 44-year-old woman, he said.

Writing on social media, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Kyiv had used a range of missiles and drones in the attack — including Ukraine's domestically made Flamingo and Pelican missiles — to hit oil and logistics facilities.

"These are billions of dollars that sustain the war machine," Zelenskyy said, referring to the financial pressure that Kyiv hopes to put on Russia's economy.

Ukraine also continued to fend off Russian attacks, Zelenskyy said. A Russian drone strike hit a monastery in Ukraine's Kherson region Saturday, killing a member of the clergy and wounding four people, he said.

A Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital also killed two children and their mother on Saturday evening, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv regional state administration. He later said that another child wounded in the same attack had died in hospital on Sunday.

The attack took place on the final day of Russia's first wartime parliamentary election — balloting that has been virtually devoid of opposition to President Vladimir Putin's policies and is all but certain to cement the Kremlin's dominance.

Russia was also holding the vote in the four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began but still doesn't fully control, and in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that was illegally annexed by Russia in 2014. Kyiv has denounced the action as illegal.

Russia's Ministry of Defense said that its forces shot down a total of 1,110 Ukrainian drones across the country, as well as over the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the waters of the Black Sea.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 450 drones had been destroyed en route to the Russian capital, and that the attack had damaged the Moscow Oil Refinery and a residential building.

He said the "unprecedented attack" on Moscow was an attempt to disrupt the elections. "The enemy failed in this regard," he said.

Since Russia's invasion more than four years ago, Ukraine has become a global leader in military drone technology, deploying domestically produced long-range drones alongside missiles for strikes deep inside Russia. Its drone technology has impressed governments and defense manufacturers around the world.

Kyiv is aiming to make the Russian public feel the war's consequences and pressure Russian President Vladimir Putin into negotiating a peace settlement. Putin has so far shown no signs he intends to stop the invasion.

Instead, Moscow and Kyiv have been drawn into an escalating duel of long-range aerial strikes as fighting along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (780-mile) front line in eastern and southern Ukraine has slowed, restricted by large numbers of drones and ground robots threatening troop movements.

fullText:
The United States warned Saturday that hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could "escalate rapidly" after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed.

US President Donald Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday.

The White House gave no explanation for the early return, which comes as a new threshold was crossed in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and are fighting government forces backed by a coalition led by Riyadh.

Loud explosions rang out twice on Saturday in the Saudi capital, where AFP journalists saw a fuel tank bearing the logo of oil giant Aramco on fire near the airport.

"This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should "seriously reconsider travel to and through the region".

The Houthis's lightning offensive seizing swathes of Yemeni territory in recent weeks has left hundreds dead and, according to the UN, displaced more than 110,000 people.

These clashes and the subsequent hostilities with the kingdom have already disrupted Saudi Arabia's exports -- the world's leading supplier of crude oil -- as well as maritime traffic.

The Riyadh-led coalition confirmed Saturday evening on X that a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the capital was "successfully intercepted and destroyed".

The coalition added that the pro-Iranian fighters had tried to target "civilians and civilian infrastructure" in several cities in the west of the kingdom, including the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, an important export hub for Saudi oil.

It said these attacks were "thwarted by the Gulf monarchy's air defences".

Saudi Arabia has responded with scores of airstrikes on Houthi-held areas but failed to stop the advance.

The Houthis said it had responded to recent Saudi attacks by carrying out "two successful military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones", Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement on Telegram.

"The first targeted sensitive sites in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu."

Saudi authorities had earlier issued an overnight air raid alert.

Hours after the early morning alert, residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through parts of the Saudi capital.

This is the first time since Yemen's civil war resumed that strikes have threatened the Saudi capital, piling further pressure on a global economy already rocked by seven months of war between the US and Iran.

"The area is under a hostile aerial threat," according to a message received just before 3:00 am by Riyadh residents, urging them to stay indoors.

"I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," a Riyadh resident told AFP. Another resident described the attack as "terrifying".

The incident comes days after Riyadh accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca on Wednesday, denouncing it as a "cowardly terrorist attack" on Islam's holy city, which welcomes millions of pilgrims each year. The Houthis strongly denied the accusation, calling it a "worn-out lie".

The group has reported scores of retaliatory strikes carried out daily by Riyadh since their offensive this month to take over the country's entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.

The United States, according to US news platform Axios, last week refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis.

Washington approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to the kingdom on Thursday to help Riyadh "deter current and future threats", the US State Department said.

War in Yemen broke out in 2014 when the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and other regions, triggering a military intervention led by Saudi Arabia in March 2015.

The fragile truce reached in 2022 between the warring parties collapsed in July, when the Houthis defied Riyadh's control of Yemeni airspace by allowing an Iranian aircraft to land in Yemen.

The apparent attack came as the Houthis improve their defences in newly conquered territory along Yemen's Red Sea coastline, with members of the group telling AFP they have been installing radar and digging tunnels.

title: NFL Insider reveals Houston Texans did not want to offer Deshaun Watson an extension in 2020
description: Deshaun Watson played his best football with the Houston Texans before his NFL career started going downhill with controversies and injuries. The Texans traded up 13 places to get Watson, who had played college football at Clemson.
fullText:
Deshaun Watson played his best football with the Houston Texans before his NFL career started going downhill with controversies and injuries.

The Texans traded up 13 places to get Watson, who had played college football at Clemson.

It was pure brilliance from Watson from the moment he wore the Texans jersey, with top performances in his rookie season itself.

However, his rookie season was cut short due to an ACL injury, but Watson came back for a massive sophomore season and ended up putting up top performances to make it to three consecutive All-Pro teams.

In 2020, Watson began negotiations with the Texans for his extension. It seemed like that would be the best decision the team could make, as he had proven himself to be a top QB in the league.

However, the franchise had a lot to think about according to an NFL Insider.

Having come off his career-best year, it was certain that Watson was always going to be given the contract he was looking for.

But the Texans had appointed Jack Easterby as their executive vice president of football operations. According to NFL Insider, Tom Pelissero, he was not keen on extending Watson's contract.

"Some on staff didn't want to extend Watson at all—most notably then–executive vice president of football operations Jack Easterby, who had arrived from New England in 2019 with designs on resetting the building and immediately had friction with Watson.

"While often electric on the field, he was frequently late to meetings, wanted increased influence over personnel and coaching decisions, and had trouble correcting some on-field shortcomings, such as a cadence that coaches felt was contributing to pre-snap penalties," wrote Pelissero on his Substack.

The Texans eventually ended up extending him on a four-year, $156 million deal. Watson only played one year before deciding to sit out the next, as he was looking for a trade away from the franchise.

Eventually, a few off-the-field issues came into the open, which ideally should have decreased his value, but the Cleveland Browns decided to give him a chance, and offered him a five-year $230 million deal.

Since then, he has only played 20 games for them and has been the subject of constant criticism from fans and the media.

title: NASCAR Cup Series Driver Steals the Show With Dolly Parton Tribute at Bristol
description: One NASCAR Cup Series driver fully embraced Bristol's Dolly Parton celebration, arriving at driver introductions wearing an unmistakable platinum-blonde wig.
fullText:
Tyler Reddick wasn't exactly difficult to spot during driver introductions Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway.

The driver of the No. 45 Toyota emerged in front of the crowd wearing a long, platinum-blonde wig, delivering his own unmistakable salute to Tennessee royalty Dolly Parton.

At a racetrack where subtlety has never exactly been the specialty, Reddick understood the assignment.

The surprise look came as Bristol celebrates Parton during its NASCAR Cup Series weekend, adding another distinctly Tennessee touch to one of the sport's biggest nights of the year.

And Reddick decided to get in on the celebration himself.

Reddick walked onto the driver introductions stage with both arms raised and the blonde wig flowing over his firesuit, leaning all the way into the moment before climbing into his No. 45 SiriusXM Toyota for 500 laps around Bristol's notoriously unforgiving half-mile.

The disguise wasn't going to fool anybody.

Parton's signature blonde hair has been part of her instantly recognizable look for decades, and Reddick's choice made the inspiration clear without saying a word.

The result was one of the more memorable driver entrances of the night.

It was also a fitting tribute at a venue that has spent the weekend celebrating the people and culture surrounding its Tennessee home. Parton's connection to East Tennessee runs far deeper than celebrity alone. Born and raised in the Smoky Mountains, she has built a legacy in the region that extends from music and entertainment to philanthropy.

Reddick's version of a tribute was considerably less formal.

He put on a blonde wig and walked onto the Bristol stage.

Reddick's lighthearted entrance came during a Bristol evening carrying considerably more emotion elsewhere.

The track has also spent the weekend honoring the late Kyle Busch, whose history at Bristol made the venue one of the defining stops of his NASCAR career. Ty Gibbs is driving a special M&M's tribute scheme, while thousands of fans waved yellow towels during Lap 18 of Saturday night's race in Busch's memory.

That made Reddick's Dolly Parton moment a fun change of pace during a night built around celebration, remembrance and plenty of Tennessee personality.

There are easier ways to walk across a driver introductions stage.

But at Bristol, with Dolly Parton being honored?

The blonde wig was tough to beat.

fullText:
Fort Valley State, Benedict game defined by almost comeback, heat & score error appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

I've been a fan of college football, especially HBCU football, for a long time. I started my HBCU career 11 years ago as a freshman at Fort Valley State, and since then I've attended a lot of football games, both as a fan and as a journalist. This is the first day where I quite literally could not stand the heat. I've been a fan of college football and specifically HBCU football for a long time. I started my HBCU career 11 years ago as a freshman at Fort Valley State, and now I've been to a lot of football games, both as a fan and as a journalist. This is the first day I quite literally couldn't stand the heat.

When my family and I arrived on site at Wildcat Stadium for the Benedict College versus Fort Valley State game, it was humid but cloudy. The clouds went away rather quickly, though, and it became unbearably hot, so much so that my family and I decided to go into the student center, where we ultimately began to socialize with alumni and community members. We nearly missed Fort Valley State's comeback and a scoring error that would have likely resulted in the HBCU version of the Michigan-Western Michigan controversy, only for an in-conference matchup.

Benedict College ultimately emerged victorious, 34-33, and the same issues that ultimately have plagued Fort Valley State in the Malon Watson era were showcased. The Wildcats showed tremendous promise against one of the best teams in the conference, and while some things need to change, they showed a level of fight that can carry them through the rest of the season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Simply put, Fort Valley State's defense was the Wildcats' star. The offense, through most of the first three quarters, simply couldn't move the ball down the field, though there were big plays, such as Roger Payne's 70-yard touchdown run and Don Hudson's 12-yard scamper that ignited the Wildcat comeback. The defense prevented Benedict from putting this game out of reach many times. The Wildcats' defense forced three turnovers from Benedict: one fumble and two interceptions, including an amazing playmaking interception that came off a tackle. The ball then popped into the hands of the Fort Valley State defender, which I saw as a potential turning-point moment for Fort Valley.

We have enough of a sample size of Marlon Watson's Wildcats competing against some of the best teams that the SIAC and Division II football have to offer. Talent is not the issue, but for Fort Valley State in this era, it's execution and play calling. The defense has been contending with teams like Delta State, Benedict, and the University of West Alabama, but to truly make that leap to championship level, Fort Valley State has to figure out how to make that offense more competent around Don Hudson Jr.

My family and I withstood the heat until early in the fourth quarter. The last play we saw that had us all outdone was Don Hudson handing off to Roger Payne. That was ultimately stuffed by the Benedict College defenders blitzing. That added to the frustration and confusion about what was being called on offense, and whether the offensive line could sustain Don Hudson long enough to make throws in the pocket.

Throughout the game, Hudson did what he normally does: make amazing runs and reads on the run. But the same problems persisted. It appeared that Don had happy feet in the pocket, and some of the concepts were odd, even though the short shutdown passes were ultimately successful at several points in the game. While I am a fan of Hudson's ability to play make with his legs and scramble, I think he'll be better served as a true dual threat. To do that, he has to navigate the pocket before bursting out to run.

The touchdown throw to JT Pendleton that ultimately turned into a 61-yard gain before being stopped at Benedict's 6-yard line was a perfect example of the proof of concept of what Dine could be if he used his mobility to navigate in the pocket. He stepped up in the pocket and found Pendleton for a great play and a great game.

Now, granted, Benedict, for some reason, decided to rush only three and play a bit of prevent defense, which ultimately led to that huge gain. Of course, that played a part in how Hudson navigated the pocket. Still, that is proof of concept I want to see more of throughout the season, and for as long as Don Hudson will be at Fort Valley State.

Former Florida A&M Rattler turned Benedict College QB1 Jett Peddy is exactly what the Tigers needed. While Jett had some moments that weren't ideal, he proved adept at calling the game and using both his arms and his legs to make things happen for Benedict's offense. That was a great recruiting win for Ron Dickerson and could be the deciding factor for Benedict ultimately making and winning the SIAC championship and advancing into the NCAA Division II playoffs once again.

I was a fan of how you could see him process the field and decide whether to run or pass in tandem with Benedict's three talented running backs. They put Fort Valley State's defense in precarious situations that, more often than not, Benedict benefited from. It's hard not to say this isn't the best team in the SIAC. I know it's a long season, and Fort Valley gave them all they could handle, but with Petty under center and a stable of talented running backs who can all make plays, Bearded is a team to watch out for.

The game was ultimately defined by a pretty odd scorekeeping error that could have affected both teams' strategy. The game was ultimately defined by a pretty odd scorekeeping error that could have affected both teams' strategy. At the start of the fourth quarter, around the 8-minute mark, Christopher Johnson made a 25-yard rush to the end zone to go up 27-15 after the PAT.

For some reason, the PAT wasn't reflected on the scoreboard, although he made it, so it read 26-15. In a normal game where Benedict goes on to win, the score discrepancy wouldn't have mattered much and probably would have been caught after the game. Because of Fort Valley State's comeback attempt, it became a huge story that left both ESPN+ commentators, Thai Floyd and Sylvester Williams, audibly confused, as well as both teams' coaches. Fans from both Benedict and Fort Valley State were confused, too.

Ultimately, Benedict was assessed the point, and Fort Valley went on to score two touchdowns to tie the game, but instead of going for the PAT, they went for two on the first touchdown to attempt to make it 26-23 because they thought Benedict had 26. The PAT was unsuccessful and ultimately led to what happened at the end. I believe that shows how the incorrect score on the scoreboard affected the game, because if they went for the PAT, the score would've been 27-22.

The touchdown at the end of the game would have made the score 28-27 with Fort Valley in the lead before the PAT. That scenario would have changed the strategy for both Fort Valley State and Benedict, as Benedict would have had to come back on offense, look to the score to regain the lead, and ultimately secure the victory.

While this doesn't take away from Benedict's win, it ultimately is an unfortunate ending to a game that had the opportunity to be one of the games of the year. Nevertheless, Fort Valley State has several things to clean up to ensure this doesn't happen again, especially against better teams in the SIAC and Division II football.

title: Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sent the baseball world into a frenzy when they traded for Tarik Skubal, but according to Andrew Friedman, it was a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make. The post Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' quest to win their third straight World Series title is alive and well, as they have officially clinched the National League West division with eight games left on their schedule. For now, the team's main goal involves getting healthy, but even if it can't, it should still be the favorite to win it all until further notice.

At the trade deadline, the Dodgers did what they always do and went all-in by acquiring the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young winner, Tarik Skubal, in a trade with the Detroit Tigers. It was almost expected that L.A. would be the team landing Skubal, but according to general manager Andrew Friedman, this was actually a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make.

With the Tigers failing to sign Skubal to a long-term contract extension over the offseason, he ended up being the big fish that every team wanted at the trade deadline. Of course, landing Skubal was going to require a massive haul of prospects, which is something the Dodgers always seem to have at their disposal.

Los Angeles has developed a reputation for simply being willing to go above and beyond what every other team in the majors is willing to do. Whether it involves shelling out more money for the top free agents, or giving up whatever prospects a team wants for its top player, the Dodgers are always making moves, which is why it wasn't a surprise to see them land Skubal.

Despite that aforementioned narrative continuing to swirl around the team, Los Angeles has claimed that it didn't want to have to make this sort of move this year. According to Friedman, the list of the Dodgers' trade targets started and ended with Skubal, which could help explain why they were so willing to part with several of their top prospects for a guy who is set to hit the free agent market in just a couple of months.

"We looked to do everything we could over the offseason to avoid being a buyer in July, short of a real impact-type talent," Friedman said, per Tom Verducci of Sports Illustrated. "And so, from our standpoint, our buy side list was Tarik Skubal. End of list."

Trading Skubal was always going to be risky for all 29 other teams in the majors because if he hits the open market, the Dodgers are going to be the favorite to sign him. Without a true salary cap in place, nothing is stopping Los Angeles from spending above and beyond what every other team is spending on its roster, and it has put that theory to the test over the past few years.

It's gotten to the point where a lockout feels inevitable, as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will expire at the conclusion of the season, and there has been virtually no momentum towards a new deal. For now, the Dodgers are intent on winning another championship, but their actions could wind up being at the center of a very important discussion this offseason, with many folks viewing the Skubal trade as the final nail in the coffin.

Indiana football took on Western Kentucky in Week 3 amid injuries to two defensive tackles and came through with flying colors, winning 38-0 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. Following the game, NFL insider Jordan Schultz revealed that scouts are keeping a close watch on the 6-foot-4, 210-pound Indiana receiver, who possesses traits that could get him drafted early.

"Keep a close eye on Indiana star WR Charlie Becker: 6-4, 210 pounds with game-breaking speed, elite athleticism and burst — with 5 TDs in three games this season. It's early, but the NFL clubs I've spoke with are raving about his pro-style game already."

Becker, still a junior, had four catches for 64 yards in Cignetti's team's 27-21 win over the Miami Hurricanes in the 2025-26 national championship game and has only improved since. His size allows him to make contested catches over smaller defenders while his hands, route-running and speed continue to impress.

Becker was discussed as a future WR2 in the NFL before the season with some scouts believing he is even faster than Omar Cooper, who also starred against the Hurricanes last season and ran a 4.42 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine. Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover has looked good since transferring from TCU this offseason, giving Indiana plenty of momentum heading into Week 4 against Aidan Chiles and the Northwestern Wildcats.

October 17, a showcase game against Ohio State in Bloomington, will give Becker a chance to duel with Buckeyes superstar Jeremiah Smith. Win that game, and Becker could find himself in early-round territory by the time the 2027 NFL Draft rolls around.

title: UFC 331 live blog: Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski
description: Follow live UFC 331 results for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski
fullText:
This is the UFC 331 live blog for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski, the main card light heavyweight bout Saturday at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

Menifield (18-7-1) heads into Saturday night's event as the underdog, but the 205-pound veteran has a habit of spoiling the plans of the matchmakers. This past May, he headed into enemy territory to win a thrilling striking battle against China's Zhang Mingyang, and was previously the first man to defeat French prospect Oumar Sy. He has won three of his past four fights.

The red-hot Baraniewski (9-0) seeks his fourth UFC victory, with none of his octagon appearances lasting longer than 90 seconds. Baraniewski, 27, debuted with a wild win over Ibo Aslan, and followed that up with a 28-second knockout over Austen Lane before scoring another fast finish against Junior Tafa. With a win over the veteran Menifield, Baraniewski likely finds himself with a number next to his name when the rankings are next updated.

Check out the UFC 331 live blog for Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski below.

All aboard the Iwo Baraniewski hype train! Is he the future light heavyweight GOAT or, as Jed Meshew has suggested, just the 205-pound version of Terrance McKinney? We'll learn a lot tonight in this matchup with the always game Alonzo Menifield.

The undefeated Baraniewski is a sizable favorite at -295 according to FanDuel, Menifield the underdog at +240.

Tentative start, both guys respecting each other's power. Menifield lands a right, Baraniewski answers with a left hand. Menifield with a good job, but Baraniewski connects with a power punch and that backs Menifield up. Menifield comes forward and gets rocked again. Baraniewski on the offensive, Menifield wisely ties him up.

They separate and Baraniewski immediately starts throwing, he has Menifield hurt. Baraniewski in top position now, working to get to full mount. Menifield survives but he looks rattled as the round comes to a close, Baraniewski continuing to fire.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Baraniewski.

Menifield immediately comes out swinging and Baraniewski just eats it. No way these guys can keep fighting like this without someone getting flattened. Pace finally slows with the fighters pummeling against the fence. Back at distance, Baraniewski and Menifield looking to establish the jab. Baraniewski connects and immediately goes headhunting, Menifield with good movement to stay out of danger. Neither guy looks particularly fresh right now and there's a lot of fight left.

Gnarly fight inside, Menifield scoring. Whenever he gets going, though, one good counter from Baraniewski gives him pause. Baraniewski beating Menifield to the punch, Menifield's chin is holding up. Menifield with a right across the chin. He ends the round as the aggressor. Close, close round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Menifield. Overall, 19-19.

Before the round starts, they're bringing in a doctor to check on Menifield's hand. All good. The broadcast zooms in and it looks like his thumb is mangled. Eep.

Quick flurry from Menifield and Baraniewski ties him up. He's pressuring Menifield against the fence. Action has slowed to a crawl. This could be good for Baraniewski with his gas tank not exactly at peak capacity right now. Menifield reverses position and now he has fence control. Crowd boos the lack of action. Menifield trying to throw short punches, but Baraniewski stays locked on to him.

We get a separation with about 90 seconds to go. They trade jabs, Menifield with a slight advantage as it looks like he has more energy. The veteran might pull this off. This is a Menifield round for me, but could go Baraniewski's way if he got the first two.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Menifield. Overall, 29-28 Menifield.

Official result: Alonzo Menifield def. Iwo Baraniewski via split decision (29-28 x2, 28-29)

Menifield calls Baraniewski "awesome" and then downplays his thumb injury, saying his problems are nothing compared to that of homeless people. He says his mom used to have to search through trash when he was growing up, "Where I come from, this is my background, I have to be [tough]."

During the opening half, Chivas created several chances, but the ball could not find the back of the net. However, Guadalajara's persistence never faded, and the reward came in the 39th minute. Denise Castro reacted to a rebound inside the box and sent it into the back of the net.

With the lead in hand, the Rojiblancas entered the second half with the mission of preserving their advantage while continuing to fight until the final minute. Xolos looked to respond, but the Rebaño's defensive work kept a clean sheet for Blanca Félix. In the final stretch, Chivas also had another opportunity to extend the lead. In the 87th minute, a free kick taken by Alicia Cervantes beat the wall and went over the crossbar; however, the play was called offside by the referee. Despite this, the Rojiblanco side's finishing finally came through in stoppage time. In the 94th minute, a great Guadalajara play once again found Alicia Cervantes inside the box, and she sent the ball into the back of the net to make it 2-0.

With this result, Chivas Femenil earned an important victory that keeps them in second place in Group B with 15 points. Guadalajara will now prepare for another away test, as they visit Cruz Azul next Friday, September 25, in a Matchday 9 AP26 clash at Estadio Centenario de Morelos at 7 PM.

- Denise stepped up for the Rebaño! In the 39th minute, Denise Castro pounced on a rebound to give the rojiblancas the lead.

- A masterful play to seal the match! In the 94th minute, the finishing touch finally found Alicia Cervantes, who finished inside the box to put the final score on the board.

- NATALIAAAA! In the 16th minute, Natalia Colin took a corner kick that struck the far post, although the ball eventually went just wide.

- In the 18th minute, Joseline Montoya unleashed an absolute rocket from inside the border side's box, but the Xolos defense stepped in to block the effort.

- In the 21st minute, the rojiblancas threatened again from a corner kick, with a delivery into a dangerous area that forced the Tijuana defense to work hard to clear the ball.

- 'LICHAAAA' AGAIN! In the 87th minute, Cervantes took a free kick that crossed the goal line, but the play was called offside by the referee.

title: Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans
description: After playing Week 1 with (almost) a fully healthy roster, with only Jonathan Greenard on the injury report after Eli Stowers was placed on IR, things aren’t quite so clean for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. On their final injury report of Week 2 , the Eagles featured six players but only two with game statuses. Jalen Carter, Hollywood Brown, […] The post Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

After playing Week 1 with (almost) a fully healthy roster, with only Jonathan Greenard on the injury report after Eli Stowers was placed on IR, things aren't quite so clean for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.

On their final injury report of Week 2, the Eagles featured six players but only two with game statuses. Jalen Carter, Hollywood Brown, Cooper DeJean, and Elijah Moore all missed time during the week but are good to go, while Andrew Mukuba is questionable and Greenard remains out as he works back from the summer pectoral injury.

While there were plenty of talking points coming out of Week 1 on offense, from the big passing plays downfield, to the Eagles' deceptive run struggles and rookie Makai Lemon's negative passing yards, on defense, one rose above the rest: Carter injuring his wrist.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Now granted, Carter still played the lion's share of the snaps for Vic Fangio against the Washington Commanders, playing 66 of a possible 70 defensive snaps, but he was seen at practice days later with a cast on his wrist and thus may not be 100 percent in Nashville against the Tennessee Titans.

And yet, even if Carter may be in pain, it hasn't forced him out of action, as he is currently a go to play in Week 2, alongside Brown, DeJean, and Moore, who were limited in some way during practice.

Mukuba also found himself on the injury report during the week, but unlike Carter, he remains questionable for the contest and will likely be a gameday decision for Fangio. If Mukuba, like Greenard, is unable to play in Week 2, the Eagles do have a contingency in place, as they've officially called up rookie safety Maximus Pulley from the practice squad for the game, but it's unlikely the former Wofford Terrier would get much action on defense, considering Fangio's propensity for playing more experienced players more often than not.

On the Titans sideline, Tennessee included three players on their final report of Week 2, with cornerback Cor'Dale Flott questionable with a quad and linebackers Cedric Gray and James Williams questionable with a concussion and elbow, respectively.

Fortunately, while the Eagles have the potential to be without higher-profile players, that shouldn't slow them down too much in Week 2, as their depth held strong against the Commanders and should remain strong, at least against an opponent like the Titans.

Friday’s Injury Report#PHIvsTEN pic.twitter.com/gdkNrruSZ3

— Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 18, 2026

In Week 1, the Eagles opted to roll with a four-man outside linebacker rotation rushing off the edge, largely sticking with their starters in true Fangio fashion, with some supplemental work off the bench from their free agent additions.

Jalyx Hunt led the team with 53 snaps and made a serious impact on the game even if his stats – three tackles – didn't show it. As has become the norm, Hunt can play the pass, the run, or even drop into coverage, and while he didn't get to Jayden Daniels, he was able to force him out of the pocket and take him off schedule. Nolan Smith followed close behind with 47 snaps, holding down the opposite side of the field as a three-down edge rusher, and behind him, the Eagles rotated in Arnold Ebiketie and AJ Epenesa, who had 28 and 12 defensive snaps, respectively.

Would the Eagles like to finish out a game with more than one sack, especially when it came from their back seven? Most certainly, but in Week 1, Cam Ward was sacked three times, and the Titans' offensive line hasn't exactly been considered the best in the NFL, so that problem could fix itself even without Greenard leading the rush.

At safety, however, things get a bit more complicated if Mukuba can't play because the Eagles simply don't have a ton of depth at the position, seemingly by choice.

Against the Commanders, Mukuba was one of only five Eagles players who logged all 70 defensive snaps alongside Zack Baun, Riq Woolen, Quinyon Mitchell, and DeJean. When the Eagles suffered an injury at safety in Week 1, with Marcus Epps leaving the field for a bit to get his shoulder worked on, Fangio turned to Michael Carter II as their sixth defensive back off the bench, logging six snaps.

But if Mukuba can't go? Then the plan may have to be adjusted over a full game, as DeJean does his best work in the slot, not as a base safety. MC2 and DeJean can play the same position and are more or less interchangeable on defense schematically, but when it comes to "true" safeties on the 53-man roster, the Eagles really only have two in Epps and Mukuba after losing Andre' Sam to a season-ending preseason injury against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Against an inexperienced quarterback like Ward, who only completed 19 of his 32 passing attempts in Week 1 against the Jets for 140 yards and a touchdown, being light at safety might not be the worst-case scenario. The Eagles lost Mukuba last year and were able to hold things down with Epps as a veteran option from their practice squad. But against a team like the Chicago Bears in Week 3? Goodness, Fangio can't want to rely on a cobbled-together secondary against a passing game that put up 269 aerial yards in Week 1.

Fortunately, there's still a chance Mukuba could play in Week 2 and that he could be back in time for Week 3 if things are close, but this injury does highlight that, unlike on the edge, the Eagles are rather light at safety and should consider ways to address that heading into the middle of the season and the trade deadline.

title: Florida State squanders early 15-point lead in loss to No. 10 Alabama
description: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Keelon Russell threw for 320 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score as No.
fullText:
TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Keelon Russell threw for 320 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score as No. 10 Alabama overcame a 15-point deficit to beat Florida State 50-36 on Saturday.

The Crimson Tide (3-0) struggled to run the ball early and had few answers for Florida State's explosive plays. Once Alabama settled in, the Seminoles (1-2) struggled to slow it down.

Russell completed 23 of 30 passes without an interception, and Alabama finished with 615 yards. Lotzeir Brooks caught eight passes for 101 yards.

Lightning delayed kickoff and interrupted the second quarter, and the teams agreed to skip halftime after the second delay.

Alabama scored touchdowns on five consecutive possessions across the second and third quarters to turn a 21-6 deficit into a 40-28 lead.

Ryan Coleman-Williams turned a short completion into a 46-yard touchdown, and Russell found Kaleb Edwards for the go-ahead score before the break.

Florida State cut the deficit to seven midway through the fourth quarter. Trae'shawn Brown answered with a 20-yard touchdown run with 2:15 remaining, capping a 90-yard drive. Bray Hubbard intercepted Ashton Daniels' pass on the ensuing possession.

Florida State: The Seminoles built an early cushion but could not get enough stops to repeat last season's stunning win over Alabama in Tallahassee.

Alabama: The comeback should ease some nerves for Crimson Tide fans after the first half, but defensive breakdowns and the inconsistent ground performance left plenty to address before returning to Southeastern Conference play.

title: Greenville shuts out Lakeview, moves to 4-0
description: Greenville shut out Lakeview, 41-0, during high school football action on Saturday.
fullText:
GREENVILLE, Pa. (WKBN) - Greenville shut out Lakeview, 41-0, during high school football action on Saturday.

Trojans quarterback Cael Thurber racked up 4 total touchdowns (2 passing, 2 rushing) in the first half. Both of his touchdown passes went to Justin Schell, one from 14 yards and another 63-yard touchdown in the final minute of the first half.

In the second half, Landon Porter and Swayze Walker added touchdowns during the 41-point victory.

The loss drops Lakeview to 2-2 on the season. The Sailors will host Cochranton on Friday, Sept. 25.

With the win, Greenville improves to 4-0 and will host Slippery Rock also on Friday, Sept. 25.

title: Broncos Add Homegrown Ex-Saints Running Back, Texans Find for Jaguars Game
description: The Denver Broncos have adjusted their roster, bringing on a veteran running back among their moves for Week 2. The post Broncos Add Homegrown Ex-Saints Running Back, Texans Find for Jaguars Game appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos are turning to local product and veteran running back Adam Prentice, a fullback who has shown he is capable of more than just being a lead blocker at the NFL level during his five-plus-year career.

This will be Prentice's second straight week of action.

This continues an important countdown for the Broncos moving forward. He is not the only one, either, as they prepare to host the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2.

We've elevated LS Mitchell Fraboni and FB Adam Prentice for #JAXvsDEN.

— Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 19, 2026

"The Broncos have added a pair of veterans to their game-day roster for the second consecutive week," DenverBroncos.com's Aric DiLalla wrote on September 19. "Denver elevated long snapper Mitchell Fraboni and fullback Adam Prentice from the practice squad to the active roster, the team announced Saturday.

"Fraboni has served as the Broncos' long snapper for each game since the start of the 2023 season. A sixth-year veteran, Prentice played 12 percent of the Broncos' offensive snaps and 68 percent of their special teams snaps in Week 1."

The Broncos can call each player up once more.

After that, they must sign them to the 53-man roster or find another option. Given their respective roles, finding room for them on the 53-man roster makes sense.

Prentice, 29, is a former Colorado State Rams standout. Prentice began his pro career with the Broncos as an undrafted free agent in 2021.

"Though he was never much of an offensive threat with the Rams, Prentice displayed solid blocking ability, toughness and a great work ethic," Travis Wakeman wrote for Predominantly Orange in 2021.

"Prentice was given minimal carries (20) during his college career but he did show the ability to catch the ball when his number was called. At the professional level, he would be trying to make a roster as a primary blocker who could be used in short-yardage situations or as a receiver that leaks out of the backfield on passing plays."

Prentice set career highs with 10 carries for 44 yards and 6 catches for 53 yards in 2025.

Prentice and Broncos head coach Sean Payton first crossed paths during their shared time with the New Orleans Saints. They have been reunited in Denver.

Fraboni, in his fifth season out of Arizona State. He began his career there as a defensive end, before transitioning to special teams. Fraboni entered the league as a UDFA with the Houston Texans,

He has also spent time with the Arizona Cardinals.

Fraboni also took his talents to the USFL, playing for the Pittsburgh Maulers. The Maulers selected Fraboni in the 35th round with the 278th overall pick.
