title: Open-source free meme generator, friendly for AI agents and humans
description: Free meme generator on Cloudflare Workers: a drag-and-drop editor for 200+ templates plus a URL-based meme API (every meme is just a link). - terryds/memegenscript
fullText:
A free meme generator that runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers:
an in-browser editor for 450+ templates, plus a URL-based API where every meme is just a link.

Every template has a human-facing, SEO-friendly editor page rendered by src/views/editor.ts:

The editor (assets/static/editor.js) runs entirely in the browser, imgflip-style:

Each page is server-rendered with a unique title, meta description, canonical URL, Open
Graph and Twitter Card tags (the example meme is the social image), JSON-LD (WebSite
with SearchAction, WebPage, ImageObject, BreadcrumbList), an <h1>, descriptive
copy, the template's source link, keyword links, and related templates. Without JavaScript
a <noscript> form posts to POST /images instead.

The site name in titles and social cards comes from the SITE_NAME variable.

The site is installable: /manifest.webmanifest (icons generated by
npx tsx scripts/build-icons.ts into assets/static/icons/), a service worker at /sw.js
(assets/static/sw.js, its cache name bound to the asset content hash so every deploy
refreshes caches), and an /offline fallback page. The worker serves pages network-first
with an offline fallback, and caches static assets, fonts, template images, and the last
80 rendered memes cache-first. On phones, assets/static/pwa.js shows a closeable
"Install" banner: Chrome/Android use the native prompt, iOS gets "Share → Add to Home
Screen" instructions; dismissal is remembered for 14 days and the banner never shows once
the app is installed.

Every template page explains what the meme is, where it comes from, its alternate names,
and related tags, so people can find a template by describing it rather than knowing its
name. The search on / (and ?q=) matches names, aliases, keywords, tags, example text,
and the description; multi-word queries require every word to match.

Know Your Meme excerpts are short, attributed, and linked; write original copy in the
manual file when you want fully unique page text.

Requirements: Node 20+, a Cloudflare account for deployment.

Cloudflare's free plan limits Workers to 10 ms of CPU per request, which is not enough
to render images. Deploy on the Workers Paid plan; wrangler.jsonc sets a 30 s CPU limit.

Variables are defined in wrangler.jsonc (vars). Secrets go through wrangler secret put
or a local .dev.vars file (see .dev.vars.example).

The API began as a TypeScript port of memegen
(Python), whose template library it still uses; the editor, pages, search, and design are
original. The table shows what replaced each Python-era dependency:

Request flow for GET /images/{template}/{text}.{ext}:

Drop a directory into assets/templates/<id>/ with a config.yml and a default.png
(or .jpg/.gif), exactly as in the Python project. Extra images in the directory become
style= options. The manifest is rebuilt automatically by npm run dev, npm test and
npm run deploy (or run npm run build:templates).

The full guide lives in docs/guide.md and the client notes in
docs/clients.md. Everything from the original README applies:

MIT. Portions of the API and the template library come from
memegen by Jace Browning (MIT); see
LICENSE.txt. Template images belong to their respective owners. Font licenses are in
assets/fonts/. Meme descriptions quote short, attributed excerpts from Know Your Meme.

title: Comparing reflection capabilities of C++, Zig and C3
description: Comparing reflection capabilities of C++, Zig and C3
fullText:
Reflection lets a program inspect and manipulate its own structure at runtime or compile time. All C++ (with its upcoming reflection support), Zig and C3 rely on compile-time reflection, so you can reason about types, enumerators, and struct members without any runtime cost. In this post I will compare how these languages approach compile-time reflection.

C3 is a relatively new programming language which mainly focuses on readability, performance, minimalism, and familiarity for C/C++ programmers.

 It doesn't have heavy runtime, garbage collection, exceptions or RAII.

 It also fully supports C ABI compatibility out of the box.

C3 uses special syntax for compile-time execution: all variables, control-flow constructs are prefixed with $. This was done on purpose to explicitly show the reader which code runs at compile time.
It uses macros for compile-time evaluation and reflection.

Let’s see all languages in action!

In Zig, the only solution I can think of is attaching a method to each enum you want to turn into a string, not a generic approach.
I’m not a profound zig expert so you can correct me in the comments.

In C3 enums have special properties. For example, if you want to print enum value, it will print it in a readable form, exactly as defined in the source code.
For example, this code: io::printfn(“%s”, Color.RED) will output RED, not 0.

If you want to take the underlying value from an enum, you can either access .ordinal or cast it to the underlying type.

You can also associate values of any type with your enumerators:

Let’s proceed with reflections!

Here, (1) C3 uses optional pre-conditions called 'contracts' which can help drastically with input validation.
They will be executed at compile-time if it is possible, if not - at runtime.

Zig:

Zig unfortunately doesn’t have ‘attributes’ or any substitute to attach compile-time data to struct members.

For this example with C3 I want to show you 2 options. In the first (1) variant we validate everything at compile-time, we can verify this easily by putting @const attribute on the macro.
In the second (2) variant we’re mixing compile-time attributes with validation at runtime. In this example you can see how syntax distinction between $if and if helps to understand
which code gets expanded at compile-time and which will execute at runtime.

All observed languages can do real compile-time reflection, which is great for serializers, debug printers, and generic helpers like the ones above.
The tradeoff is ergonomics: C++ gets the power via verbose template machinery and splices,
 while C3 makes the same ideas more readable and expressive through its macro system and special syntax for compile-time execution,
 it's very easy to understand where code will execute at compile time and where it wouldn't.

Zig in turn doesn't have macros, instead it relies on comptime functions and blocks, inline for loops and type-introspection builtins, which is also a good, modern and mostly readable approach.

Personally, I've found C3 to be a very promising systems programming language that needs more attention; everybody knows about C++ and Zig is marketed very well, but C3 lacks that kind of marketing, though it can compete easily with Zig, Odin, or any other new systems programming language out there.

 Also it doesn't have tons of breaking changes with each minor version. It's a lot more stable than Zig (honestly, it's pretty embarrassing that Zig is still stuck on 0.1x versions after over 10 years of development), and since C3 is already on 0.8.x versions, 1.0 is very close, see the roadmap.

You can search for more info about C3 on the main website.

Want to discuss the language or have a question? Join official C3 server on Discord.

title: Using system-one models inside high-throughput data pipelines
description: Jev (the system-one model) used with hank-based fallbacks can cut entity resolution costs and time by incredible amounts. Here's how.
fullText:
Jev (TypeSafe's system-one model) is a quantum leap forward for data processing pipelines, if harnessed correctly. We used Jev to accelerate an entity resolution pipeline to join donors and committees across Ohio campaign finance data. Hank-assisted resolution pipelines that use Jev as the workhorse reduced model costs by 99.56% and increased measured call-time throughput to 7.35× the baseline while retaining near-Fable quality.

But it's not all roses. Applying the wrong signal or prompting the wrong way causes large mistakes at scale. No free lunches, only subsidised ones.

We'll talk about the results, explain the task of entity resolution, and at the end we'll provide some prompts and principles that can work for integrating models like Jev into AI data pipelines.

Recorded model cost as a multiple of Jev only, against families matched, with bubble area for accumulated call time.

On a segment of the Ohio dataset that we selected to be difficult, using Fable to join entities costs $9.83 for 1.2 MB of prepared evidence, and takes 844.64 seconds.

An optimized hank (like the one below) is an alternative to direct comparisons using a model or a code-based approach. Here, it reduces model costs to $0.3012 for 715.08 seconds (a 32.6× reduction in cost but about the same time).

decideAnswer source-bound choice questions

the 10 referred · medium thinking

One codon, cloned per call. The runner binds the model, not the hank.

budget per call · 300 s deadline · 16,384 output tokens · fail on exceedevery attempt kept · prompt · response · session log · accounting

Using only Jev to adjudicate drops accuracy significantly, but Jev as the primary workhorse inside a five-family review stage with Luna provides 226x lower cost ($0.0000361 per KB), 7.35x higher throughput (10.5 KBps in call-seconds against Fable's 1.4), while being within 0.5 percentage points of Fable in accuracy.

Jev is the final missing piece for something we set out to do 18 months ago; to scale these workflows up to Terabytes of data.

The task is simple. Can we resolve entities across the Ohio Campaign Finance dataset? Entities here could be donors, committees, companies, etc. This is the task we have been working on as part of a much larger ingestion and data pipelining test designed to measure 4a, our internal superagent that can autonomously build and self-optimize AI data pipelines.

In practice, ER is incredibly difficult. Humans make honest mistakes - middle names are a common example.

We also move houses and jobs, change names, get married, omit information, and overall shenaniganize our lives.

Then there's (alleged) hostile obfuscation - large donors and companies attempting to spread out detection with different entity names, honest looking mistakes, etc etc.

Our ER pipeline resolves these problems using atoms - bundles of equivalent donor evidence. We put rows together into atoms, and models decide on what these bundles are (a company, a person, a committee, a joint donor or an unnamed record), and how they're related (same person, same household?). As we join more and more atoms, the dataset slowly resolves itself.

Here's one case: 11 rows, five atoms, two people. Ordinary code makes the atoms and keeps every original row. Jev judges which atoms represent the same donor, then whether the two donors share a household. The household is a connection between people, not permission to merge them.

If you were so inclined (either rich or a frontier lab), you could have a frontier LLM adjudicate every atom and bundle. However - even if you could pay for all of this (our estimate for the four-file Ohio snapshot is about $9,614 for Fable) - speed makes it difficult to do so. Even the best of us only have about 3 billion seconds of life.

Additionally, we have found that at scale, using cheaper models with additional review steps can surpass the accuracy of even frontier models deployed raw.

Here are the things we learned making Jev useful for this task.

This was the original yes criterion for a household link:

This is the criterion we replaced it with:

The revised instructions also say that DR and DRIVE don't break an address match, and that a shared employer, business address or PO box doesn't establish a household. On the same 13 development questions, Jev went from answering no to all 13 to yes to all 13, matching all 13 reference answers. Those are development results, not the final benchmark score.

Much like prompting in the 3.5-turbo days, more examples and more specific choices make things easier. Same for humans: we all prefer MCQs over essays!

More work remains to be done in integrating intelligence classifiers across data problems, especially when it comes to pipelining the raw performance on offer. This is the largest change we've seen in architecture since the flash (gemini, deepseek, glm) series of models to change how we structure data work in production. We are already seeing significant bumps in accuracy, cost and speed across other tasks like mining, selection, sanitization, and a lot more. We'll share results as we can make them ready for publication.

You can download the publication-safe experiment data and the Ohio campaign-finance sources here.

Want to try this on your own data? Start with Jev's typed questions, and use Hankweave for the reasoning steps.

title: Newsom signs California election safeguards aimed at Trump administration
description:
An election worker puts ballots in a counting machine at the Los Angeles County Ballot Processing Center on June 3 in City of Industry. Gov. Gavin Newsom has signed bills to protect California's elections process from interference and increase transparency in campaigns. (Kayla Bartkowski/Los Angeles Times)
Gov. Gavin Newsom on Saturday signed legislation to increase security for the state’s voting systems and protect Californians’ ability to cast ballots in an effort to guard against potential interference in the Nov.
fullText:
Gov. Gavin Newsom on Saturday signed legislation to increase security for the state's voting systems and protect Californians' ability to cast ballots in an effort to guard against potential interference in the Nov. 3 election, including by the Trump administration.

Newsom pointed to the Trump administration's recent effort to restrict mail-in voting through the U.S. Postal Service, which was struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court, and the presence of federal monitors at California polls last year as evidence that Trump "will continue his efforts to interfere with the November election."

"Donald Trump won't stop until he can exert dictatorial control over your free vote and disenfranchise millions of people this November. California will stop him at every opportunity," Newsom said in a statement. "We have no bigger task than fighting to protect the right to vote from interference and meddling — the future of democracy is on the line. These bills today build upon the wall California has built to safeguard our electoral process."

The governor signed the package of bills at the Japanese American National Museum in Little Tokyo, where a year earlier federal agents gathered outside a political rally he was hosting. Then-Border Patrol Sector Chief Gregory Bovino, who had been leading the immigration operations in California, was among those outside the event, joined by agents in helmets, camouflage, masks and holding guns. Newsom described their presence as political intimidation.

One bill Newsom signed Saturday cites efforts to "weaponize law enforcement authority for political purposes," including Republican "Sheriff Chad Bianco's seizure of ballots in Riverside County," and the election monitors sent by the U.S. Justice Department to polling sites in five counties during a 2025 special election on redistricting.

Such moves "have given rise to unprecedented concerns about law enforcement interference" in elections and "[demonstrate] that these threats are not merely hypothetical," the bill by state Sen. Tom Umberg (D-Santa Ana) reads.

The law, Senate Bill 884, which takes effect immediately, requires counties to open ballot drop-off locations 30 days before an election — two days earlier than usual — and allows counties to ban electioneering, or trying to influence voters' decisions, within up to 200 feet of polling sites. It also bans police from making arrests near voting locations except for crimes against people, property, or disrupting the voting process.

Atty. Gen. Rob Bonta and Secretary of State Shirley Weber, who oversees state elections, praised the bill signings and said they stood ready to defend Californians' right to vote.

"No one should doubt the degree of our resolve in protecting our democracy," Weber said. "This legislative package ensures that California voters will not be silenced or intimidated."

Bianco, a GOP candidate for governor who placed fourth in the primary, drew swift condemnation and legal challenges this spring after he ordered deputies to seize more than 650,000 ballots from the Riverside County elections office. Voting rights groups and Bonta challenged the move, which is being decided by the California Supreme Court.

Bianco carted off truckloads of ballots from the Riverside County Registrar of Voters in February after securing a warrant based on claims that the office allowed fraudulent votes in the special election to redraw California's congressional districts under Proposition 50 in 2025.

Earlier this year, Newsom signed a bill preventing local and federal law enforcement agencies from taking ballots without a warrant.

On Saturday the Democratic governor signed a bill making it a felony to seize or order the seizure of ballots, election records or voting machines. Future seizures could be punishable by up to four years in prison.

"The federal administration and those seeking to spread lies about our democracy continue to call for interference in elections in ways we have never seen before in this country," Assemblymember Gail Pellerin (D-Santa Cruz), the bill's author and a former longtime county elections chief, said last month. "AB 282 helps ensure that every lawfully cast vote can be counted, and that the will of the voters of every political party will be respected."

Republican lawmakers argued in previous hearings that the bill is unnecessary because it is already a crime to steal ballots.

Another bill, Senate Bill 259, makes it a crime to interfere with a mail ballot on the way to or from a voter or order the seizure of ballots that are in transit to a local elections office.

Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1664, which requires elections officials to notify the attorney general and secretary of state immediately upon learning of any warrants, subpoenas or law enforcement investigations involving election records or voting equipment.

Newsom also signed bills to boost protections under the California Voting Rights Act, including an explicit ban on voter suppression and expanded access to election materials in languages other than English.

The governor also signed legislation to require more transparency from social media influencers who are paid by political campaigns. The measure, Assembly Bill 1130, came in the wake of a controversy in the June primary election when social media influencers took on a more visible role in the campaigns.

Candidates including Democratic billionaire Tom Steyer paid thousands of dollars to influencers who posted videos endorsing Steyer or talking about him in a positive light. These videos did not always disclose that influencers were paid by a candidate's campaign.

title: Trump's surprise 'AI Force' leaves tech industry searching for answers
description:
The tech industry is struggling to make sense of President Donald Trump's surprise announcement that he is creating an artificial intelligence task force and appointing a czar to oversee the administration's approach to the technology.
Trump, in alengthy Truth Social poston Saturday morning, said he was forming the government body and would also soon name an AI czar to lead it. He offered few details, leaving members of the tech world unsure what the task force would do, who would be involved or how it would operate.
Four representatives for the sector, who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, told POLITICO that the industry was not widely informed of Trump's decision prior to the Truth Social post.
"Nobody knows what the idea even is," one of the people said.

The tech industry is struggling to make sense of President Donald Trump's surprise announcement that he is creating an artificial intelligence task force and appointing a czar to oversee the administration's approach to the technology.

Trump, in alengthy Truth Social poston Saturday morning, said he was forming the government body and would also soon name an AI czar to lead it. He offered few details, leaving members of the tech world unsure what the task force would do, who would be involved or how it would operate.

Four representatives for the sector, who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, told POLITICO that the industry was not widely informed of Trump's decision prior to the Truth Social post.

"Nobody knows what the idea even is," one of the people said. Another said that feedback on the idea was not widely solicited within the industry.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Several of those canvassed said they view the move as a response to growing public alarm at the developing technology's potential risks. AI researchers at top AI labs in the past few weeks have issued stark warnings about the technology's power to destroy humanity, while executives including Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis have called for a slowdown so its risks can be adequately addressed.

"I think that he clearly feels pressure to say something, but he's torn because he's just spent the last few days saying that the whole thing is a hoax," Adam Kovacevich, CEO of the progressive tech industry coalition Chamber of Progress, said of Trump and his prior dismissal of AI doomsday scenarios

Since the departure of David Sacks, who stepped down as the Trump administration's previous AI czar earlier this year, the White House has been "making up AI policy as it goes," Kovacevich added. "I think it's clear they've really missed the presence of an organized leader like David Sacks was."

One of the tech industry representatives said they were confused about whether the task force would be charged with formulating more AI regulations or recommending policies that would further stimulate the tech's development.

Taylor Barkley, director of federal government affairs at the industry-aligned Abundance Institute, is eyeing it as a way to solidify a light-touch government approach to the technology he says will foster innovation.

"Any AI Force or AI Czar should have one job: keep the field open so entrepreneurs at every scale can compete, free from onerous regulation," he told POLITICO. "Existing criminal and civil law can handle bad actors. New permission regimes will stifle the very activity America needs most."

Trump's post Saturday showed a clear desire to keep the industry booming: "We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows!"

Trump's comparison of the new AI task force to Space Force led at least one tech industry representative to speculate that the proposal could be led by the Pentagon. "Rather than use civilian agencies to regulate it, use the Pentagon to try and dominate it," they said.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and NVIDIA did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the proposal.

Brendan Bordelon and John Hewitt Jones contributed to this report.

title: Tudhope wins second Ayr Gold Cup on Pellitory
description: Pellitory wins the Ayr Gold Cup for trainer David O'Meara after a lengthy delay following heavy rain - a second victory in the race for jockey Danny Tudhope.
fullText:
Pellitory won the Ayr Gold Cup for trainer David O'Meara after a lengthy delay following heavy rain overnight and on Saturday morning.

There were two inspections of the course, with races pushed back but ultimately cleared to go ahead.

Jockey Danny Tudhope, who became the first Scottish winner of this race in 50 years when he rode Summerghand to victory in 2022, took the glory again as he fended off Tuco Salamanca who finished in second, with joint-favourites Binhareer and Far Above Dream not placing.

Pellitory - owned by Evan Sutherland - is better known over seven furlongs, but that served him well over heavy ground, securing a first win over the shorter distance.

"He's never really been brought back to six furlongs, it was a bold move," Tudhope said.

"To win this race once was unbelievable, to win it twice is amazing. I couldn't be happier."

O'Meara added: "We felt he would [love these conditions]. He stays seven [furlongs] and has run over a mile - that's a huge thing today.

"Today was all about Evan and his horse, I'm delighted for him."

Olid's Man Utd take big step forward after 'intense week'
description: A week ago, the picture at Manchester United looked bleak. Then on Saturday, victory was snatched away from them at Arsenal. But have we seen signs of improvement from Eva Olid's side?
fullText:
A week ago, the picture for Manchester United looked a lot bleaker than it did at the full-time whistle on Saturday.

Regardless of the stoppage-time equaliser they conceded at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, United's performance marked a major sign of progress.

Defeats in their opening two matches, including a 5-0 thrashing by Chelsea, meant the list of questions for new manager Eva Olid seemed endless.

United were disorganised, lacking in identity and were wide open at the back as their new era under Olid began in disappointing fashion.

Those early displays did little to fill supporters with confidence, and Olid faced criticism for her decisions despite being in the job just a matter of weeks.

However, a gutsy defensive display against Arsenal delivered a well-earned 1-1 draw and they were only denied victory by a 95th-minute leveller.

While United's wait for a first Women's Super League win of the season continues, this performance suggested there may not be quite the cause for concern many suspected.

Arsenal earn point with late leveller against Man Utd

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Olid, 41, took over as manager in the summer, joining from Hearts, and promised to implement a new attacking style of play that focused heavily on possession.

However, in their opening two games, United had just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches. In the second of those games, they suffered the five-goal humbling at home by Chelsea.

Few expected them to come away with anything against an Arsenal team who many tipped to win the title before the season kicked off, albeit they have struggled to score goals efficiently.

Olid knew it would be a test but said on Friday she wanted her players to believe in themselves, show confidence, and to go back to the defensive roots they knew and built so well under her predecessor Marc Skinner.

"It has been an intense week because there were a lot of emotions from players and staff. Nobody wants to lose 5-0," said Olid.

"We grew as a team. The first day after losing 5-0 is not easy for anyone. We spoke and said we needed energy this week and a positive mindset.

"The focus was the defensive shape. It's trying to get them more confidence."

Olid ultimately wants her United team to dominate the ball and create more chances in front of goal, but this time they delivered on her plea to be defensively solid.

They looked well organised in an even first half in which United midfielder Simi Awujo stood out, while Andrea Medina tracked back effectively.

They won more duels than Arsenal, put in more tackles and completed more interceptions than their opponents - but still had only 40% of possession.

Former England midfielder Izzy Christiansen told Sky Sports: "Manchester United have done a terrific job defensively. Overall, it's just been solid.

"It looks so much better. The addition of Awujo has added some running power and they look so much freer in the final third."

Arsenal's pressure grew in an edgy second half, but United held on for as long as they could and were unfortunate to concede with seconds left on the clock.

They had led from midway through the half, after Julia Zigiotti seized on a mistake from Georgia Stanway.

Smilla Holmberg's late volley denied United the spoils, but Olid saw foundations she could build on.

"I think the attacking will come," she said. "If you implement a new style of play, you need time.

"That effort, that intensity, can never be missed. We deserved three points for the hard work and the effort.

"Of course, we need to create more chances. That is why I'm here. We need time, but today is the minimum that we have to deliver. I hope we can improve the attacking side."

The biggest question is whether United really can build on this performance.

They were already a difficult team to break down under Skinner but came up short in previous big games against WSL title rivals.

In three Women's FA Cup finals, United won once against Tottenham, falling to higher-placed Chelsea on the other two occasions.

Four years have passed since they won a game at Emirates Stadium against Arsenal, and their heavy defeat by Chelsea last week showed the gap to the elite still remains.

Olid was brought in to transform their style by implementing an attacking philosophy that the club hope will deliver them long-term success.

Patience was already beginning to wane after their demoralising early defeats, so conversations took place and they had to revert back to what they already knew.

The result of that is significant progress from last week, but is it progress for the long term?

"We are a team who need to press high, but at the same time we want to be better with the ball," Olid said on Sky Sports.

"We lose simple passes and we cannot recognise the free player. Those things need to improve. It will come, I'm sure.

"But we need to keep this [defensive structure], then from there, little by little, be an attacking team, create more chances, score more goals.

"I cannot pretend it's happening in four weeks, but I'm sure it will come."

title: Littler seals dramatic final-leg win over Aspinall
description: World champion Luke Littler beats Nathan Aspinall 10-9 to reach the last eight of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
fullText:
World champion Luke Littler beat Nathan Aspinall in a dramatic finale to reach the last eight of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Littler, 19, trailed 9-8 in a best-of-19 contest that had been close throughout and he held throw in the 18th leg to force a decider.

Needing to break Aspinall's throw to win, Littler started the leg with his seventh 180 of the match and checked out 58 for a match-clinching 12-darter.

The two Englishmen had been involved in a World Matchplay classic in July, when Littler threw a nine-darter in the opening leg of an 11-8 victory.

"The pace of the game suits us both, we're good friends and we bring the best out of each other," said Littler, who has a chance to complete a clean sweep of the PDC's premier events in 2026.

"I only played well in the last session [from 6-6 onwards]. In the first two sessions, I didn't feel confident but I managed to get it to 6-6 and I was very good in the third."

The world number one will meet former Premier League champion Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals on Sunday.

Clayton beat Japan's Motomu Sakai 10-8 and is one of two Welshmen in the last eight, with Gerwyn Price also progressing courtesy of a 10-5 win against Canada's Jim Long.

England's James Wade was the other winner in Saturday's evening session, defeating Wessel Nijman of the Netherlands, and will face Price next.

Littler survives scare to progress in Amsterdam

Champion Van Gerwen loses in first round to Gurney

Earlier on Saturday, world number two Luke Humphries lost the deciding leg of his last-16 match against Dirk van Duijvenbode.

Van Duijvenbode's next opponent will be fellow Dutchman Gian van Veen, who was beaten by Littler in January's World Championship final.

England's Ross Smith and Northern Ireland's Josh Rock also won their last-16 ties to complete the quarter-final line-up.

The tournament concludes on Sunday, with the quarter-finals taking place from 12:00 BST and the semi-finals and final being played during the evening session (18:00 BST).

title: Moyes demands more from Everton - but don't mention Europe
description: Fifth in the Premier League table and yet to lose this season, Everton are on the up, but boss David Moyes wants further improvements - and don't mention Europe.
fullText:
Unbeaten after five games and fifth in the Premier League, Everton boss David Moyes is refusing to think of Europe after allowing himself to dream last season.

"We are not using those words this year," said Moyes bluntly after a 1-0 victory at home against Ipswich Town took the Toffees to nine points.

They have two wins and three draws from their first month of the campaign, a healthy start.

But the way 2025-26 ended for Everton was a painful experience for Moyes and the club's fans, and nobody will be getting ahead of themselves this time.

A 3-0 win over Chelsea in March had left Moyes' side eighth, three points off what would have been a Champions League place.

But just as the fans dreamed of a first European experience since 2017-18, the wheels came off with no wins in their final seven games.

Everton finished 13th, four points behind Brighton, who qualified for the Conference League, and five off Sunderland, who joined Bournemouth and Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

So it is no wonder Moyes is refusing to get carried away now.

Asked whether he had challenged his players to earn European qualification this season, Moyes said: "Not [saying] in front of you people [the media], that's for sure, because we're still preparing ourselves and make sure we can do the best we can.

"I enjoyed saying the words last year. If you think of what we had done, been relegation material when we came in January [2025], got out and won the games, 12/13 new players had to come in...

"But the players had done so well, I started to believe that we had a real chance, and it allowed me to be like that."

Everton's strong start, in which they have also won two Carabao Cup games to set up a home last-16 tie against Newcastle in October, had been based on a solid defence.

Moyes' side have kept five clean sheets in seven matches overall and got the three points against Ipswich thanks to an 11th-minute goal from Thierno Barry, his fifth of the season.

What makes Everton's form even more impressive is the fact Barry is the only recognised striker at the club after Beto moved to Fiorentina on transfer deadline day, with key attacking midfielder Iliman Ndiaye joining Manchester City on the same day.

However, Moyes felt his side, one of only five still unbeaten in the Premier League, still have plenty of work to do before he will be happy.

"We've had draws at Tottenham and Bournemouth away from home and we've done pretty well," said Moyes. "Keeping clean sheets is something to be pleased about and try to build on.

"We've statistically been making more chances and we had 21 shots [against Ipswich], which is very good, but only two on target which isn't very good.

"The players get huge credit to get to this point, unbeaten in five games. It's really good, but I'm expecting them to do this.

"If we're thinking 'we're doing a great job because we've gone a few games', no, the manager expects that. I'm actually more disappointed that we aren't scoring more goals.

"I'm rapping them like you wouldn't believe - why are we not getting better crosses into the box, better finishes, shooting from the edge of the box, not scoring more? That's the only thing we're missing from being a half-decent side."

When Moyes returned for a second spell in charge of Everton in January 2025, the Toffees were 16th, one point clear of the relegation zone.

He has had to cope with rising expectations but was quick to point to the club's progress since he came back.

"I heard a lot of things [said] that last year was not so good and I thought 'my goodness, I don't know what the people are talking or writing about because it's absolute baloney'.

"It was fantastic what we did and we came so close to doing something that would have been incredibly special after no money, being on the verge of relegation, moving to a new stadium - and it has never been an easy job for anyone moving to a new stadium - so we came really close."

Assessing Everton's unbeaten status, former England midfielder and BBC pundit Danny Murphy said: "Nothing surprises me with a David Moyes side.

"They're so well organised, so well motivated and always dangerous when their backs are against the wall. There's been a lot of discontent among the fanbase regarding the owners and a transfer policy that left themselves short in forward areas.

"But the rest of the side is so well balanced, they all know their jobs, they know what they're doing and that backline with the keeper behind it is really solid. So, I never thought it was a catastrophe that they didn't get a striker in.

"Because they're so well organised and defensively so good, they're always going to nick results when they're not playing well. I do understand the fans' frustration, but I didn't think for a second they'd be in any danger because they didn't get cover in for their forwards.

"It is a thin squad, but they've still got quality."

Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford told BBC Sport the result felt like a positive way to end this part of the season, with the international break meaning the Toffees are not in league action again until 11 October when they will face Hull City.

"You have to dig in, that's the Everton way," Pickford said. "We are building momentum and we will be focused and ready to go when we come back. It was a great way to finish the week off."

Looking at the contribution of goalscorer Barry, who found the net just eight times last season but now looks a greater threat, Pickford said: "He works hard and the goals will come from working hard. The first year in the Premier League is always tough. He has found his feet and he has started a lot better this year.

"It's always good to finish with a win, especially before a long international break."

title: No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat
description: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.
fullText:
The closer Tottenham went to scoring, the more it seemed likely they would concede.

"Too fragile" was how boss Roberto de Zerbi described his side after the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa.

Comfortable and on top until Johan Manzambi's scrappy opener for the visitors - while Spurs were temporarily down to 10 men as Micky van de Ven had treatment - the home side never recovered.

It only got worse as goals from Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia put the visitors 3-0 up.

De Zerbi's men now go into a three-week international break still waiting for a first Premier League win this season as Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke's late goals - the club's first in the league - were of little consolation.

In the bottom three after spending over £300m in the summer, there appears to be no end in sight to Spurs' struggles.

Tottenham have failed to win any of their past 36 Premier League matches when conceding first, so the writing was on the wall at half-time.

They dominated the opening 20 minutes and Villa keeper Zion Suzuki denied Savio and Archie Gray but, without a goal, Tottenham were always going to be vulnerable at the other end.

And so, in first-half injury time, a Villa goal was almost inevitable.

Andy Robertson tried to stop a corner but only gifted the ball to John McGinn and, after Boubacar Kamara's effort, Manzambi prodded in from close range. It added the insult to Van de Ven's injury, a blow to the face that kept him off the pitch.

Some Tottenham fans missed the goal as they headed for their half-time refreshments, but several thousand did not bother to stay until the end.

They streamed out of the stands after Buendia's brilliant 25-yard bullet found the top corner in the 79th minute, and that meant those fans missed Gallagher and Van Hecke's late efforts.

De Zerbi said: "My focus is why we concede the first goal with 10 players, we can stay stronger, communicate more and more, defend in a compact way.

"I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur as a centre-back in that minute and Mateus Fernandes as a midfielder. If we have a red card we can play 70 minutes with 10 players.

"In the second half we scored the goal with [Mohammed] Kudus, offside, I don't know if some players lost energy but we conceded an unacceptable goal. We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season.

"We had many meetings [about it] and we have to explain another game like Newcastle where we played the first half well and then we lose. It's my responsibility.

"I take my responsibility, but in that moment of the game we have to defend, we have to defend compact, the leaders have to be leaders.

"I am very sad and frustrated with the performance. We cannot lose this game in this way. The second goal we conceded was incredible."

"Sacked in the morning" chanted the Villa fans to De Zerbi who, at times, looked out of ideas once his side fell 2-0 behind.

It was Tottenham's worst start to a top-flight season since 2008-09, when they also had two points after five games.

Juande Ramos was dismissed as manager after three more defeats before Harry Redknapp lifted them up to eighth. Spurs have also now gone five league games without a win at the start of a season for the first time since 1986.

Former Brighton striker Glenn Murray, however, says De Zerbi needs time.

"He is trying to build something, it will take time," he told BBC's Final Score. "Taking the emotion out of it, looking at the stats, they have had more shots in three of the past four games, more possession and more touches in the opposition box.

"They are positives, be patient, the metrics are there to say he will turn it around. They need to be patient with Roberto de Zerbi, with all the signings, it takes time to gel and get to know each other."

A decisive moment came when Kudus thought he had levelled on the hour, but Robertson was ruled just offside having delivered the cross. Seven minutes later Jackson scored from Suzuki's long launch downfield and it was game over.

Villa's rebuild, the club committing to spending more than £250m, was out of necessity because of their own high-profile exits.

There was an expectation change was forthcoming and the Europa League winners were always going to go through a period of transition.

But a first league victory was vital for them too after three defeats in their opening four games.

While Villa look in better shape as new players settle, Spurs have thrown money at their problems after two relegation battles, but they are no closer to solving them. They ended Saturday sitting 19th in the table.

Sandro Tonali, the £100m midfielder from Newcastle, was overshadowed by Villa's tenacious skipper McGinn - a £2.75m buy from Hibs eight years ago.

Brazil winger Savio was denied three times by the impressive Suzuki but faded, while Omar Marmoush was signed to bring goals, but provided nothing.

De Zerbi said: "I didn't speak with the players [afterwards], I didn't want to say anything. The players who go to the national team, they have to play and work.

"The others, [James] Maddison, Gallagher, [Dominic] Solanke, Tosin [Adarabioyo], [Marcos] Senesi, Savio have to work more because their physical condition, I didn't like in this game."

Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win

Manzambi catches eye as Villa beat Spurs - player ratings

Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole questioned Tottenham's transfer business after their spend of about £302m.

After Tonali, £85m went on bringing in Mateus Fernandes from West Ham. The Portuguese midfielder was subbed at half-time and De Zerbi said he "didn't like" Fernandes' performance, while £75m was spent on Savio from Manchester City.

Marmoush will cost £60m once his loan becomes permanent, but Spurs need their big-money buys to prove their worth and perform sooner rather than later.

"Spurs are dominant, chances, and you felt the tension growing - all of a sudden Spurs were just wanting to get to half-time. Once you defend with anxiety, things happen," Cole told TNT.

"When these things go against you, they go against you. Van de Ven going off was a factor, they didn't deal with it well. When you are anxious you make rash decisions.

"Villa defended well but didn't deserve to go in a goal up, and then this place deflated.

"They are not picking up points, a club flirting with relegation two years in a row, I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle."

De Zerbi, though, defended Tottenham's summer window spending despite their current malaise.

"I am happy with the squad, but the market was long, the situation changed many times," he said.

"There was also financial fair play and we have to respect that. We didn't sell the players we thought there was a possibility to sell.

"The club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players. If we didn't make any different decisions it was because we couldn't."

title: Gvardiol signals return to best at left-back for Man City
description: Josko Gvardiol's season last time out was disrupted by a serious injury but the defender now appears to be returning towards his best by helping Manchester City to an impressive start to the new campaign.
fullText:
Josko Gvardiol appears to be returning towards his best by helping Manchester City to an impressive start to the new campaign after his previous season was disrupted by a serious injury.

Following a 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal in August, City have recovered to win six straight games in all competitions and the Croatian has been part of a defence that has conceded just twice in their opening four Premier League games.

With new captain Ruben Dias and England international Marc Guehi beginning to form a solid partnership in central defence, Gvardiol has been deployed at left-back and making the position his own.

Enzo Maresca's side host Sunderland on Sunday (14:00 BST) in a game the manager has described as being their "toughest" so far this season "because of how good they are".

Victory against the Black Cats will maintain City's winning streak and send Gvardiol off on international duty with Croatia - who face England and Spain in the Uefa Nations League - in high spirits following World Cup disappointment in the summer as his country went out at the last-32 stage.

'Just the beginning' - Samba, 17, steals Man City show

With numerous quality options available in central defence, Maresca needed to find a place in the starting line-up for Gvardiol.

The former RB Leipzig player missed five months last season after a broken leg, allowing Nico O'Reilly to continue featuring in an unfamiliar place at left-back.

The Englishman, though, has had to be content with a place on the bench so far this term, although the 21-year-old has been told by Maresca he will be given more opportunities in his favoured midfield position.

Sources close to Gvardiol have described him as being like a "soldier", accepting whichever position he is assigned to and performing to the best of his ability for the benefit of the team.

He is thought to be "satisfied" by Maresca's decision and feels overall he has gained more tactical knowledge of the game since moving to England.

Gvardiol had told reporters in the summer it would take "at least a year before everything heals inside", but is understood to be pain free now and has returned to 100% match fitness.

He has played at both centre-back and left-back after arriving at City in 2023 for a £77m fee paid to Leipzig, making him the second most expensive defender of all time behind Harry Maguire.

Sources say Gvardiol feels left-back is a more physically demanding role than centre-half, but one he enjoys as it allows him the freedom to roam forward into goalscoring positions where he has flourished with his marauding runs.

The 24-year-old scored an injury-time winner in the season-opener against Bournemouth, while also providing two assists, including Erling Haaland's controversial strike that sealed a derby success at Manchester United.

Gvardiol's attacking capabilities do not take away from his defensive prowess.

At Old Trafford last Sunday, he helped City to an unlikely victory with a defiant clean sheet after being reduced to 10 men following Phil Foden's 23rd-minute red card.

Gvardiol kept Bryan Mbeumo in check for large parts of the contest, winning nine of his 11 duels - no player on the pitch managed more - and contested four tackles, a match-high of any City player.

In all, he has won the seventh most duels of any Premier League player this term, while he also ranks in the top 10 for most tackles made by anyone in the top flight.

That has meant Algeria international Rayan Ait-Nouri, signed at left-back last summer from Wolves, can't get a look-in in his natural position and has instead been used further up the pitch by Maresca.

Gvardiol had a tricky game at Porto in the Champions League tie, getting booked in the first half and then substituted early in the second, but it appeared to be an off-day rather than something more worrying.

During the summer he committed his long-term future to City by signing a new five-year deal, despite interest from Bayern Munich and Barcelona.

The defender said he was "happy" to extend his stay at Etihad Stadium and under Maresca "everyone has to fight for their position, no-one is secure".

Gvardiol, though, will be assured of his place if he continues his bright start.

title: Brown maintains perfect record with brutal Hedges stoppage
description: Pat Brown continues his perfect start to life as a professional with a seventh successive stoppage to hand John Hedges his first defeat in front of a raucous Manchester crowd.
fullText:
Pat Brown displayed destructive power to stop John Hedges in the sixth round and claim the British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles in Manchester.

Brown started slowly in front of a home crowd at Co-op Live Arena but was rewarded when he got behind his jab.

A thudding left hook to the body dropped Hedges in round six and he landed the same shot moments later to wrap up victory.

An emotional Brown, 26, spoke of how "special" it was to win the British title in his hometown.

"I don't care about all of the belts, it's for my family and my people," Brown said on DAZN.

"I've had a childhood with them all but I had to go off-grid to train and they've always stayed behind me.

"And for Ross - my cousin, who I love dearly - I said to him I would go all the way and I will."

Brown extends his perfect professional record to seven victories, with each of those coming via knockout, while Hedges lost for the first time in his 13-fight pro career.

Dreams of Old Trafford - Brown targets British title and famous nights

This fight was originally set to take place in Altrincham, but Matchroom made the switch to East Manchester's Co-op Live because of ticket demands.

And the 5,000-strong crowd made themselves heard when Brown entered the ring first, followed by a chorus of boos for Essex fighter Hedges.

Chants of 'Oh Patrick the Bomber' and 'Sale' rang around the arena as Hedges took the upper hand in the opening rounds with his awkward style.

Brown looked for ways to set up his heavy power-punches, but Hedges' sharp footwork and holding at the right time nullified the threat.

The pendulum started to swing in Brown's favour in the fifth when he began using his jab to set up combinations, with a right uppercut punctuating the round.

Hedges paid tribute to Manchester icon Ricky Hatton at the weigh-in after the first anniversary of his death passed on 14 September.

And it was a Hatton-like rippling left hook to the body from Brown that sent Hedges crashing to his knees.

Hedges beat the count but was sent tumbling back down to the canvas with another blow to the midsection - this time he was unable to pull himself back to his feet.

Family man Brown, who made his ringwalk with his father, had previously said "putting belts on his dad's shoulders" was all that mattered.

After Moses Itauma and Conor Benn both experienced losses when skipping the British title route and heading straight for world title glory, Brown said he wants to go on the "journey".

Chris Billam-Smith and Lawrence Okolie are two examples of those who have recently held the British cruiserweight title and gone on to win world honours.

Brown now holds the British and Commonwealth titles, and could look to European title-holder Viddal Riley next.

Riley, 29, last fought in April when he secured a unanimous points decision win over former world title challenger Mateusz Masternak.

When speaking to BBC Sport on Wednesday, the view of Old Trafford - the home of his beloved Manchester United - sat in the background.

Not since 1993, when Chris Eubank and Nigel Benn's unification bout ended in a draw, has the stadium hosted a boxing match.

Brown said one day headlining at Old Trafford would mean more to him than belts.

Most importantly, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn sees the vision: "Pat Brown, world championship, Old Trafford. I see it."

Brown still has a long way to go if he's to be mentioned in the same breath as former world champion Hatton, but he's used his latest opportunity to make his mark.

title: Carrick has faith in VAR despite derby error
description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick still has faith in VAR despite the derby blunder that cost his side in their home defeat by Manchester City
fullText:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he still has faith in the video assistant referee - but added that the apology for the error that led to their defeat in the Manchester derby does not mean much.

Referee's body Pro Ref issued a formal apology to United within three hours of the end of Manchester City's 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

Neither VAR Matt Donohue nor his assistant Blake Antrobus have been selected for games this weekend after failing to spot City midfielder Enzo Fernandez clearly in an offside position and interfering with play before Erling Haaland's matchwinner for City.

Carrick was livid after the game, saying it was a "worrying" interpretation of the rules.

And before his side's Premier League trip to Fulham on Sunday, the United boss was asked if he still had faith in VAR.

"One-off things can happen," he said.

"At the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don't think I need to go over that. But yes, I've got faith in it. It's the system we work towards and that we use."

Referee's chief Howard Webb has been heavily criticised over general officiating standards in the game.

Analysing the incident on 'Match Officials Mic'd Up', Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the outcome, stating the officials had been too focused on a potential offside against Haaland and had failed to assess Fernandez's position.

Webb has spoken to United about the situation in an effort to be more accountable.

"The apology doesn't mean an awful lot," said Carrick.

"I can appreciate and respect them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong - it does happen. We just have to deal with it.

"Maybe we get one or two decisions on the law of averages or whatever but that one had a huge impact on the game and that's why it was particularly tough."

Carrick has backed central defender Leny Yoro despite his disappointing performance in the 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton on Wednesday.

Yoro was linked with Real Madrid, Paris St-Germain and Liverpool when he joined United from Lille as an 18-year-old in July 2024.

The £52.2m fee underlined the faith United's recruitment department had in Yoro's potential.

So far though, it has been unfulfilled.

The 20-year-old has featured in 55 Premier League games, but 25 of those have been as a substitute. His only starts this term have been against Sabah FK in the Champions League and Brighton, when his positioning was called into question as the visitors became the first side to win at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals for over 50 years.

"I've got no worries for Leny," said Carrick. "He's got a fantastic future ahead of him.

"There's no cut off point. Some players find when they're 18 that they are at a level where they can really perform. Sometimes it's 22, 23, 24 when you see players start developing.

"What we've got to be careful of, and I certainly won't do, is making knee-jerk decisions on certain players just because of one game or one half or one moment in a game. We've got a lot of belief in Leny."

title: Hear'Say, 'Snake' & Tony Blair: A Coventry win 25 years in the making
description: Coventry City's win over Nottingham Forest - thanks to Jay Dasilva's goal - was a victory which was over 25 years in the making following some dark days for the Sky Blues.
fullText:
Hear'Say were top of the pops, a mobile phone game called 'Snake' was all the rage and Tony Blair was Prime Minister.

Wind the clock back to April 2001 and things looked rather different.

It was also the last time Coventry City tasted victory in English football's top flight.

That came courtesy of a 1-0 win over Sunderland - John Hartson heading in the winner for Gordon Strachan's side in front of 20,946 fans at Highfield Road.

Much has happened in the life of Coventry since that moment 9,287 days ago. A rollercoaster journey might be understating it.

They were relegated at the end of the 2000-01 campaign and would spend the next 11 seasons in the second tier before dropping down to League One in 2012.

Then followed a particularly dark and turbulent period in the club's history featuring points deductions and a stint in administration.

Having left Highfield Road in 2005 they became embroiled in a bitter dispute over the Ricoh Arena in 2013 and its rent.

The nadir, arguably, was when they were forced to play matches away from Coventry, at Northampton Town, before later plummeting down to the fourth tier for the first time in 59 years in 2017.

Doubtless there were those packed into the Bridgford Stand at the City Ground on Saturday who were present during those years of Sky Blue hell.

So the explosion of emotion at the full-time whistle - after Jay Dasilva's goal settled matters - felt like Sky Blue heaven.

"It's been a tough opening for us, so those first Premier League points feel great," Coventry boss Frank Lampard told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I thought the players were brilliant. The fight, work ethic and togetherness but also the tactical side of it. They dug and fought for each other which is what you need to win a Premier League game."

Coventry had been stranded on 99 Premier League wins for over a quarter of a century before this victory ticked them over to three figures at long last.

Lampard hopes this victory could be a key staging post in a campaign where avoiding relegation will be the main aim.

"It's really important for some of the players," he told BBC Match of the Day.

"For many of them it is their debut in the Premier League, they haven't been here before and they need to feel like they belong and play like that."

Lampard acknowledged his players must have thick skins to come through the slog of a Premier League season.

The fact this victory came off the back of a 5-0 drubbing at home to Brighton makes it all the more rewarding for the Coventry boss.

"There are lots of things we can learn and sometimes this year we may take those hits, it's a reality for teams that get to the Premier League," added Lampard.

"It's important we overcome them in terms of how we take it on board and stay together.

"It is easy to point in different directions when you lose but the group's really strong, really together, there'll have a good feeling from this one. But we'll keep our feet on the ground because it is one win, but it was needed for us."

title: Celtic win 'changes game' - but can they reverse Rangers' derby dominance?
description: Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side.
fullText:
Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side.

Rangers triumphed 3-0 at home in last Sunday's Old Firm League Cup quarter-final before Celtic opened their Europa League campaign with a 3-1 defeat at home by Ferencvaros on Thursday.

However, Celtic's early season domestic form has them going into Sunday's match in the east end of Glasgow - which like last week will have no visiting supporters in attendance - with a five-point advantage over their Ibrox rivals.

"If Celtic win and they're eight points clear, it changes the game," Brown said on BBC Scotland's YouTube channel.

"Can [Rangers] go to Celtic Park and do they exact same thing as last week?

"Celtic now have had a week to understand how that game went. They are going to have to make sure that they match that energy but also match that willingness to go and win the match."

Celtic seek spark as Rangers aim for further derby joy

Scottish Premiership: Celtic v Rangers

20/9/26 from 11:00 BST (radio), 19:15 (TV)

Brown was impressed by Rangers manager Derek McInnes' change of approach in the season's first derby, change to a 3-5-2 shape and going man for man with Celtic's front three.

"They went after Celtic from the get go," Brown said. "They looked like they wanted the win more. For him to change his tactics, nobody expected him to do that. That is a very, very good manager to pick that out."

Brown also pondered Celtic's tactical plan.

"Martin O'Neill when he was manager [from 2000-05], loved a 3-5-2 and it was fantastic to watch," said the former Scotland captain.

"He had two big guys up front. That was an unbelievable team. He's not got those players that probably can be suited to a 3-5-2."

With Yang Hyun-jun still on Asian Games duty with South Korea, Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest have both been used on Celtic's left flank.

But Brown believes the club's problems go beyond that.

"Rangers got in their face, they blocked Callum McGregor off and as soon as you block Callum McGregor off and you man-mark Cal, it's hard for anyone else to go and dictate.

"That's when you need a [Benjamin] Nygren to drop under, a [Mika] Baur to go and drop under and them do their job as well. You can't always keep looking at Cal to do everything."

And Brown believes who starts best could be crucial.

"Rangers were up for the fight," he added on Sportsound. "The first 15 minutes, it should be a battle. If you can go and win that battle, you can get the ball down.

"Celtic started very, very slow last week. They need to go back to basics, make sure they've got the fight, make sure they've got the hunger because they've got the talent - I know they've got the talent.

"You cannot have just one of those days against your biggest rivals, ever."
